# Programme Run Section — Follow-Up Work

## Context

The Programme → Run section landed in its current shape across PR-0a → PR-B (May 2026). It's structurally sound: inline mode picker (PR-B), composing handler that sequences `updateProfile` + `refreshRunSchedule` atomically, per-mode operational heroes (PR-4), DayActionSheet for per-day actions (PR-1), `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` repo config (May 17).

What's still incomplete or incorrect:

- **Post-race state is paper.** `race_no_show` and `race_completed_unlinked` are defined in `ScheduledRunStatus` but never written by any code path. The UI has dead branches for them. `linkedRunId` is similarly defined but never written.
- **No recovery phase.** After a user completes a race plan, the UI shows a dead-end "Race day has passed" muted banner. The "Switch to structured running" button on the post-race card today mislabels what it does.
- **No automatic week rollover.** A run-only user (no lifts) never sees a rotation of their `programState.runDays`. The same Mon/Wed/Sat entries persist until they manually edit their schedule. Race-prep users' `currentWeek` never ticks up automatically.
- **Per-day template overrides die on schedule refresh.** Setting Monday=tempo via the per-row `<select>` writes `userOverride: "tempo_20"`. Any subsequent `refreshRunSchedule` (triggered by a schedule edit, target change, or — once PR-D ships — the auto-transition) regenerates `runDays[]` from scratch and silently drops the override.
- **"This week" label in the freeform hero is wrong.** Uses `weeklyData[weeklyData.length - 1]` (most recent week with any runs), which can be a past calendar week when a user hasn't run this week. Labels last week's data as "This week."
- **"Next planned run" card lacks temporal anchor.** Today's `Next · {dayLabel}` doesn't distinguish today / tomorrow / past-planned. The user has to compute proximity.
- **Mode-change pending state is silent.** During the 1-2 second `updateProfile` + `refreshRunSchedule` window, only the non-active chips dim — no positive "we're working on this" signal.

This document is the plan to close all of these, designed end-to-end in a /grill-me session (22 decisions, May 17 2026).

---

## Revision — soft-link reframe (May 17 2026, second /grill-me)

After PR-F, PR-D, PR-E, PR-C, PR-G shipped, a follow-up grill on race-day reconciliation reached a different conclusion than the original plan. The reframe:

**What we built:** persisted `linkedRunId` linkage between saved runs and `runDay` slots, plus a state-machine status (`completed_exact`, `race_no_show`, etc.) tracking whether the linkage exists.

**What the reference apps do** (see `CONTEXT.md` for the full audit): Strava, Nike Run Club, Garmin Connect, and TrainingPeaks all do linkage **invisibly** — date-based at render time, or start-time selection. None surface "link / unlink" as a user concept.

**The revision:** drop user-facing linkage entirely. Compute completion at render time via "saved run with matching date + template exists." This means:

- **DROP:** the planned Q1 "Was this your scheduled race?" RunSummary prompt — out of pattern with reference apps.
- **DROP:** the planned Q2 late-reconciliation UI (post-race card "Link a past run" button, History overflow) — same reason.
- **MODIFY:** the planned Q3 enum collapse — go further. Remove `completed_exact / completed_modified / completed_late` entirely. runDay statuses become `planned | skipped | race_no_show | expired`. Completion is derived, never stored.
- **KEEP:** Q4 "What's next?" card after recovery clears. Independent of linkage.
- **KEEP:** Q5 mid-recovery mode-change banner. Independent.
- **KEEP:** Q6 auto-rollover archive + Welcome-back sheet. Modify to use `expired` status from the simplified enum.
- **NEW:** rip `linkedRunId` writes out of `completeRunDay`. The function becomes `markRunDayDone(idOrDayIndex)` that flips status from `planned` to a non-existent-anymore terminal — replaced by the soft-link computation. Actually: even `markRunDayDone` may not be needed if completion is purely derived. To investigate during implementation.

**Race-day recovery trigger (new mechanism):** today, PR-D's `completeRunDay` enters recovery when the race-day runDay completes. Under soft-link, recovery enters when an effect detects: `profile.runMode === "race_prep"` AND `today >= raceGoal.targetDate` AND `a saved run exists on raceGoal.targetDate with matching distance`. Strava-synced races trigger recovery on next app open after sync.

**Race-no-show trigger:** PR-D's auto-transition stays. The 3-day-grace + no-saved-run check still fires on app open. Independent of linkage.

This is captured as **PR-J — soft-link reframe**, to be sequenced after the current 5 PRs settle and before any new linkage-related work. See `CONTEXT.md` "Linking a saved run to a planned training-plan slot" for the full reference-app audit.

## PR-F — Run-section polish

Small follow-ups, independent of any state-machine or rollover work. Shippable first.

### Scope

1. **Fix "This week" labelling bug** in the freeform hero. Replace:

   ```ts
   const thisWeek = weeklyData[weeklyData.length - 1] ?? null;
   ```

   with:

   ```ts
   const thisWeekKey = localWeekKey(new Date());
   const thisWeek = weeklyData.find((w) => w.week === thisWeekKey) ?? null;
   ```

   When no bucket exists for the current calendar week, hide the "This week" line.

2. **Next-planned-run label with today/tomorrow/Pending detection.** Replace the current:

   ```tsx
   <p>Next · {DAY_LABELS[nextStartable.dayIndex]}</p>
   ```

   with a derived label:
   - `nextStartable.date === todayKey` → "Today"
   - `nextStartable.date === tomorrowKey` → "Tomorrow"
   - `nextStartable.date < todayKey` → "Pending" (past-planned, still startable but the date has passed)
   - else → `DAY_LABELS[dayIndex]`

3. **Preserve per-day `userOverride` across `refreshRunSchedule`.** In `useProgram.ts:refreshRunSchedule`, snapshot the existing overrides before regenerating and re-apply after. Pattern:

   ```ts
   const overrideSnapshot: Record<number, string> = {};
   for (const rd of programState.runDays ?? []) {
     if (rd.userOverride && (rd.type === "run" || rd.type === "both")) {
       overrideSnapshot[rd.dayIndex] = rd.userOverride;
     }
   }
   // ... generator runs ...
   runDays = runDays.map((rd) => {
     const preserved = overrideSnapshot[rd.dayIndex];
     return preserved
       ? { ...rd, userOverride: preserved, templateId: preserved }
       : rd;
   });
   ```

   Drops orphan overrides (where the day became rest); preserves where the day still has a run/both slot.

4. **Pending status line during mode changes.** Reuse the existing `modeError` slot in `ProgrammeRunSection.tsx`:
   ```tsx
   {
     modeChangePending ? (
       <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Updating your plan…</p>
     ) : modeError ? (
       <p className="text-xs" style={{ color: THEME.running }} role="alert">
         {modeError}
       </p>
     ) : null;
   }
   ```

### Tests

- Pin "this week" filter via `weekKey === currentWeekKey` exact-match.
- Pin override-preservation round-trip in `useProgramWriters.test.ts`: pre-populate `runDays` with a `userOverride`, fire `refreshRunSchedule`, assert the written runDay still carries it.
- Snapshot the next-run label derivation across todayKey / tomorrowKey / past-date / future-week cases.

## PR-D — Race state-machine writers

The structural foundation. Closes the "paper states" gap that PR-0a → PR-0b-iii left behind.

### Scope

1. **Auto-transition effect in `useProgram` load path.** When `programState` resolves, walk `runDays[]` for an entry matching `date === programState.runPlan.raceGoal.targetDate`. If found and `status === "planned"` and `(today - date) >= 3 days` → write `status: "race_no_show"` via `saveProgram`. Idempotent (subsequent runs find non-planned status and skip).

2. **Make `race_no_show` recoverable.** In `programTypes.ts:LEGAL_TRANSITIONS`:

   ```diff
   - race_no_show: [],
   + race_no_show: ["completed_exact", "completed_modified", "completed_late"],
   ```

   In `scheduledRunStatus.ts:TERMINAL_STATUSES`:

   ```diff
   - "race_no_show",
   ```

   `race_no_show` becomes a "soft terminal" status — recoverable via the existing reconciliation flow.

3. **Extend `completeRunDay` to accept `savedRunId`.** Signature becomes:

   ```ts
   completeRunDay(idOrDayIndex: string | number, savedRunId?: string)
   ```

   When `savedRunId` present, write `linkedRunId: savedRunId` alongside the status transition. Callers:
   - `RunSummary.tsx` post-save (line ~681) — has savedRunId, plumb it through
   - `RunSummary.tsx` reconciliation "Mark scheduled run complete" (line ~865) — same
   - `DayActionSheet.tsx` "Mark complete (manual)" — no savedRunId, omit the second arg

4. **Recovery-phase entry coupled to completion.** Inside `completeRunDay`, when the transition is `planned → completed_*` AND the target runDay is the race day (i.e. `date === raceGoal.targetDate`) AND the user's mode is `race_prep`, also write:

   ```ts
   runPlan.phase: "recovery"
   runPlan.recoveryEndDate: <distance-scaled>
   ```

   See PR-E for the duration table.

5. **Drop `race_completed_unlinked`.** Remove from `ScheduledRunStatus` enum, `LEGAL_TRANSITIONS`, `scheduledRunStatus.ts` helpers (`isScheduledRunReconciliation` returns `false` always — or delete the helper). Clean dead branches in:
   - `src/components/program/ProgrammeRunSection.tsx`
   - `src/components/program/DayActionSheet.tsx`
   - `src/components/home/DayPeekCard.tsx`
   - `src/lib/trainingResolver.ts` (the `isReconciliation` field in `ResolvedRun`)

6. **Keep `linkedRunId` on the type.** Reserve for future navigation hook (e.g. "tap a completed race in History → jump to RunSummary view"). No consumer yet.

### Tests

- Auto-transition: pre-populate `programState` with a race-day runDay where `date` is 4 days ago and `status: "planned"`. Render hook. Assert `setDoc` was called with that runDay's status updated to `race_no_show`.
- Recoverability: starting from a `race_no_show` runDay, call `completeRunDay(id, savedRunId)`. Assert the transition succeeds and `linkedRunId` is set.
- Idempotency: run the load effect twice. Assert the second pass writes nothing.
- Coupling: when `completeRunDay` transitions a race-day runDay, assert `runPlan.phase === "recovery"` and `recoveryEndDate` is set.

## PR-E — Recovery phase

Builds on PR-D's writers. Adds the actual phase semantics.

### Scope

1. **Phase storage.** Add to `RunPlan` type in `programTypes.ts`:

   ```ts
   interface RunPlan {
     mode: "structured" | "race_prep";
     raceGoal?: { distance: RaceDistance; targetDate: string };
     totalWeeks?: number;
     currentWeek?: number;
     compressed?: boolean;
     phase?: "recovery"; // NEW
     recoveryEndDate?: string; // NEW — "YYYY-MM-DD"
   }
   ```

2. **Duration table.** Helper in `runScheduler.ts`:

   ```ts
   export function recoveryWeeksForDistance(distance: RaceDistance): number {
     switch (distance) {
       case "5k":
         return 1;
       case "10k":
         return 2;
       case "half":
         return 3;
       case "marathon":
         return 4;
     }
   }
   ```

3. **Recovery template generator.** Add a branch in `refreshRunSchedule` (or a new `scheduleRecoveryWeekV2`):

   ```ts
   if (runPlan.phase === "recovery") {
     // emit all easy_30 entries on the same weekly slots as the user's
     // weekSchedule, frequency unchanged
   }
   ```

   `runMode` stays `race_prep` during recovery (don't flip to structured). The phase distinguishes "in recovery" from "out of recovery" while preserving the user's original mode for re-entry semantics.

4. **Recovery exit logic in the load effect.** When `today >= recoveryEndDate`, the next render shows the "Recovery ended — what's next?" card variant (PR-C). One-week grace beyond `recoveryEndDate` before silent auto-promotion: at `today >= recoveryEndDate + 7 days`, clear `phase` and `recoveryEndDate`, leaving `runMode` as the user's pre-race value (which is still `race_prep` — but if the user wants to leave race_prep they pick a different mode via the chip row).

### Tests

- Phase entry: complete a 10K race runDay → assert `phase === "recovery"` and `recoveryEndDate === raceGoal.targetDate + 14 days`.
- Template emission: with `phase === "recovery"` and a 4-run-day weekSchedule, assert generated runDays all have `templateId === "easy_30"`.
- Phase exit: setting `today` past `recoveryEndDate` triggers the card variant change. At `+7d`, auto-promote (phase cleared).
- Distance scaling: assert 5K=7d, 10K=14d, half=21d, marathon=28d.

## PR-C — Post-race card UX

UI wrap. Depends on PR-D + PR-E writers.

### Scope

Replace the current "Race day has passed" muted banner (`ProgrammeRunSection.tsx:626-642`) with a state-driven card. Four variants:

**Variant 1: Completed → In recovery**
Trigger: race-day runDay status is `completed_*` AND `runPlan.phase === "recovery"`.

```
✓  10K — Saturday 14 Sep
   Race complete. Recovering for the next 2 weeks.
   Templates this week are all easy.

   [ Skip recovery early →  ]              (small link)
   [ View race-day run →    ]              (small link, only if linkedRunId)
```

**Variant 2: Mid-recovery**
Trigger: `runPlan.phase === "recovery"` AND today between race date + 1 and `recoveryEndDate`.

```
   Recovering — 12 days left.
   Easy runs this week.

   [ Skip recovery early →  ]              (small link)
```

**Variant 3: Recovery ended → choose next**
Trigger: `runPlan.phase === "recovery"` AND `today >= recoveryEndDate` AND `today < recoveryEndDate + 7 days`.

```
   Recovery complete.
   What's next?

   [ Set next race                ]
   [ Switch to structured running ]
```

**Variant 4: No-show**
Trigger: race-day runDay status is `race_no_show`.

```
?  10K — Saturday 14 Sep
   We marked this as no-show after three days with no log.
   Log it now if you actually ran.

   [ Log race now                  ]   ← primary, coral
   [ Set next race                 ]
   [ Switch to structured running  ]
```

### Behaviour

- All "Set next race" buttons open the existing inline race-goal form (already in `ProgrammeRunSection.tsx`).
- "Switch to structured running" calls existing `handleModeChange("structured")`.
- "Log race now" navigates to `/run?scheduledRunId=<race-runDay.id>` — uses the existing URL-pinning flow, which PR-D's extended `completeRunDay` will then write `linkedRunId` on completion.
- "View race-day run" — needs a `linkedRunId` value to navigate; route is `/run/{linkedRunId}` per the existing run detail pattern.
- "Skip recovery early" sets `runPlan.phase` undefined, clears `recoveryEndDate`, triggers a `refreshRunSchedule` to regenerate normal structured templates.
- In-card explanation copy directly under the headline — no separate toast.

### Tests

- Each variant renders the right set of buttons given the corresponding state.
- "Log race now" link includes `?scheduledRunId=<id>`.
- "Skip recovery early" clears `phase` and `recoveryEndDate` in the next setDoc call.
- The auto-transition wrote `phase: "recovery"` IS reflected in Variant 1 immediately on next render.

## PR-G — Auto week rollover

Independent of post-race work. Closes the "structured / race-prep runDays never rotate" gap.

### Scope

1. **Load-effect detection.** In `useProgram`'s load path, after `programState` resolves:

   ```ts
   const detectStaleWeek = (state: ProgramState): boolean => {
     const currentWeekKey = localWeekKey();
     const lastKnownWeekKey =
       state.runDays?.[0]?.weekKey ?? state.weekHistory?.[0]?.weekKey;
     return !!lastKnownWeekKey && lastKnownWeekKey < currentWeekKey;
   };

   let rolling = programState;
   let iterations = 0;
   while (detectStaleWeek(rolling) && iterations < 12) {
     rolling = advanceWeek(rolling);
     iterations++;
   }
   if (iterations > 0) {
     await saveProgram(rolling);
     toast.success(
       `Week advanced — ${iterations} week${iterations > 1 ? "s" : ""}`
     );
   }
   ```

   12-iteration cap prevents runaway in pathological cases (user opens app after 3+ months).

2. **Keep the Lift-tab "Advance to Next Week" button** as the "advance early" escape hatch. User who finished all this week's lifts on Wednesday can still tap it to roll forward immediately.

3. **Race progress strip auto-advancement.** With B-loop rolling weekly, `currentWeek` ticks up automatically. The race progress strip ("Week 3 / 8 · Build") stays current without any manual action. Once `currentWeek >= totalWeeks`, the race-day check (PR-D) fires and the post-race card takes over.

### Tests

- Stale-week detection: programState with `runDays[0].weekKey` set to 2 weeks ago. Render hook. Assert `advanceWeek` ran twice and `saveProgram` wrote the result.
- Iteration cap: programState with `weekKey` 14 weeks ago. Assert iterations capped at 12.
- No-op when current: `weekKey === localWeekKey()`. Assert no setDoc, no toast.
- Manual button still works: tap "Advance to Next Week" on the Lift tab → fires `advanceToNextWeek()` directly, bypasses the calendar gate.

### Trade-off honestly noted

A planned-but-never-done Saturday run gets archived in `weekHistory` as `status: "planned"` on the Monday rollover. That's intentional — honest record of "we didn't do this." If the user later logs the run with the Saturday date, the saved run is independent of the archived runDay; the runDay status remains `planned` in history. Acceptable for v1; could be improved by writing `status: "skipped"` (auto) on rollover for non-race past-planned runs, but that's an opinionated take we're deferring.

## PR-L — Server-side reconciliation (Apple Watch precondition)

Hard prerequisite for the near-term Apple Watch sequence. WatchOS apps can't run our React/TS reconciliation logic — they hit endpoints — so when Watch lands, state must be server-authoritative or the two clients will drift.

Ports the three pieces of shipped client-side reconciliation (PR-D, PR-E, PR-J) into Cloud Functions. Removes the `useEffect`-driven write path from `useProgram`; the hook becomes a pure Firestore reader + UI dispatcher.

### Scope

1. **Race no-show trigger** — new scheduled Cloud Function (daily, ~04:00 UTC). Iterates users where `programState.raceDate` is within the last 3 days and no run matching `raceTarget` distance was logged within ±2 days. Writes the no-show transition. Pattern matches existing `weeklyPerformanceRollup` user iteration.

2. **Recovery entry trigger** — extend existing `onRunCreated` Firestore trigger. When a saved run's distance matches the user's `programState.raceTarget` (within tolerance) and the run date is within ±2 days of `raceDate`, write `programState.recovery = { startDate, endDate }` using `recoveryWeeksForDistance` from PR-E.

3. **Recovery exit trigger** — fold into the same daily scheduled function as #1. When `recovery.endDate < now`, clear the recovery block.

4. **Fell-behind detection** — new scheduled Cloud Function (weekly, Mondays ~05:00 UTC, after performance rollup). Per-user evaluation of prior week's `weekHistory` entry: if `<50%` of prescribed runs have matching saved runs, set a `programState.pendingFellBehindPrompt` flag. Client renders the bottom sheet (PR-J) when it sees the flag on next app open and clears it on user choice.

5. **Remove client-side reconciliation** from `useProgram.ts`. Delete the reconciliation `useEffect` that today wraps race-no-show / recovery / fell-behind logic. The Q11a-A deep-equal guard (stopgap) also goes — there's no client write to guard.

### Tests

- Cloud Function unit tests for each new trigger (firebase-functions-test harness; already used by `weeklyPerformanceRollup`).
- Race no-show: fixture user with `raceDate = today - 1d`, no matching run → assert no-show write. Same user with a matching run → assert no write.
- Recovery entry via `onRunCreated`: fixture run matching `raceTarget` → assert recovery block written with correct end date. Non-matching distance → no write.
- Recovery exit: fixture user with `recovery.endDate < now` → assert cleared. With `endDate > now` → no change.
- Fell-behind: fixture week with 1/4 prescribed runs matched → assert flag set. 3/4 matched → no flag.
- Client: `useProgram` no longer calls `setDoc` from the reconciliation path. Render hook with stale state, assert it surfaces the state but does not mutate it.

### Migration

Existing users with client-side-reconciled state stay correct (state in Firestore is the same shape). New server triggers take over forward. No backfill needed — the next time each user's race/recovery/week-end event fires, the server reconciles.

### Trade-offs honestly noted

- **Latency.** Recovery hero pops in 3-10s after race completion on cold Function start vs <1s today. Acceptable — recovery is a multi-day state, not a moment.
- **Offline.** Run logged offline → queued via `offlineQueue.ts` → triggers fire when sync completes. User sees stale state until reconnect. Acceptable — recovery state isn't time-critical at the second-by-second level.
- **`functions/` is plain CommonJS JS.** Reconciliation logic loses TS type-safety on the server side. We extract shared constants (`recoveryWeeksForDistance` durations, `raceTarget` distance map) into a plain-JS module imported by both client (via build-time copy or shared package) and functions, to avoid drift.

### Sequencing

Ships before any Apple Watch work begins. Should sequence after PR-K (Q25 taper, small) and after PR-J ships its client-side version (we port the matured logic, not the in-flight one).

No telemetry to justify deviating. **Q10b (personalisation):** distance only — don't condition on experience or race-effort. Experience inference is fragile (new users may have years of unlogged training), race-effort needs estimation we don't have. Revisit with telemetry. **Q10c (surfacing):** keep current "Recovery week N of M" — explicit > vague date. Users in recovery are training-aware. No new work; existing PR-E values stand. Revisit in 6 months with churn data on race_prep users.                                                                                                                       |
| 11  | `useProgram` reconciliation cost & race conditions    | **Q11a → C** (server-side reconciliation), sequenced as **PR-L** before Apple Watch sequence. Watch is near-term; WatchOS can't run our React/TS reconciliation, so server-authoritative state is unavoidable. C dissolves Q11b (no client writes → no multi-tab clobber) and Q11c (no client reconciliation → no cold-start race). **Stopgap:** ship Q11a-A (deep-equal guard on the existing `useEffect`) in the interim — ~1hr work, prevents the recursion bug from biting production while PR-L is built. Removed in PR-L when the `useEffect` itself is deleted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### Apple Watch arc (W1–W14)

Decisions specific to the Apple Watch companion app. Numbered W1+ to keep separation from the original Programme-run sequence (Q1–Q25). Cross-arc references that mention "Q24" refer to the original Q24 (fell-behind sheet) unless explicitly tagged otherwise.

| W1  | Apple Watch data model & sync surface                  | **W1a → B+water** (run logging + water logging at launch; lift logging deferred). Water already lives on the Home screen as a glanceable action — extending it to the Watch is trivial and high-value for a fitness wearable. Lift logging is hard on a small screen and lower priority; revisit when run-logging is proven. **W1b → A** (direct Watch → Firestore via the Watch's own Firebase SDK, signed in via shared keychain). iPhone relay (B) is fatal for phone-free runs — defeats the whole point of Watch cellular. WatchConnectivity is also notoriously flaky. **W1c → A** (Watch GPS authoritative when paired; iPhone fallback when Watch absent). Modern Watch GPS is purpose-built and comparable to phone GPS. Merge-server-side (C) is over-engineered for v1. **Impact on PR-L:** server-side reconciliation must remain client-agnostic — no client-version checks, no "writes only from React app" assumptions. Already true in PR-L's design but pinned explicitly here. | W2  | Apple Watch architecture & onboarding                  | **W2a → B** (narrow shared Swift package). Capacitor doesn't support watchOS, so a native SwiftUI WatchKit target is forced. A (standalone, no sharing) risks drift on shared primitives — if marathon recovery duration changes in TS but not Swift, Watch shows a different end date than iPhone. C (thin-client, all logic server-side) is structurally impossible for real-time GPS. B keeps the shared surface narrow: pace formulas, `recoveryWeeksForDistance`, race distance enum, runMode enum, scheduled run status enum. Established as a `tropos-shared` Swift Package, ~1 day porting cost, then CI-enforced parity. Pieces excluded: nutrition, social, performance engine, charts. **W2b → C** (both Apple-standard install + in-app prompt). A alone is too passive — many users never browse the Watch app list. B alone misses users who installed iOS before Watch shipped. C costs an extra dismissible Home card, gated on `WCSession.isPaired`. **W2c → A** (shared keychain auto-sign-in). Tropos isn't security-sensitive enough to justify B's friction; C creates "why can I see but not start?" confusion. Implementation: App Group capability on both targets, write Firebase ID + refresh tokens to shared keychain on iPhone sign-in, read on Watch first launch. Firebase watchOS SDK supports custom auth since watchOS 7. **Implicit:** Watch starts runs independently of iPhone — no proximity check, full run lifecycle local (GPS, splits, pace cues, save). Matches Strava / NRC / Garmin. | W3  | Apple Watch run-screen UX                              | **W3a → A** (pace-first hero layout). Tropos is a training app, not a tracker — pace drives in-run decisions (interval targets, tempo effort), distance is a milestone. Splits with NRC (training) vs Strava (logging); Tropos's race-prep positioning aligns with NRC. Shipping one good default for v1; configurability (W3a-C) is v2. **W3b → B** (30s rolling-average pace). Instantaneous pace (A) is unusable — bounces 30s/mi on GPS noise alone. Cumulative average (C) hides current effort. Stacked current+average (D) too dense for a Watch face. 30s rolling-average is the modern standard. **W3c → A** (pause/resume + end, long-press end). Manual lap button (B) is redundant — guided runs auto-mark intervals. Inline music skip (C) is feature creep; users can swipe to the music app. Long-press end prevents the catastrophic "ended my run by accident at mile 18" failure mode NRC suffered for years. **W3d → A** (full guided-run mirror with haptics). B is half-built — iPhone is in pocket or absent on Watch runs, so cues must come from Watch (haptics + paired AirPods). C ("see iPhone") is hostile to phone-free runs. Means porting `useGuidedRun.ts` cue logic to Swift — not enormous (mostly "if elapsed > X, fire cue Y"). **Impact on `tropos-shared` package (W2a):** scope expands to include the 30s-rolling-average pace smoother and the guided-run cue scheduler — not just raw m/s → min/km conversion. Pinned here so the shared package boundary doesn't drift later. | W4  | Apple Watch offline & connectivity behaviour           | **W4a → three durability layers** (revised from "hybrid C"). In-memory buffer for the GPS hot path (per-tick, cheap), disk checkpoint every ~30s to local persistent storage (SwiftData or file — survives crash + watchOS app eviction), Firestore write of the assembled run doc on completion (Firestore's offline queue handles actual sync). Pure in-memory is fatal: watchOS suspends apps aggressively and memory can be evicted mid-run. Pure Firestore-offline-persistence has historically been flaky on watchOS, so it's the _sync_ layer, not the durability layer. Mirrors NRC / Strava checkpointing pattern. **W4b → A** (full offline R+W). Runs log, water logs, read views show last-cached data — stale-data indicator is **mandatory** (not optional as originally framed): a small "⟳ syncing" pill on cached views, hard-refresh on connectivity return. Stale planned-run is the failure mode without this indicator (user runs yesterday's prescribed workout because the Watch hadn't pulled the program change). **W4c → per-collection rules, five not three** (revised from original C). Runs split: GPS core append-only (each run = new doc, no conflict possible), metadata (title, notes, shoe) LWW by serverTimestamp. Workouts (lifts): LWW by serverTimestamp, dedupe by `clientWorkoutId` — workouts are heavily edited mid-session, append-only doesn't fit. Meals: LWW by serverTimestamp, dedupe by `clientMealId` — meals get corrected post-photo. Water: summed per-day across writers with tombstone-based deletes (so deleted entries don't reappear via re-sync). Profile: LWW by serverTimestamp. **PR-L impact:** reconciliation function now needs five explicit routes and tombstone support, not three. **W4d → B + pending-sync banner**. In-run sync dot (green = synced, yellow = queued, red = save failed) during active runs only — runners need to know if their PR run is being saved. Outside runs, no per-screen badge (too noisy), but if the queue is non-empty on Watch home, show a small "X items pending sync" banner with tap-to-retry. Mirrors Garmin's "sync pending" pill. Red-state at run end fires a haptic so users don't walk away thinking the save succeeded. **Impact on `tropos-shared` (W2a):** picks up the disk-checkpoint module (shared by Watch and iPhone) and the `clientId` conventions (`clientRunId` / `clientWorkoutId` / `clientMealId`) that drive server-side dedupe.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| W5  | Apple Watch ↔ iPhone live-run coordination             | **W5a → B + Watch-wins tiebreaker**. First device to start a run wins; second device silently mirrors as follower. A's prompt is hostile when the common case is "I tapped iPhone-start by accident while my Watch is already recording" — silent mirroring matches Strava + NRC. But "first to start" is ambiguous within a 5-second start-collision window (clock skew + WatchConnectivity message ordering), so the protocol encodes a deterministic rule: **Watch wins ties** (dedicated GPS hardware, designed for run primacy). **W5b → C + 10% threshold + Watch→iPhone only**. Manual handoff only via an explicit "Transfer to iPhone" prompt when Watch battery hits 10% mid-run (not 15% — Garmin's threshold, avoids prompt fatigue). Auto-handoff (B) is the dream but Bluetooth GPS-stream splicing is engineering-expensive and the failure modes are worse than no handoff. No handoff (A) is too defeatist for the real "marathon Watch dies at mile 18" scenario. If user ignores the prompt and Watch dies, W4a's disk checkpoint preserves whatever was written and the run uploads on reboot. iPhone→Watch direction deferred to v2 (iPhone batteries are bigger, rarely matters). **W5c → A + normal sleep + long-press end + staleness indicator**. Follower device shows a live mirror — pace, distance, elapsed, controls. B (placeholder only) is hostile if user has phone out. C (use follower for other things) is fantasy: during an active run the follower is in a pocket or being watched, not used for water-logging. End button requires long-press on follower (matches W3c — prevents pocket-end). Follower screen follows normal iOS sleep behaviour (don't force-on, that drains battery). WatchConnectivity lag is 1-2s typical; if last update >5s old, dim the pace number and show a "⟳ syncing" pill so the runner doesn't trust stale pace. **W5d → A + Watch-wins tiebreaker + defer auto-merge**. Dedupe by `clientRunId` — Watch and iPhone negotiate over WatchConnectivity at start time, one canonical clientRunId is emitted, only the authoritative device writes. Watch wins ties (consistent with W5a). If WatchConnectivity is unavailable at start (Watch in airplane mode), both devices generate independent clientRunIds → two runs in History. Rare enough to accept; user deletes the duplicate manually. Server-side GPS-track-similarity auto-merge (B-style) deferred to v2 — false-merge risk is high and the data destruction is unrecoverable. **PR-L impact:** reconciliation function only needs to handle the rare "two clientRunIds, same user, overlapping start time" case by leaving them as separate runs (no merge in v1). **Impact on `tropos-shared` (W2a):** WatchConnectivity protocol contract pinned to shared package — `StartRunMessage`, `RunStateUpdate`, `HandoffRequest`, `PauseCommand`, plus the Watch-wins tiebreaker constant.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| W6  | Apple Watch app data freshness & background refresh    | **W6a → A** (read-through on launch, no listener, no APNs). Originally proposed C (Firestore listener while foreground + APNs silent push for background changes); stress-test killed it. APNs silent push is rate-limited to ~2-3/hr per app, so heavy edits drop pushes — staleness isn't really solved by push. Foreground listeners cost persistent network and battery on a constrained Watch radio. The narrow win (program edited on iPhone _while_ Watch app is foregrounded) is rare and not worth the APNs setup + Cloud Function + battery cost. Cold-launch over cell already takes 1-2s of fetch regardless of strategy — a read-through there is no slower than a listener's initial snapshot. Strava and Garmin both fetch-on-launch rather than maintaining background listeners. **W6b → simpler B** (read-through + optimistic local increment + write-behind, **no listener**). Cross-device water sync only matters when both devices are concurrently in use, which is rare. Without listener, tapping +1 on Watch when iPhone just incremented produces a temporary display inconsistency — W4c's water-sum server-side rule reconciles to the correct total on next Watch refresh. No data loss, just brief display lag. Matches the existing iPhone water-card optimistic pattern. **W6c → hybrid (Sync now primary, Start anyway secondary, auto-proceed <5s)**. Show a stale-data badge when (a) last successful sync >24h ago, OR (b) on launch we detect server `updatedAt` > cached `updatedAt`. Badge surface offers "Sync now" as the prominent CTA and "Start anyway" as the secondary action — the lazy-tap path is the safe one. If sync completes within 5s, auto-proceed to start so the friction is invisible in the common case. The override-allowed escape (Start anyway) preserves the legitimate "no signal at race start, plan already pulled" use case. **Net architecture impact:** drops APNs silent push, drops persistent Firestore listeners on Watch, drops the Cloud Function that would have emitted push triggers. Simpler than the original framing. **Impact on `tropos-shared` (W2a):** _removes_ the listener-setup module from the planned shared contract — the package boundary shrinks slightly. PR-L's water-sum rule already covers the W6b cross-device case; no new reconciliation work.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| W7  | Apple Watch notification & alert policy                | **W7a → APNs default routing + Watch-local triggers for in-run events only** (revised from original "manual domain split"). The original C ("run-related → Watch, non-run → iPhone") breaks under cross-cutting cases: streaks span run-days and rest-days, shoe-mileage reminders are run-related but shouldn't fire mid-run, water reminders fit both contexts, lift PRs come from iPhone-logged workouts. The actual rule is "which device has the user's attention now?" — which is what Apple's APNs routing already does (delivers to Watch when iPhone is locked / wrist-raise / etc.). So we don't define the split: send all notifications via standard APNs and let Apple route. **The only Watch-local triggers are in-run events** (pace cues, mid-run PR haptic, in-run sync state) which bypass APNs entirely and fire from the Watch app. **W7b → Smart Stack widget + complication** (no Watch-specific push reminders). Complications alone are invisible to users with analog watch faces (no slot); Smart Stack (iOS 16+ Live Activities surface) is the modern Apple pattern and matches Fitness app's own approach. Morning "today's prescription" push fires from iPhone under W7a's routing — no Watch-specific push needed. Default opt-out matches Tropos's "calm, adaptive" brand positioning (most fitness apps default-on; we don't). **W7c → B + Friday-evening weekly check-in** (informational, iPhone-routed). No daily missed-run pings — single-day misses are normal, and shame-driven daily reminders have known retention backfire (Duolingo owl research). Q24's fell-behind weekly sheet handles low-completion weeks. The Friday evening "you have N unfinished prescribed runs this week" fires as an informational nudge (factual tone, not punitive) — covers the 6-days-missed gap that Q24 (original arc — fell-behind sheet) alone leaves silent for too long. Routed via APNs (W7a). **W7d → C-tiered with "headline PR only mid-run, sub-PRs batched"**. Pure mid-run celebration (A) breaks focus and risks false-positives on GPS noise; pure end-of-run (B) loses the in-moment dopamine. C: single 0.3s custom haptic pattern reserved for PRs (not the generic `success` haptic), fired only on the _headline_ PR for the run (the PR matching the run's primary distance — 5K run → 5K PR only). Sub-PRs (e.g. fastest 1K split inside a 10K run) batched for end-of-run save-screen celebration. Conservative thresholds (e.g. 5K PR fires at 5.0km + 0.1km buffer with smoothed pace) prevent false positives. All celebration logic runs Watch-local — no iPhone or network dependency. **No PR-L impact** — notifications are local-device events. **Impact on `tropos-shared` (W2a):** adds `prTracking` module (PR detection must run on Watch). Adds **PR-classification logic** — which PR is the "headline" for a given run — needs to be deterministic and shared so Watch and iPhone celebrate identically.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| W8  | Watch-side complications & Smart Stack widget content  | **W8a → A with explicit content state machine**. Ship one complication slot at v1 ("Today's planned run"), but the _content_ of that slot is a state machine, not a fixed string. Priority order: in-run (pace + distance, highest priority) > today's scheduled run (short template label + distance) > lift day ("Lift" or hide per user preference) > rest day ("Rest" or fade) > freeform fallback (weekly km or "Log run"). Single slot avoids competing with Apple Fitness / weather / battery for watch face real estate (Apple Fitness / NRC / Strava all ship one or two complications max). Multiple complications (B/C) deferred until telemetry shows which slot users actually fill — premature menu-expansion has no signal. Circular-small slots constrain copy to ~4 chars; pin per-template short labels (e.g. "E30" for easy_30, "T8K" for tempo_8K). **W8b → C but state-driven, not clock-driven** (revised from original "morph by time of day"). Clock-driven morphing breaks for shift workers / non-9-5 runners and risks the evening "you didn't run today" shame-ping pattern explicitly avoided in W7c. State-driven matches Apple Fitness widget's actual behaviour (morphs by ring state, not clock). Five-state catalogue: (1) pre-run today — "Today: Easy 30 · target 6:00/km"; (2) run in progress — "Active · 2.3km · 5:23/km · target 6:00/km"; (3) post-run completed today — "Done · 5.2km · 5:48/km avg · NEW 5K PR"; (4) rest day — "Recovery · 3 of 4 runs this week" (passive); (5) tomorrow preview after a user-configurable evening hour (opt-in) — "Tomorrow: long run 18K". Smart Stack will surface the widget when its heuristics predict a glance; we don't control timing, we control content. **W8c → C-hybrid with pinned mechanics**. Event-triggered + 1-hour safety net via WidgetKit's `TimelineProvider`. Engineering details: app calls `WidgetCenter.shared.reloadAllTimelines()` on local state transitions (run start, run end, midnight rollover); `TimelineProvider` policy uses `.after(now + 1hr)` as the safety-net cadence. 1-hour interval is separate from `WKApplicationRefreshBackgroundTask` quota (~50/day total) — WidgetKit refresh is cheaper than I initially framed. Accepts up-to-1-hour staleness for iPhone-side program edits, consistent with W6a's "no Firestore listener on Watch" decision. **W8d → B with pinned details**. Staleness signal is **not** time-based on the data itself — it's `lastSuccessfulSync > 24h ago`, tracked in shared UserDefaults between app and widget process (widget process can't query Firestore directly). 24h threshold matches W6c's stale-badge rule (single source of truth for staleness across surfaces). Visual treatment: 60% opacity render (still legible) + small ⟳ overlay in a corner. Hiding the widget (C) is too aggressive — reads as "app broken." Showing without indicator (A) is dishonest — user trusts stale "today's run." **Impact on `tropos-shared` (W2a):** beyond `TodayRunSnapshot` already noted in W7, add the **complication content state enum** (`.inRun`, `.scheduled(template)`, `.lift`, `.rest`, `.freeform(weeklyKm)`) and the **widget state enum** (`.preRun`, `.inRun`, `.postRun`, `.rest`, `.tomorrowPreview`) as shared types — so Watch and any future iPhone widget render from the same state model. **No PR-L impact.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| W9  | Apple Watch app navigation & screen architecture       | **W9a → B with pinned details** (single-screen Today + drill-in for secondary). TabView (A) wastes a swipe gesture on rarely-used surfaces; hub-and-spoke (C) is the dated watchOS 1-3 pattern; full NavigationStack (D) loses the home-screen anchor. B matches Apple Fitness / NRC / Strava (single primary screen, drill for depth). Three pinned details: (1) **run-in-progress is a fullscreen modal overlay** over Today — Today shouldn't disappear mid-run, modal handles its own lifecycle (pause/resume/end via W3c long-press); (2) **long-press Start = ad-hoc escape hatch** that bypasses today's prescription and opens the freeform mode picker — needed for "freeform easy run on a lift day" or "different template than prescribed" cases; (3) **settings via toolbar gear icon** (or watchOS Force Touch menu) — buried but rarely needed. **W9b → A with hierarchy pinned**. Modular vertical scroll (C) is verbose for Watch; B (hero only) buries water (the second-most-used Watch surface per W1). A: hero takes ~60% (today's planned run + Start button), water "+1" tile below, weekly progress strip at bottom. Hierarchy: **Start = primary CTA on scheduled run days; replaced by smaller secondary "Log a run" button on rest days** (which routes into the mode picker, same target as W9a's long-press). Water tile always present, smaller. **Week strip metric** = `completedScheduledRuns / prescribedRuns · Week N of M` for race-prep users (matches Q24's fell-behind sheet), `weeklyKm` for freeform users. Works on the smallest Watch screens (38mm/40mm) with the week strip becoming a single text line. **W9c → C (smart skip)**. A is too eager (accidental Start while reaching for water); B is friction for the common case. C: on a scheduled run day, one tap → countdown → run (intent unambiguous from today's prescription); on freeform / no-plan, brief 4-template mode picker (Easy / Tempo / Long / Intervals — matches current `programEngine` template set, no "custom" on Watch for v1). **Template provides initial target, doesn't lock total distance** — user runs as long as they want; haptic guidance scales (e.g. "approaching target" instead of "stop"), matching the existing `useGuidedRun.ts` behaviour. Picker is Watch-local, works offline (per W2c + W4). **W9d → B (last 3 runs + iPhone link)**. A (full scrollable history) is overkill on Watch — deep analysis belongs on iPhone where pinch-zoom maps work. C (no history) is too pessimistic — quick "what was yesterday's pace?" glance is useful, Apple Fitness shows last 3 workouts too. B: 3 runs visible, tap a row → **Watch-native run detail (stats only — distance, time, pace, splits; no map)**; "View all on iPhone" link via Handoff opens iPhone History page, graceful fallback message if iPhone unreachable. List refreshes from local store when a new run saves (no Firestore listener per W6a). **Impact on `tropos-shared` (W2a):** nothing new — `TodayRunSnapshot` (W7), complication/widget state enums (W8), and template definitions (already in `programEngine.ts` / `templates.ts`) cover this navigation layer. **No PR-L impact.** | W10 | Watch run-screen multi-screen layout & paging gestures | **W10a → A, no auto-return** (revised on second-pass stress test). Digital crown scroll with page-snapping (one click = one page) for primary / splits / music. Horizontal swipe (B) collides with watchOS screen-edge dismiss and Series Ultra Action button; crown is glove-tolerant and the established convention (Apple Workout, Garmin, Strava all use it). Original draft included a 10s auto-return to primary — **dropped on second pass**: it's a fragile invention (no reference app does it), and the "pace is always more time-critical" assumption breaks for non-target-pace runs where the user genuinely wants splits in view. Match Apple Workout — user stays where they put themselves. **W10b → B (primary + splits + music) with three pinned details**. Three screens matches Apple Workout exactly. A (minimal) is too austere — splits are universally requested. C (Garmin-style 5 screens) is over-engineered: heart rate fits inline on primary, map is hard to read on a Watch screen, 5 screens is too many to crown-scroll mid-run. D (configurable) is right answer in 18 months with telemetry, premature now. Pinned: (1) **HR inline on primary, top-right, small**, but **only when confidence is high** — optical HR is wildly inaccurate during running (wrist movement artefacts); show a small status dot (green = locked, yellow = uncertain, hide if confidence too low for several seconds) to prevent runners from making effort decisions on bad data; (2) **music screen uses in-app `MediaPlaybackView`-style controls** (track + prev/play-pause/next), with an **explicit empty state** ("No music playing · Open Music app" CTA) when no audio source is active — empty/missing screen would read as broken; (3) **splits screen shows last 5 by default**, full list scrollable via crown — a marathon's 42 km of splits is unusable as a single scroll. **W10c → A (list view, adaptive columns)**. Graph (B) is hard to read at a glance on a 41mm screen mid-run. List with `pace + delta vs target` per completed split is more scannable and matches what runners actually want. Three-column `Km#                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Pace | Delta`for target-pace workouts (delta color-coded — green ahead, red behind); two-column`Km# | Pace`for freeform / easy runs (no target). Respects user's`distanceUnit`preference. Live in-progress split shown in a distinct "current" row at the top (italicised / "in progress" indicator), frozen at end-of-run with a "partial" marker. GPS dropout mid-split accepted as ±2-3% error (matches Garmin/Apple). Pause behaviour: stops distance accumulation and resumes from the same point — split still completes at full km regardless of pause time. **W10d → C with three pinned engineering details** (primary screen morphs during active interval). A (persistent band) steals real estate on easy runs; B (separate guidance screen) is hostile (having to swipe mid-tempo to see what you're meant to be doing). C: during an active interval the primary screen's supporting content swaps — pace stays hero, "Tempo · 187m to go · 4:45/km" replaces the usual weekly-target/total-elapsed content; at rest transition, swaps to "Rest 60s · jog easy." Pinned: (1) **200ms`.opacity`/`.move`transitions** between phases — Apple's standard for state changes that should feel responsive but not abrupt (SwiftUI default 0.35s is too fast for a transition the runner needs to register); (2) **pace hero dims to 50% opacity during rest** — pace targets aren't active during rest, dimming is a visual cue; (3) **specific haptic-name mapping** to avoid collision with vocabulary used elsewhere (W7d reserves`success`for PRs, run start/end uses`start`/`stop`): `intervalStart → directionUp`(speeding into work),`intervalEnd → directionDown`(winding down),`restStart → click`(light tap entering rest),`restEnd → notification`(heads-up before work resumes); (4) **audio cue fallback via paired AirPods** when watchOS haptics are disabled at OS level (silent mode, accessibility) — same audio cue track used by`useGuidedRun.ts`, implied by W3d's "full guided-run mirror" but pinned explicitly here. Pause behaviour during intervals: both the run timer and interval timer freeze; resume continues both. **Impact on `tropos-shared`(W2a):** beyond`IntervalState` (already noted), add the four **haptic phase-name constants** (`HapticPhase.intervalStart`/`.intervalEnd`/`.restStart`/`.restEnd`) mapped to system haptic types — so Watch and any future iPhone consumer use identical names, and audio-cue fallbacks reference the same enum. **No PR-L impact.** |
| W11 | Watch onboarding flow on first launch                  | **Reference apps:** Strava + Apple Workout drop user straight to action (auto-sign-in, JIT permissions); NRC's upfront-permission-wall is the worst-reviewed pattern; Garmin uses hybrid (location early + JIT for the rest); Hevy and Strong both require iPhone counterpart and block standalone Watch use. **W11a → C with auth sub-states pinned**. Auto-sign-in via shared keychain → Today screen → JIT permissions. Matches Strava + Apple Workout's "get to action fast" model. D's intro screens are friction Strava deliberately avoids; A's "permissions entirely deferred" creates awkward "where do I enable HR?" moments. Launch sequence needs explicit auth sub-states: (1) **keychain has valid Firebase token** → Today screen; (2) **keychain empty / token revoked** → "Open Tropos on iPhone to sign in" screen with `WCSession.isReachable` polling for auto-progress; (3) **iPhone not paired** → W11d explainer. Critical mechanic: **don't just check `Auth.currentUser != nil`** — Firebase doesn't auto-validate tokens, so a user who signed out on iPhone leaves a non-nil-but-revoked token on Watch. **Call `getIDToken(forcingRefresh: true)` on launch** to catch revoked accounts cleanly. Also **show a 10s spinner during keychain settling** on first install (App Group sync can take seconds) before falling through to "Open on iPhone." **W11b → C (hybrid: location early, others JIT) with denial fallbacks pinned**. Pure B (all JIT) means tapping Start triggers a modal mid-tap — jarring. Pure A is NRC's upfront-wall. C: location requested ~5s after Today screen stabilises with a one-line in-screen explainer ("Tropos needs location to track your runs · Allow"). **Pin: When-in-use only** — Tropos doesn't need background location; `HKWorkoutSession` grants location-in-background even with WIU for cellular Watch standalone runs. HealthKit requested at **first run save attempt** (not first launch, not HR enable) — rationale dialog "Save this run to Apple Health?" triggers HealthKit prompt if not granted. **Notifications never requested on Watch at all** — W7a routes all notifications via standard APNs (iPhone-side delivery, Apple auto-routes to Watch), and Watch-local haptics (W10d interval transitions) are inline not OS-level. Denial fallbacks: **Location denied** → one explainer screen "Tropos needs location to track runs · Open Watch Settings" with `x-apple-watch-settings:` deep link (no re-prompt — violates iOS HIG); **HealthKit denied** → one-time toast "Apple Health save skipped · Enable in Settings later" then graceful degradation (run still saves to Firestore), no re-nagging on subsequent runs. **W11c → B simplified + accessibility pins**. Single coachmark over whichever primary CTA is visible (Start on run days, "Log a run" on rest days per W9b). Apple HIG discourages coachmarks generally, but Apple Workout itself pulses workout-type buttons on first launch — exception when affordance isn't obvious. Simplified copy: **"Tap to start a run"** only (drop the long-press hint — overload for first-time users; long-press is discoverable later or never, fine for casual users). Dismiss permanently after first display via shared UserDefaults flag (clears on uninstall, which re-shows on reinstall — fine, reinstall is rare). Hevy briefly tried multi-step coachmarks in 2024 and removed them after user backlash; our C option correctly rejected. Accessibility pins: (1) **respect `UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled`** — fade-in static arrow instead of pulse for users with vestibular sensitivities; (2) **VoiceOver announcement** via `accessibilityLabel = "Tap to start a run"` + `accessibilityViewIsModal = true` so the coachmark gets focus on screen-load before main content. **W11d → A with mechanic corrected**. Block-with-explainer when iPhone isn't paired or Tropos isn't installed there. Hevy and Strong both require iPhone counterpart; Tropos needs iPhone for program editing, history, social, nutrition — building a parallel Watch-only sign-in surface is wasted effort for ~99% non-use. **Original draft proposed sending an install-notification to iPhone via WCSession — technically impossible**: WCSession requires _both_ sides to have the app installed, so there's no companion extension to receive the message if iPhone Tropos isn't installed. `SKStoreProductViewController` is iOS-only with no Watch equivalent. Final mechanic: **plain text instruction on Watch** ("Install Tropos on your iPhone to continue · Open the App Store and search 'Tropos'") + **`WCSession.isReachable` polling every 30s** for auto-progress when iPhone Tropos launches and is in range (cheap — `isReachable` is a property check, not a network call). State detection: `WCSession.isPaired` distinguishes paired-but-no-app from no-iPhone-at-all; show slightly different copy for each case. **Impact on `tropos-shared` (W2a):** nothing new — onboarding is platform-specific code, no shared logic. **No PR-L impact.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| W12 | Watch settings catalogue & structure                   | **Reference apps:** Strava + NRC + Hevy + Strong all ship minimal Watch settings (everything else iPhone-only) — the dominant companion-app pattern. Garmin is the outlier (many on-device settings) because Garmin watches are _standalone_, not companions. Apple Workout's split between audio-feedback-volume (per-device) and distance-unit (account-wide) inspires W12c. **W12a → A (minimal in-run toggles only) with 4-item catalogue pinned**. Watch settings UX on a tiny screen is slow and error-prone; keep deliberate choices on iPhone. Exceptions are in-run toggles where grabbing iPhone mid-run is hostile. Concrete catalogue: (1) **audio cues on/off**, (2) **voice cue frequency** (every km / every 5min / never), (3) **auto-pause on/off**, (4) **audio cue volume slider** (paired AirPods + Watch speaker). HR display on/off is **deferred** — W10b's confidence-gating handles it (no user toggle needed; HR shows when reliable, hides when not). Haptic intensity is OS-level (watchOS Settings), not our control. Plus a **"More settings on iPhone →"** row using WCSession message to surface iPhone Settings page (graceful fallback toast when iPhone unreachable, same pattern as W9d "View all on iPhone"). 4 items fits one screen, no scroll. **W12b → A (24pt gear icon, top-right of Today)**. Force Touch (B) was deprecated in watchOS 7 and the hardware is gone Series 7+; Apple HIG says don't use anywhere now. C is mixed convention. A is the modern pattern. Pins: **24pt gear icon top-right** (inline with time indicator, doesn't shrink hero); **VoiceOver tab order explicit** — gear announces _after_ main content (hero, Start, water, week) since settings is secondary to today's run. **W12c → C (split by category) with explicit rule and category table**. Pure A (iPhone canonical everywhere) forces Watch to write through to Firestore on every toggle — slow on cell, broken when offline. Pure B is confusing (user expects "km" to mean km everywhere). C splits by user expectation: **"consistency expected across devices = data preference (Firestore-stored); per-device personalisation expected = display preference (local UserDefaults)."** Concrete category table pinned to `tropos-shared`: **data** = distance unit, weight unit, voice cue language, voice cue voice (Sam/Alex), race goal, program preferences — _voice cue language/voice goes to data despite being technically local-file selection_ because users expect consistency. **display** = audio cues on/off, audio cue volume, auto-pause on/off, voice cue frequency. Apple Workout makes this exact split (audio feedback volume per-device, distance unit account-wide). No migration needed — Watch is new, reads existing iPhone settings from Firestore on launch (per W6a read-through). **W12d → A (sign-out available on Watch) with three pins**. B is hostile (user wants to sign out on the Watch they're holding _now_); C is destructive (could disconnect iPhone unexpectedly, breaking flow). A: explicit confirm sheet → routes to W11a's "Open Tropos on iPhone to sign in" screen. Pins: (1) **confirm sheet copy** — "Sign out of Tropos on this Watch? · You'll need to sign in again on iPhone to use Tropos here." (makes Watch-scope + iPhone re-sign-in requirement explicit); (2) **pre-flight check for pending writes** — Watch may have a queued run that hasn't synced; if non-empty, warn "X items not yet synced — sign out anyway? Data will be lost." User chooses (Z option, not discard-silently nor block-until-drained); (3) **keychain cleared on Watch only** — App Group keychain entry for Firebase token wiped on Watch; iPhone keychain unaffected per Apple's per-device-keychain design. Multi-account support automatic via W11a's `getIDToken(forcingRefresh: true)` on next launch. **Impact on `tropos-shared` (W2a):** beyond the `SettingsCategory` enum, pin the **concrete category table** (which keys are `.data` vs `.display`) as a shared constant so Watch and iPhone route storage identically without drift. **No PR-L impact** — data settings live in profile doc, already covered by PR-L's profile LWW rule from W4c.
