| W13 | Watch app testing strategy                             | **Reference apps:** Strava runs a physical Watch lab (gold standard but multi-month investment); NRC uses paid contractor dogfood + TestFlight (mid-tier); Hevy is TestFlight-only with founder publicly discussing the "small team, ship fast, accept some field bugs" trade-off; Strong similar to Hevy. Tropos's team scale puts us in the NRC / Hevy hybrid camp; Strava's lab approach explicitly rejected as over-investment for our scale. **W13a → D (unit + iOS simulator + manual device-test checklist) with three pins**. C (full automated device CI) is what Strava can afford but multi-month investment we can't justify pre-launch. A (unit only) is too thin — iOS simulator tests catch a lot of iPhone-side regressions cheaply. (1) **Concrete 10-item checklist** lives at `docs/testing/watch-device-checklist.md` as source of truth (PR template links to it), split into **8 per-PR items (fast, ~1hr)** — GPS accuracy on one outdoor run, Apple Health workout write, connectivity-drop survives mid-run, cross-device clientRunId tiebreaker, haptic patterns distinguishable, cellular phone-free run, disk checkpoint after force-quit mid-run, keychain sync — and **2 weekly items (slow, multi-hour)** — 24h background-refresh budget burn, full WatchConnectivity state matrix; (2) **Screen recording (any tool — Loom, QuickTime, etc.)** required for run-related items in PR description; desk-test items get text confirmation; (3) **Simulator UI coverage targets**: 60% global, 80% for critical paths (auth flow, run logging, food parsing, run save). **W13b → D (hybrid: staff dogfood + TestFlight cohort) with four pins**. A alone is slow; B (physical lab) is overkill; C alone misses fast-iteration day-to-day issues. (1) **Mandatory weekly dogfood on the week a Watch-touching PR merges** (optional otherwise); (2) **8-scenario structured dogfood**: scheduled-run start, ad-hoc-run start (long-press Start), pause/resume mid-run, long-press end, splits screen via crown, phone-free run, Today widget updates post-run, sign out + sign back in; **PR author appends 1-2 scenario-specific checks** tailored to the PR's change; (3) **Watch in-app "Send feedback" button writes to Firestore `feedback/{uid}/watch/{auto-id}` collection** (works offline via W4a queue, no iPhone dependency unlike WCSession approach — team reviews via internal admin tool); (4) **TestFlight cohort target 50 recruited via in-app banner shown to users with ≥5 completed runs** (signals engagement, filters tyre-kickers); **promotion gate at ≥25 completed a full run cycle on the build**; cohort communicated upfront to "expect 1-2 builds per week." **W13c → C (tagged tests) with three pins**. A is naive — HealthKit fails silently on simulator; B is too rigid. C uses Swift Testing's tag traits — `@Test(.tags(.simulatorOnly))` / `.deviceOnly` / `.either`. (1) **Xcode 16+ minimum** dev environment (tag traits unsupported below); (2) **macOS GitHub Actions runner for simulator CI** (~$12/month at Tropos PR volume — trivial; watch concurrency on free tier); **device-only tests are manual** on developer machines, no nightly device CI for v1; (3) **Monthly device-test sweep on Series 4 + Series 9** (low-end + current); **minimum supported = Series 4 / watchOS 10**, aligning with Apple's official baseline. Default to `@deviceOnly` when uncertain (avoids CI noise from flaky simulator-incompatible tests). **W13d → A+B narrowed (staff smoke gates TestFlight, TestFlight gates production) with three pins**. Pure A misses field issues; pure B is slow. Sequence: ship to TestFlight only after **staff smoke passes**; promote TestFlight to App Store only when **(i) 14-day TestFlight window elapsed AND (ii) zero `severity-critical` bugs AND (iii) ≥10 testers completed a full run cycle on the build**. Cosmetic bugs don't block — only criticals do. Pins: (1) **`watch_run_completed` telemetry event (aggregate-only, counts not per-user identifiers)** for the ≥10 metric; **user-identifiable analytics opt-in lives on iPhone under privacy settings** (per W12c — analytics is a `.data` category preference, iPhone-canonical, Watch respects iPhone's setting); (2) **`severity-critical` GitHub label**: any team member can apply, release manager (PR author by default) confirms; **critical-fix triggers a fresh 7-day TestFlight window** (not full 14), **release manager can extend** for soak-time-dependent fixes (e.g. battery-drain regressions need 5+ days); (3) **Two-tier hotfix gate** when production is critically broken: **standard hotfix = 48h TestFlight + ≥3 testers complete a run on the build**; **expedited hotfix = 12h TestFlight + staff member completes a run on the build + screen-recording proof of fix** (use only when production is critically broken, e.g. app crashes on launch). **Impact on `tropos-shared` (W2a):** the package's `Tests` target is **the first build target** — gates all subsequent Watch work. **≥80% line coverage** required on the locked-decision modules: pace smoothing + 30s rolling average (W3b), `recoveryWeeksForDistance` (Q10a), `IntervalState` transitions (W10d), haptic phase constants (W10d), settings category table (W12c), state enums (W8), `TodayRunSnapshot` (W7), PR classification (W7d), Watch-wins tiebreaker constants (W5d). No Watch UI work begins until the shared package hits the bar. **PR-L impact:** Cloud Function reconciliation tested independently via Firebase Functions emulator + test framework — separate concern from Watch testing but worth flagging as a parallel testable surface.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| W14 | Watch PR build order & sequencing                      | **W14a → B (medium, 8 PRs) with two pins**. Coarse (A: 3-5 large PRs) makes review hostile — 5000+ line PRs nobody can meaningfully review. Fine (C: 1 PR per W-decision = 13+ PRs) is overhead-heavy — CI, review, merge cycles outweigh value. B clusters W-decisions into ~8 reviewable PRs at ~500-1500 lines each. Pins: (1) **Calendar estimate ~10-12 weeks** at ~1 week/PR cadence, including PR-L prerequisite — quarterly planning sees this; (2) **Prototype-first discipline for architectural-heavy PRs** (PR-W-1 and PR-W-3): build a throwaway-branch prototype to validate the structure before committing to the broader PR (e.g. prototype the Today screen layout before locking PR-W-1's architecture, prototype pace smoothing before locking PR-W-3's run-flow shape). **W14b → C (trunk-based with feature flag) with three pins**. A (strict linear) is too slow; B (long-lived feature branches) accumulates merge debt. C: all PRs merge to main behind a feature flag; flag flips when alpha gate is met. Pins: (1) **New `src/lib/featureFlags.ts` module** (subscription.ts is conceptually wrong home — paid features vs experimental features); single Boolean `watchApp` to start; (2) **Dual-gate model** — JS feature flag controls iPhone-side UI surfaces (Watch-install-prompt card on Home, gated on `WCSession.isPaired`); TestFlight build cohort controls Watch app distribution (alpha → beta → production). The Xcode Watch target builds unconditionally; the JS flag only controls iPhone-side visibility. Both gates flip independently; alpha staff get a TestFlight build with the JS flag still off in production; full launch flips JS flag true and promotes TestFlight to production cohort; (3) **Boolean for v1, percentage rollout deferred** — Tropos doesn't yet have percentage-rollout infrastructure. **W14c → A (record + save run minimum = alpha gate) with two pins**. Alpha = "we can use it." B (include W6 prescription discovery) and C (full feature set) both delay the dogfood feedback loop. NRC, Strava, Hevy all shipped their Watch apps with just "record + sync" first; widgets came later. Pins: (1) **Complete alpha loop** = record run + GPS works + Apple Health write + save + run appears in iPhone History via Firestore sync. No WatchConnectivity (cross-device deferred to PR-W-5), no widget, no settings polish; (2) **Alpha cohort communicated upfront about scope** — "widget + complication arrive in PR-W-6, this build doesn't have them" — prevents "app appears broken" misreads. **W14d → C (hybrid: types upfront, logic incrementally) with three pins**. Pure A (full shared package before any Watch UI) is too strict — blocks Watch progress on logic that won't be needed until late PRs. Pure B (everything incremental) risks shared types drifting between PRs. C: ship type definitions + constants in PR-W-0, ship algorithmic logic in subsequent PRs as consumers land. Pins: (1) **PR-W-0 has type-encoding + invariant tests** (not "empty Tests target"): Codable conformance for Firestore serialisation, invariant checks (e.g. `HapticPhase.intervalStart` distinct from `.success`), enum exhaustiveness; (2) **≥80% coverage gate scoped to algorithmic modules only** (pace smoothing, PR classification, recovery duration, state transitions, settings category routing) — not type-only files where 80% line coverage is meaningless; (3) **Per-PR coverage scope** — gate applies to modules introduced/modified in that PR, not the entire shared package on every PR. **Reference apps:** NRC and Strava both shipped Watch apps with "record + sync" as alpha cut, growing widget/complication surfaces in later releases — pattern validated. Hevy's TestFlight-only pre-launch matches our dual-gate flag approach. **PR sequence (8 PRs, locked):** **PR-W-0** `tropos-shared` SPM skeleton + core types (location: `ios/tropos-shared/` with `Package.swift`; iPhone Xcode target + Watch target both import via SPM); **PR-W-1** Watch target + architecture skeleton + foundational auto-sign-in via shared keychain (W2 + W11a); **PR-W-2** Today screen scaffold + Start CTA + minimal 4-item settings + coachmark (W9 + W12a 4-item + W11c coachmark); **PR-W-3** core run flow + GPS + 3-layer durability + HealthKit JIT + save (W3 + W4a + W11b HealthKit) — **alpha gate**; **PR-W-4** multi-screen layout + intervals + haptics + HR confidence (W10 + W3d guided-run mirror); **PR-W-5** cross-device + freshness + reconciliation (W5 + W6) — **PR-L hard prerequisite** (Cloud Function reconciliation must merge first); **PR-W-6** notifications + complications + Smart Stack widget (W7 + W8) — may split into PR-W-6a (notifications + APNs) and PR-W-6b (complications + widget) if implementation exceeds 1500 lines; **PR-W-7** onboarding polish (denial-fallback screens, deep-links) + sign-out flow with pre-flight pending-writes warning + JS flag flip on TestFlight beta cohort (W11 full + W12d sign-out) — **beta gate**. **Hard dependencies:** PR-W-0 blocks all; PR-W-1 blocks PR-W-2+; PR-W-3 blocks PR-W-4 + PR-W-5; PR-L blocks PR-W-5. **Risk register:** Apple submission delay (1-2 wk/cycle), HealthKit denial behaviour discovered late (PR-W-3 era), WatchConnectivity production behaviour differs from simulator (PR-W-5), watchOS Series 4 compatibility (caught by Q24c monthly device-test sweep), real GPS accuracy lower than simulator (caught by Q24a checklist item 1). Mitigation: **each PR ends with a real-device dogfood per Q24a's checklist**, surfacing issues at PR boundary not at release time. **`tropos-shared` impact:** each PR-W extends the package — PR-W-0 ships type definitions and constants with encoding tests; PR-W-3 ships pace smoothing and distance/pace algorithms with full unit tests; PR-W-4 ships PR classification + haptic mapping with tests; PR-W-5 ships WatchConnectivity protocol contract (`StartRunMessage`, `RunStateUpdate`, `HandoffRequest`, `PauseCommand`) with tests. Coverage gates each PR per W13. **PR-L impact:** explicitly enumerated as the hard prerequisite for PR-W-5; PR-W-5 cannot start until PR-L merges. |

### Running Plan v2 arc (RP1–)

Decisions specific to the v1 → v2 transition for the running-plan architecture — the lift/run asymmetry, `PlannedTrainingItem` unification, cross-modal periodisation. Numbered RP1+ to keep separation from the original Programme-run sequence (Q1–Q25) and the Watch arc (W1–W14). Distinct concern: this arc focuses on the source-of-truth shape that feeds both the iPhone Home screen and the Watch (W-arc consumes `programState.runDays[]` extensively; lifts are currently weekly-template-driven, not date-indexed).

Cloud Function reconciliation audits dual-write integrity (same pattern as PR-L for runs). **RP1d → C (strategy pattern refactor as standalone PR)**. Standalone PR (~1-2 weeks, clean rollback). **Two additional pins**: (1) **Minimal one-way consumer API** — adapter exposes only what Home actually consumes today (v1 → v2-minimal-view); don't pre-expose unused`PlannedTrainingItem`surface that could drift as RP1a evolves; (2) **CI snapshot diff for lift-card rendering** — automated before/after comparison catches render regressions. **Three concrete pieces of work, sequenced**: (1) **RP-1:`PlannedTrainingItem` proposal doc** (~1 day, ships immediately, no code) — paper design for the unified type, state machine, invariants, backfill mapping rules; (2) **RP-2: Home lift-rendering strategy refactor** (~1-2 weeks, depends on RP-1) — minimal adapter, snapshot tests, standalone PR; (3) **RP-3: v2 migration PR** (~3-6 weeks, depends on RP-2 + RP1b trigger fires) — dual-write + Cloud Function reconciliation + one-time backfill + force-update gate. **`tropos-shared`impact:** none in v1 (RP1a is iPhone-side design). When RP-3 lands, the unified`PlannedTrainingItem`enters`tropos-shared` as a shared type so Watch can consume both lifts and runs through one interface. **PR-L impact:** RP-3's dual-write reconciliation uses the same Cloud Function pattern as PR-L; explicit per-collection rule added to the existing five-rule set (per W4c). |
| RP2 | Race-prep + lift-deload sync (PRD for RP1b primary trigger) | **Reference apps:** Hal Higdon's marathon plans don't address lifting at all (runners assumed pure); Strong + Hevy don't address running at all (lifters assumed pure); Hybrid Athletic / Caliber / Hybrid Athlete apps try cross-modal but logic is manual user choice; Garmin Coach is run-only; TrainingPeaks is multi-sport but periodisation is coach-job not app-job. **No reference pattern exists for "lifts auto-deload during run taper"** — Tropos is inventing the cross-modal logic. This lock IS the draft PRD that triggers RP1b's primary v2 trigger. **RP2a → D (suggest-only) with three pins**. Full coupling (C) too prescriptive — many users lift recreationally, don't want lift volume held hostage to run plans. Do-nothing (A) defeats RP1 v2 purpose entirely. Light-deload-only-on-taper (B) misses build-phase fatigue accumulation. D: Tropos surfaces recommendation, user accepts (default) or overrides per-week. Pins: (1) **Default = accept banner** (one-liner, not blocking modal): "Taper week 1 of 2 — lift volume drops one set. [Got it / Override]"; (2) **3-consecutive-override-then-suppress rule** — after 3 identical overrides (e.g., "keep normal volume"), suppress the prompt for this race-prep block and adopt the override as the new default; surface "you can change this in Settings" once on suppression; (3) **Only fires when `runMode === "race_prep"`** — freeform / structured mode is no-op. Lets us adapt over time based on override telemetry. **RP2b → A (drop one set) with three pins**. Reduce-sets is the most common approach in published hybrid-athletics literature (5/3/1's deload weeks drop sets). Reduce-loads (B) is risky on already-fatigued legs. Skip-workouts (C) loses consistency — users feel "lazy" missing lift days even when prescribed. Different-exercises (D) too complex to model and explain. Pins: (1) **Rule = "drop one set per exercise"** (concrete, easy to communicate, no percentage math) — volume reduction varies -25% to -33% depending on exercise's normal set count, but the rule is the rule; (2) **Specialised templates (5/3/1, Texas Method, etc.) defer to their own deload week** if defined; if not defined, skip the workout entirely for that taper week; (3) **Uniform across upper/lower body for v1** — race-prep specifically taxes legs but per-body-part targeting gets complex fast (squat vs deadlift vs leg press vs lunges). Re-evaluate with telemetry. **RP2c → B-with-default-skip + three pins**. Pure A (race day = always skip) too rigid — 5K race ≠ marathon for next-day capacity. C (distance-aware) requires per-distance rules that get arbitrary fast. D (day-before also rest) over-protective. B-default-skip = conservative coaching norm; rare "race-and-lift" audience can override. Pins: (1) **Surface decision in pre-race Friday weekly check-in** (W7c) the week before race day — gives user time to plan; (2) **Race-day lift skipped, NOT re-scheduled** — race day + recovery week deload = the volume reduction; re-scheduling defeats the purpose; (3) **Override respected silently** — no warning when user accepts lifting on race day ("you're lifting on race day" is patronising). Day-after race covered by RP2d's recovery-week deload starting immediately post-race. **RP2d → A (lifts deload during recovery) with three pins**. Recovery week is when the body is healing — continuing normal lifts contradicts the explicit recovery goal. B (lifts stay normal) is incoherent. C (user choice) dumps the decision during a vulnerable moment. D (suspend lifts entirely) loses lift momentum and habit signal. Pins: (1) **Deload rule = same as RP2b — "drop one set per exercise"** — one consistent rule across both taper and recovery, eliminates "is recovery -20% or taper -25%?" memorisation; (2) **Duration = run recovery duration per Q10** (5K=1wk, 10K=2wk, half=3wk, marathon=4wk — Hal Higdon-aligned); (3) **Same 3-consecutive-override-then-suppress rule as RP2a** — cross-arc consistency reduces user surprise. Stacked race cycles: **recovery deload supersedes race-prep deload** until recovery period ends (recovery is the more conservative state). **Critical implications:** (1) **This lock IS the draft PRD** — locks the design that RP1b's primary trigger requires; product owner now needs ≥1 month race-prep usage data to validate the gap before v2 migration starts. (2) **`PlannedTrainingItem` (RP1a) must model cross-modal phase state** — a lift workout needs to know "I'm in week N of race-prep, taper has started, RP2b's drop-one-set rule applies." (3) **Override-tracking telemetry** — measures whether default recommendations are correct; acceptance rate >70% confirms defaults; <30% means rethink the recommendation. (4) **`tropos-shared` impact:** none in v1 (W1a deferred Watch lift logging entirely). When RP-3 ships, the Watch could surface "taper week: 2 sets instead of 3" on the lift day complication via the v8 unified shape. **No PR-L impact** until RP-3 ships, then dual-write reconciliation covers lift-workout writes per W4c's per-collection rules.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| RP3 | `programState` migration safety on first-v2-open UX         | **Reference apps:** Notion runs schema migrations server-side transparently to client; Linear has explicit "Loading workspace..." splash on schema changes; Apple iCloud Photos migration shows "Preparing your library..." with progress (Apple's canonical pattern for non-trivial client-side migrations); Strava / Garmin don't expose schema migrations to users. Tropos's pattern is closest to Apple iCloud Photos — potentially-long backfill for power users, no Firebase-native convention. Fills the previously-reserved RP3 slot. **RP3a → C (splash 2s → background banner) with four pins**. Pure modal (A) is hostile for power users with 200+ workouts (5s+ migration). Pure background (B) risks user starting to log a workout mid-migration → shape collision. D's "continue in background" button over-engineered. C balances: typical users see brief splash and never know it was there; slow cases gracefully degrade. Pins: (1) **Min splash display = 500ms** — prevents flash-of-splash-then-immediate-disappear on the typical 50ms-to-complete case; (2) **Max splash display = 2s** — then dismiss splash and switch to banner; (3) **Banner: top of screen below status bar, persistent (non-dismissible) until done, tap shows progress-detail modal** — matches Apple iCloud Photos' "Photos sync paused" pattern; (4) **Writes prevented during migration**: toast on attempt "Setting up your training plan · Try again in a moment" — less complex than write-queue-and-replay, more predictable. 2s threshold hard-coded for v1; telemetry will reveal whether 1s or 3s is right. **RP3b → D (drop + flag + post-migration banner) with four pins**. A (drop silently) leaves users in the dark. B (show "X items couldn't be migrated" mid-migration) intrusive during splash moment. C (halt migration with error screen) blocks the user from using the app entirely — worst UX. D continues migration (user keeps moving) and flags the account so a banner explains post-migration. Pins: (1) **Failed-to-migrate entries preserved in `users/{uid}/migrationOrphans/` subcollection** — banner links to a screen showing these so user can re-anchor manually (assign to a date) or delete; (2) **Detectable inconsistencies enumerated**: orphan `templateId` (references a template no longer in `templates.ts`), missing required field (e.g., `phase` absent), type mismatch (e.g., `fatigueScore: "high"` instead of number), un-anchorable to `weekSchedule` (user's weekSchedule has zero lift days but entry is a lift); (3) **Banner suppression rules**: dismissed once → suppressed 14 days then re-shown; dismissed twice → suppressed permanently. Don't nag indefinitely; (4) **Support tooling**: orphan subcollection queryable read-only; each orphan entry includes original timestamp + `originalEntry` blob for forensics. Support can reproduce the user's pre-migration state. **RP3c → C (resumable via per-entry checkpoint) with four pins**. A (retry 3 times with backoff) blind to structural failures (quota, permanent outage). B (fail-fast manual retry) hostile UX. D (offline-first migration) too complex for multi-shape data. C: checkpoint per batch, resume on next attempt. Pins: (1) **Checkpoint stored in `users/{uid}/migrationCheckpoint` Firestore doc** — cross-device coordination (local UserDefaults would break multi-device); (2) **Checkpoint granularity: every 10 entries** — 20 checkpoint writes for 200 workouts. Loss on interruption = at most 10 entries to re-migrate (idempotent per RP1c, no harm); (3) **Atomic final completion**: final checkpoint = Firestore batch write that sets `migrationStatus: complete` AND bumps `programSchemaVersion: 3` together — never half-complete; (4) **No bail-out threshold**: migration paused indefinitely until network returns. Banner shows "Migration paused · Tap to retry" with manual-retry button. Auto-retry every 30s while app is in foreground. **RP3d → D (hybrid: `programSchemaVersion` + `migrationStatus`) with four pins**. A (`programSchemaVersion` alone) doesn't capture in-progress partial states. B (`migrationStatus` alone) redundant with schemaVersion for final state. C (local-only flag) breaks multi-device coordination. D combines: `programSchemaVersion` is authoritative data state (v2 vs v3, written only after migration completes); `migrationStatus` tracks progress (`pending` / `in_progress` / `complete` / `error`); devices coordinate via this. Pins: (1) **Firestore transaction for race resolution** — first device to flip `pending → in_progress` wins; second device's transaction fails on read-version mismatch, retries, sees `in_progress` → shows "Updating on another device · This device will sync when done" UX; (2) **`migrationLockExpiry: serverTimestamp + 5min` field** — if second device sees `in_progress` but lock is expired, it can attempt takeover (resume from checkpoint); (3) **Lock takeover also uses Firestore transaction** — same first-wins logic when multiple devices race to take over an expired lock; (4) **Server-authoritative on reinstall** — fresh client reads `programSchemaVersion` + `migrationStatus` from Firestore on launch; sees `complete` → skips migration entirely. No "fresh client thinks it needs to migrate" footgun. **Critical implications:** (1) **RP-3 migration PR scope** gains six new tested behaviours — splash↔banner state machine, orphan-subcollection writes, inconsistency-detection per enumeration, Firestore checkpoint logic, multi-device race resolution, lock-takeover after 5min expiry. (2) **Six telemetry events** (aggregate-only per RP4d): `migration_started`, `migration_completed`, `migration_failed_inconsistency`, `migration_failed_network`, `migration_resumed`, `migration_takeover_from_expired_lock`. (3) **Support tooling addition**: read-only query on `users/{uid}/migrationOrphans/` keyed by `migrationWarning: true`. (4) **No new `tropos-shared` impact** — RP3 is iPhone-client-side + Firestore data. (5) **No new PR-L impact** beyond W4c's reconciliation per-collection rules. |
| RP4 | `programSchemaVersion` bumping conventions                  | **Reference apps:** Firebase Firestore is schema-less; most apps don't version explicitly. Notion / Linear use server-side transparent migrations + versioned API endpoints. Garmin / Strava don't expose this externally. GraphQL / OpenAPI ecosystems use versioned schema + deprecation cycles. **No Firebase-native convention** — Tropos invents. Numbered RP4 (not RP3) — RP3 slot reserved for the deferred migration-safety-on-first-v2-open grill. **RP4a → D (hybrid: one version per Firestore document + sub-versions when needed) with three pins**. Pure A (one user-tree-root version) couples unrelated fields. Pure B (current state — `programSchemaVersion` + `weekScheduleVersion`) works fine. C (per-collection + embedded sub-versions everywhere) over-engineered. D refines B with explicit rule. Pins: (1) **One version field per Firestore document** — profile (own doc) has `weekScheduleVersion`; programState (own doc) has `programSchemaVersion`; (2) **Sub-version added ONLY when both criteria are met** — (a) the subfield is _read independently_ of its container (e.g., a Cloud Function reads `runDays[]` without touching `weekHistory[]`), AND (b) the subfield has its _own migration helper_ in `migrations.ts`. Both required; (3) **New collections start unversioned** — add versioning only when the shape first evolves; not a default-on burden. **RP4b → C (bump when migration is needed) with four pins**. A (any field change bumps) is too noisy. B (only breaking changes) is too narrow — renames are breaking but feel additive. D (calendar-based) is arbitrary. C is the principled rule: if old data works correctly without migration, no bump. Pins: (1) **Rule = "if any reader CANNOT correctly read old data without a migration step, bump"** — forward-compat tolerance (undefined → default inline) does NOT count as migration; (2) **Deprecation periods don't bump** — when old field + new field coexist temporarily, no version change; (3) **Removal of deprecated field bumps** — the breaking moment is removal, not addition; (4) **PR template checkbox forces author awareness** — "Does this change require a migration helper? If yes, bump `CURRENT_PROGRAM_SCHEMA_VERSION` + add an entry to `migrations.ts`." Process gate prevents drift. **RP4c → A (forward-compat only) with two pins**. B (bidirectional, clients write any version indefinitely) is too complex for our scale. C (strict-forward-only, reject old data) breaks rolling deploys. D (versioned API endpoints) over-engineered. A matches `migrations.ts` current "shape-repair on read" pattern. Pins: (1) **Schema parsers (Zod, runtype, etc.) MUST use `passthrough` / `extend` mode** for forward-compat — strict-mode parsers reject unknown fields and break forward-compat; document the convention in `docs/proposals/schema-versioning.md`; (2) **No new required-for-new-version fields during dual-write periods** — during RP1c's ≥4-week dual-write window, can't add a v3-only required field that v2 can't write. Wait until off-ramp gate (≥4 weeks <1% divergence + min-client-version bump) before dropping v2 support. **RP4d → A (field-presence authoritative) with four pins**. B (User-Agent / SDK version header) is hostile — couples backend to client release cycle. D (no detection) ignores the real signal. A matches `migrations.ts` current pattern. Pins: (1) **Cloud Function validator authoritative on version** — server matches payload fields against declared `programSchemaVersion`; if v3 fields present but `programSchemaVersion: 2` declared, reject as `invalid-argument`. Client claim is hint, server is authority; (2) **SDK version logged on every Cloud Function call** (via Cloud Logging, queryable for analytics — adoption rate, deprecation planning); (3) **No capability gates on SDK version** — version is data marker, not capability marker; (4) **Force-update flow uses schema version (not SDK version) as trigger** — RP1c's off-ramp logic remains schema-version-driven. **Critical implications:** (1) **RP-3 dual-write handshake is now precisely defined** — v3 client writes carry `programSchemaVersion: 3`, server validates v3 field shapes, dual-writes both shapes per RP1c. v2 clients keep working until RP1c off-ramp gate. (2) **`migrations.ts` is the canonical migration ladder** — each `CURRENT_PROGRAM_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump corresponds to one `migrateVN→VN+1()` function. (3) **`docs/proposals/schema-versioning.md` design doc** ships alongside RP1a's `planned-training-item.md` proposal — pins these conventions for the next contributor. (4) **PR template update** adds the migration-bump checkbox. (5) **No `tropos-shared` impact** — versioning conventions are server-side + iPhone-client-side; Watch consumes whatever shape is delivered. **No PR-L impact** beyond what W4c already specifies. **STATUS 2026-05-24 — partial artifacts shipped.** `docs/proposals/schema-versioning.md` and `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` shipped (closes implications #3 and #4). RP4a pin #1 wording clarified in the proposal doc: "at most one doc-level version field; sub-versions are additive per pin #2 criteria" — prevents future contributors from adding `profileSchemaVersion` "to comply" with a strict reading. RP4d pin #1 (CF cross-checks declared version against payload shape) and pin #2 (SDK version logged on every CF call) deferred to v3 cycle — TODO comment added to `functions/lib/validatePlanPayload.js` so the gap is rediscovered when v3 work begins.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

### Food parser orchestration arc (F1–)

Decisions on the food-logging orchestration layer — when each parser (NL / Gemini text / Gemini image / barcode) fires, how Pro gating applies, how offline + cross-parser results reconcile. Numbered F1+ to keep separation from Q (Programme-run), W (Watch), and RP (Running Plan v2) arcs. Distinct concern: this arc focuses on the food-logging UX surfaced via `FoodComposerCard.tsx`, `useFoodAnalysis` hook, and the `analyzeFood` / `analyzeFoodText` Cloud Functions.

| F1    | Food parser orchestration (text + AI + barcode) | **Reference apps:** MyFitnessPal — NL search-first, no AI; user picks from database matches. MacroFactor — custom-tuned NLP, database-driven, no Gemini-style layer. Cronometer — strict database lookup, very high-quality data, no AI parsing. Lose It! — "Snap It" AI photo (Pro-only); text input is database lookup only. **Pattern: reference apps converge on database-first; AI is a Pro upsell layer.** Tropos is unusual in offering BOTH client-side NL parser AND server-side Gemini — opportunity (better UX) and complexity (orchestration questions). Stress-tested across two passes; 32 pins total. **F1a → A with smart-skip on zero/low-confidence match, six pins**. Pure cascade (B) hides Gemini cost from the user. Parallel (C) wastes compute. Tier-split (D) creates free/Pro UX inconsistency. A keeps explicit user choice but adds a paved on-ramp when NL fails. Pins: (1) **NL top-match confidence < 0.5 triggers "Try AI analysis" CTA banner** above empty/low-confidence results; (2) **Banner placement: above results**, not inline; (3) **Never auto-fires** — user-initiated only (respects compute cost transparency); (4) **`aiAnalysisEnabled: boolean` privacy opt-out** in user settings (default `true`); when `false`, hide all AI CTAs and replace smart-skip with "Try typing more detail"; (5) **Multi-item input**: CTA surfaces if ANY item has confidence < 0.5 (aggregate the lowest); (6) **i18n deferred to v2** — Spanish + French DB seeds + locale-aware parser; v1 ships English-only with "Try typing in English" tip on persistent low-confidence matches. **F1b → B+C hybrid (free text-AI with cap, image Pro-only), eight pins**. Pure A (current — Pro for text + image) gates the most-common path (typing food and getting AI parsing) behind Pro — hurts free retention. Image-AI is genuinely Pro-tier (Vertex AI image input ~$0.0025 vs text ~$0.000125/1k chars, **20x cost**). Split. Pins: (1) **Free = 10 text-AI calls/day**; Pro user-facing = unlimited but **100/day server-side abuse-protection cap**; (2) **Cap resets at user's LOCAL midnight** (device timezone; `timezone` field on user doc if available, else UTC fallback); (3) **Trial users (per `subscription.ts` trial logic) bypass the rate limit** entirely — Pro behaviour during trial showcases the value; (4) **Image AI stays Pro-only** (0/day for free, 100/day Pro abuse-protection); (5) **Cap does NOT refund on meal delete** — prevents spam-create-delete-refresh abuse; (6) **Settings page shows daily usage** ("AI analyses today: 3 / 10" pill); tap → upgrade flow for free users; (7) **Caps are SEPARATE** per feature — text-AI counter and image-AI counter are independent in `rateLimiter.js` (two action keys: `text_ai`, `image_ai`); (8) **Trial activation unlocks immediately** mid-day — Pro behaviour applies as soon as trial starts, no wait for next cap window. **Soft upsell UX**: invisible when ≥5 remaining, subtle pill "3 left" at 3-5, active prompt "Out of AI analyses today — Pro for unlimited" at 0. **F1c → C (log first, refine later), ten pins**. A's "Queued" status is uninformative (food disappears until queue drains). B is hostile when offline at the gym. C: user logs immediately with NL-parsed data, Gemini refines in background when online, updates entry quietly with badge. Pins: (1) **"Refined by AI" badge in meal list** (small "AI" pill next to meal name) AND **in meal detail** (banner: "Refined by AI on [date]"); (2) **Silent failure** when Gemini errors — log `gemini_refinement_failed` to Cloud Logging; NL-parsed entry is functional; don't surface technical failures; (3) **Refinement queue checks meal doc exists** before applying (drop the refinement task if deleted); (4) **ASAP refinement when online** (no delayed batching — defeats the perceived-UX purpose); (5) **Sequential queue processing** (one refinement at a time, low concurrent load); (6) **Refinement is NOT rate-limited** — background quality-of-service, not user-initiated; the cap applies to explicit "Try AI" taps only; (7) **Silent refinement, no push notification** — the badge is the audit trail; (8) **`gemini_high_delta_refinement` telemetry when caloric value differs from existing entry by >25%** — for monitoring systematic disagreement patterns (don't surface to user; user-edit-lock per F1d protects); (9) **Defer refinement while meal detail is currently open** in the UI — track open-detail-ID in app state, queue refinements for that ID until the screen closes (eliminates the "fields change while I'm looking" UX bug); (10) **7-day backlog limit** — only refine meals from the last 7 days (by `clientCreatedAt`); older queued meals stay as-is (low-value refinement, API spam, week-late surprise). **F1d → D (hybrid: Gemini fills missing, never overwrites user-edits), eight pins**. A loses Gemini value when user types incomplete info. B (Gemini-wins) too aggressive. C (confidence-wins) hard to calibrate (NL and Gemini confidence values are different scales). D respects user intent. Pins: (1) **`userEditedFields: string[]` array** on the in-progress meal entry; populated as user manually edits (clicks number/text field and changes it); once a field name appears, it's locked from AI overwrite; (2) **Initial NL parse does NOT count as user-edited** — only manual post-parse edits lock; (3) **Undo button on "Refined by AI" badge** restores pre-refinement state, **time-bounded to 24h** (after that, refinement is canonical, older snapshot garbage-collected to avoid bloated docs); (4) **Refinement applies only when Gemini confidence ≥ "medium"** (matches existing `confidence` enum on `FoodAnalysis` type); low-confidence results discarded silently; (5) **User-disagrees-with-AI surface deferred to v2** — F1d v1 = silent fill-missing only; disagreement surfacing adds complexity for an edge case, revisit with usage data; (6) **Explicit tracked-for-lock fields**: `{calories, protein, carbs, fat, portionSize, name}`; **`notes` and `tags` are user-only** (Gemini never touches); fields outside this list don't participate in the lock system; (7) **New fields from Gemini auto-added** (no lock-checking since they didn't exist on user side) — `fiber`, `sugar`, `sodium`, etc.; (8) **No cascade locking** — each field is locked independently; editing `calories` only locks `calories` (no math-relationship enforcement; real foods have caloric variance from labels); **per-item locking** in multi-item meals — lock is at the item level, not the meal level; each sub-item has its own `userEditedFields[]`; meal totals derived from sub-items. **Critical implications:** (1) **Settings page** adds the `aiAnalysisEnabled` privacy opt-out toggle AND the daily-usage pill ("AI analyses today: X / 10"); (2) **`rateLimiter.js` Cloud Function** gets two new action keys: `text_ai` (10/100 daily) and `image_ai` (0/100 daily), independent counters using the existing transaction pattern; (3) **`offlineQueue.ts`** extends with: deferred-refinement task type, 7-day backlog filter, defer-while-meal-detail-open check, doc-exists check before applying; (4) **`useFoodAnalysis`** hook tracks per-item lock state for multi-item meals + per-item `userEditedFields[]`; (5) **`FoodComposerCard.tsx`** gains: smart-skip CTA banner above empty results, "Refined by AI" badge with undo button time-bounded to 24h, `userEditedFields` tracking on each tracked-fields input; (6) **Telemetry events** (aggregate-only per RP4d): `text_ai_call`, `image_ai_call`, `gemini_refinement_failed`, `gemini_high_delta_refinement`; (7) **CLAUDE.md update**: replace current "AI food analysis via Gemini API · Pro feature" line with the split — text-AI free with 10/day cap, image-AI Pro-only. **No Watch impact** — W1a deferred food logging on Watch entirely. **No PR-L impact** beyond W4c's existing per-collection rules (meals: LWW by `serverTimestamp` with `clientMealId` dedupe — refinement updates respect this). **STATUS 2026-05-24 — F1b implementation drift surfaced by Sub2 audit.** F1b's locked structure (separate `text_ai` + `image_ai` counters, daily reset, free=10 text + 0 image, pro=100 each, trial bypasses entirely) is NOT what currently ships. Trial bypass IS aligned (`isUnlimited = isPro **STATUS 2026-05-25 — F1b implementation slice (Track C) complete.** Server-side per-action quota helper (`functions/lib/aiScanQuota.js`) — daily window with user-local-midnight reset via `Intl.DateTimeFormat`+ the user doc's`timezone`field (UTC fallback for missing/invalid), separate`text_ai`+`image_ai`counters, free = 10 text/0 image, Pro = 100 each, trial bypass via`computeEffectiveTier` → "pro" — shipped via PR #757. Lose It! — barcode is free; "Snap It" image-AI is Pro. **Pattern: reference apps lean on a proxied/cached layer rather than direct OFF calls.** Tropos hits OFF directly today via `BarcodeScanner.tsx` (314 lines, `@zxing/browser` + direct OFF v2 API, no cache, 10s timeout). Stress-tested across two passes; 25 pins total. **F2a → B (fill missing only) with six pins**. OFF data is community-submitted and frequently incomplete (calories present but protein missing, etc.). A (bypass entirely) leaves users stuck. C (always refine) wastes compute on clean barcodes. D (user-prompted) adds friction in the common case. B triggers F1c's background refinement only when at least one tracked field is missing. Pins: (1) **Refinement triggers on `null` / `undefined`, NOT `0`** — zero is valid data (black coffee, sparkling water, sugar-free gum); (2) **ANY missing tracked-field triggers** — if `protein` is null but `calories/carbs/fat` are present, fire refinement (Gemini may also adjust other fields, respecting F1d locks); (3) **Deduplicate repeat scans by barcode + `clientMealId`** — second scan within 30s reuses first lookup result, no re-fetch from OFF, no re-queue refinement; (4) **Don't correct macro/calorie inconsistency** — if OFF returns calories=200 but macros sum to 50, use OFF's values as-is (real foods have ±20% label variance anyway; F1d's user-edit-lock lets users fix manually if they spot it); (5) **Always prefer per-serving over per-100g** — if only per-100g is available AND serving size is parsable as grams, scale to serving; if serving size is unparsable freeform string, flag entry with `unitConfidence: "low"` + surface banner "Per-100g data only · Confirm serving size"; (6) **`servingSize` is locked-by-OFF for barcode-entry path** — overrides F1d's default (which doesn't track servingSize for general locks); Gemini doesn't rewrite OFF's descriptive servingSize string (e.g., "1 bottle (500ml)" stays). **F2b → A (always free) with two pins**. OFF API is free; client-side `@zxing/browser` is local; no Tropos compute cost. Rate-limiting a free-cost feature is friction without benefit. Pro-gating barcode would feel mean (the cheapest input mode locked behind paywall). Image-AI's Pro gate was justified by ~$0.0025/image; barcode has none. Pins: (1) **Server-side 100/day abuse cap per user** via `rateLimiter.js` — prevents shared-IP rate-limit issues at OFF (one malicious user spamming → OFF rate-limits our IP/User-Agent → all Tropos users hit OFF errors). Indistinguishable from "always free" to legit users; (2) **No-anonymous-auth requirement documented** — Tropos currently doesn't support anonymous auth (only Email / Google / Apple per CLAUDE.md). If anonymous is ever added, anonymous accounts get tighter 10/day barcode cap. Document in `docs/agents/auth.md` (or equivalent) that anonymous auth must stay disabled for the 100/day cap to hold. **F2c → C as target architecture, A as current stopgap, nine pins**. A (network-only direct-to-OFF, current behaviour) works for v1 but exposes us to OFF latency + outages. B (per-device cache) is partial. C (Cloud Function proxy cache with global share) is the proven Yuka / MyFitnessPal pattern — instant for cached barcodes, outage-tolerant, faster. C adds a Cloud Function + Firestore cache collection, so it's deferred until measurable need. **Trigger to build C: p95 barcode lookup latency >3s over 7-day window OR an OFF outage incident.** Pins: (1) **30-day cache TTL** — product nutritional facts rarely change; conservative window; (2) **"Powered by Open Food Facts" attribution** in `BarcodeScanner.tsx` UI footer + About / Settings / Credits (OFF ToS-required); (3) **Cache key = barcode only** — barcode is globally unique per SKU; regional variants have different barcodes; nutritional facts are universal; (4) **Cost telemetry** — log `barcode_lookup_latency_ms`, `barcode_cache_hit_rate`, `barcode_cf_cost_estimate` (aggregate-only per RP4d); dashboard alerts on p95 > 3000ms; (5) **Persistent high-delta auto-invalidation** — cache entries include `refreshedAt` timestamp; auto-invalidate after 7 days of `gemini_high_delta_refinement` telemetry hits (>25% caloric difference vs Gemini) for that barcode. **For newly-cached entries (first 7 days), use a tighter 1-day high-delta threshold** — single high-delta hit invalidates within the new-entry window; after 7 days of stable data, switch to the 7-day-persistent rule; (6) **CF min-instance=1** on the `lookupBarcode` Cloud Function (Cloud Functions v2 feature) — ~$3-5/month at most; eliminates cold-start latency that would defeat the cache speed benefit; (7) **Multi-region deferred to v2** — monitor `barcode_lookup_latency_ms` bucketed by user region; if EU p95 > 3s, deploy a `europe-west1` mirror. US-only acceptable for v1; (8) **`lookupBarcode` CF requires auth** — `context.auth` check at handler top, same pattern as other Tropos CFs; prevents anonymous scraping of our cached data; (9) **Stopgap (A) ships immediately**: add OFF attribution footer + 100/day abuse cap to current `BarcodeScanner.tsx`. **F2d → D (explicit fork: type details OR try AI) with eight pins**. A's bare error ("Product not found · Try manual entry") is dry. B's auto-smart-skip might be over-eager (homemade meals genuinely shouldn't be in OFF — AI is the right fallback, not "manual entry"). C (auto-fall-back via OCR) too speculative. D respects user intent with a clear fork: two prominent CTAs. Pins: (1) **AI analysis is primary button** (top, filled with brand color); **Type details is secondary** (bottom, ghost button) — reasoning: most barcode-not-found scenarios mean the product genuinely isn't in OFF; AI is the right path; (2) **AI route shows placeholder hint** ("What is this product?") with NO auto-filled text — barcode is captured silently in meal metadata for analytics; user types the product name they recall; (3) **Type-details route opens standard `FoodComposerCard` with "Add to my pantry" pre-checked** — manually-entered products auto-add to user's local DB; bonus: builds personal food DB over time; (4) **AI call counts against F1b's text-AI cap** — same as F1a's smart-skip CTA; consumption is the same regardless of entry path; (5) **Back gesture returns to fork screen, not camera** — user can pivot between AI / type-details without re-scanning; (6) **Pantry reviewable in Settings → "My pantry"** — list entries with usage stats ("Used 0 times in last 30 days"); user can edit/delete; auto-check stays default-on at scan time but unchecking is one-tap for one-offs; (7) **Pantry entries surface FIRST in NL parser results** (above database matches), labelled "Your pantry" — user picks the right one; pantry is opt-in for re-use, not auto-substitute; (8) **AI calls log `entryPath` field** in telemetry — values: `"nl_smart_skip" \| "barcode_not_found" \| "direct"`. Lets product analytics see which entry path drives Gemini usage; informs UX tuning. **Critical implications:** (1) **Pantry feature surfaces** — was implicit, now becomes a real product surface (`Settings → My pantry` with usage stats + edit/delete + auto-add toggle). New scope, modest UX work; (2) **`unitConfidence: "low"`** field added to meal entries when per-100g-only data is used; banner UX in `FoodComposerCard.tsx`; (3) **`entryPath` telemetry attribution** on AI calls — extends F1's telemetry events with `entryPath` dimension; (4) **`rateLimiter.js`** gets `barcode_lookup` action key with 100/day cap (free, doc-pinned that anonymous = 10/day); (5) **`BarcodeScanner.tsx` stopgap changes** (ship immediately): OFF attribution footer + 100/day cap + dedupe-by-barcode-clientMealId check; (6) **`lookupBarcode` CF (deferred to v2)**: Firestore collection `barcodeCache/{barcode}`, 30-day TTL, auth-required, min-instance=1, US-only initially; (7) **`offlineQueue.ts` (when F2c-C ships)**: barcode lookups for cache-miss-while-offline get queued like other writes; (8) **CLAUDE.md update**: barcode scanning section gains "Powered by Open Food Facts" line; pin the 100/day abuse cap. **No Watch impact** (W1a deferred food logging on Watch; barcode is camera-based). **No PR-L impact** (no new collections that need cross-device reconciliation; cache is global, not per-user). **Revisited at F2c-r** — see refined framing under no-launch-pressure lens (telemetry-gated build trigger + privacy invariant + "A-current-C-conditional-on-data" reframe replaces the prior "C-target-A-stopgap" framing).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Stress-tested across THREE passes; 32 pins total. **F3a → D (single-shot + add-another-item loop) with eight pins**. Pure single-shot (A) loses cross-item context for complex meals; multi-shot (B) before AI returns is confusing UX; burst (C) is 3x cost per meal. D balances: AI extracts all items from one photo by default; "Add another item" CTA appears after AI returns for power-user case (restaurant meal with separate plates). Matches Google Lens. Pins: (1) **Quantity stepper for duplicates** (default 1, bump to 2 without retaking) — saves an AI call and matches natural mental model; (2) **Each photo's results are independent** — low-confidence on photo #2 → retry/type for that item only, previously-added items stay; (3) **Hard cap 5 photos per meal entry** — beyond that, "5 items added — start a new meal entry for more"; (4) **Newest items at top** (reverse-chronological) — freshest in user's mind first for review; (5) **Edit route preserves meal context** — all items from camera flow stay in the same `clientMealId`; manually-added items merge in; (6) **Per-item delete on confirmation screen** (⊖ icon or swipe-to-delete) — deleted items removed from in-progress meal, doesn't trigger re-analysis; (7) **"Merge into one" CTA when AI returns >3 items from a single photo** — collapses into a single entry, user types name, macros sum across merged items (handles sandwich-style over-decomposition); (8) **Photography-tips messaging includes "not a menu/package" hint** — when F3c's consecutive-low-confidence tips fire, brief inline copy reminds the user to photograph actual food, not a menu listing or package. **F3b → C (confirmation with original photo) with nine pins**. Auto-save (A) hides AI errors. Inline preview (D) loses visual verification. B (confirmation without photo) misses the visual sanity-check. C shows photo alongside parsed items + macros — best for "yes that's a chicken bowl, AI nailed it." Matches Vivino. Pins: (1) **Photo TOP, item list BELOW** (scrollable) — photo is the source-of-truth visual; (2) **Respect EXIF orientation at display time** (display upright); EXIF stripped on upload copy, used pre-strip for display; (3) **200pt-tall (16:9) thumbnail at top, tap to expand to full-screen modal with pinch-zoom** — standard iOS pattern; (4) **Explicit Confirm / Edit / Discard semantics**: Confirm = saves to Firestore + closes; Edit = closes confirmation, routes to `FoodComposerCard` with items pre-filled; Discard = exits without saving + **does NOT refund image-AI cap** (already consumed); (5) **30-minute background timeout** — confirmation state in client memory only (no Firestore write yet); on resume after >30min backgrounded, show "Your photo session expired · Start over?" with retry; prevents memory bloat from idle confirmations; (6) **Multi-photo carousel at top of confirmation when >1 photo** (horizontal swipeable) — single photo = single thumbnail; tap any photo expands to full-screen pinch-zoom; (7) **Save-failure preserves state + retry via `offlineQueue.ts`** — network drops on Confirm tap → retry banner ("Couldn't save · Tap to retry"); photo + parsed items stay in client memory; uses F1c's resumable-write pattern; (8) **Two-stage resize**: local preview retains original-source resolution capped at **4096px on longest edge** (handles 50MP+ cameras for pinch-zoom quality); upload-to-CF copy is resized to **1280px** (privacy + bandwidth) with EXIF stripped; (9) **VoiceOver accessibility labels** matching Watch arc standards (per W11c) — photo: `accessibilityLabel = "Photo of: " + extracted item names`; tap-to-expand: `accessibilityHint = "Tap to view full size"`; per-item delete: `accessibilityLabel = "Remove " + item name`; Confirm/Edit/Discard: clear action verbs. **F3c → B (block save with retry/type fallback) with seven pins**. Pins: (1) **`useMeals.editMeal(mealId, updates)` new API** — Firestore write + bumps `updatedAt` + increments counters atomically (transaction); (2) **Performance OK no throttle** — typical <10 edits/day per user, negligible Firestore cost; (3) **Macro recalc reuses existing `mealTotals.ts:sumMealTotals()`** — totals derived from items; meal-doc fields are mirrors; (4) **F1d `userEditedFields[]` interplay** — manual edits populate the array, F1c background refinement skips locked fields; same logic post-save as in-progress; (5) **Validation reused from create** — `foodValidation.ts` rules; reject invalid edits with same error UX; (6) **Offline edit queues via `offlineQueue.ts`** — existing pattern, F5d's LWW handles any conflict; (7) **Edit clears barcode `unitConfidence: 'low'` flag** (per F2 interaction) — user explicitly providing correct values; banner clears too. **AI-refinement badge stays as historical fact** — distinct from F1d's lock; badge = "this meal was refined by AI at some point," persists across edits. **F5b → B (last-modified + revision count, with two-counter split) with six pins**. A too sparse — no signal that meal was edited (matters for F1d interplay). C/D require sub-collection — overkill. B is right minimum. Pins: (1) **`updatedAt: serverTimestamp` field** on Meal doc — bumped on every write; (2) **TWO counters**: `revisionCount: number` (any write, internal/debug) + `userEditCount: number` (only manual edits via `editMeal()`, drives UI); (3) **"Edited" pill visible when `userEditCount > 0`** — AI refinements bump `revisionCount` but NOT `userEditCount` (user expects pill to mean THEY edited); (4) **Delete/restore (`deletedAt` toggle) does NOT bump either counter** — distinct signal from field-change; (5) **Support sees THAT meal was edited, not WHAT** — full per-field audit deferred to v2 via `mealRevisions/{mealId}/items/` sub-collection; document limitation in support runbook; (6) **Lazy migration via `updatedAt` presence signal** — reads without `updatedAt` get default at read time (`updatedAt = createdAt`, both counters = 0); writes after migration always include the fields; avoids recursive `mealSchemaVersion` introduction. **F5c → B (soft-delete with 24h restore) with eight pins**. A (no undo) hostile for accidental deletes. C/D require F5b-D audit history which we rejected. B is the standard Apple Photos pattern: delete → trash → auto-purge after 24h → user can restore in that window. Pins: (1) **`deletedAt: timestamp \| null` field** on Meal doc — set on soft-delete, `null` for active; (2) **Active-meals query filter**: `WHERE deletedAt == null` on the existing meal list query; (3) **Day totals are query-derived** from `deletedAt == null` meals — soft-delete + restore states automatically reflected; no special handling; (4) **Auto-purge from MOST RECENT `deletedAt`** — if user deletes/restores/deletes again, clock resets on each delete; restoration sets `deletedAt = null` and the 24h clock pauses; (5) **Inline "Meal deleted · [Undo]" toast** immediately after delete (auto-dismiss 5s) + **Settings → "Recently deleted meals" archive** for users who miss the toast; both surfaces are necessary; (6) **Settings list sorted by deletion time DESC** with meal name + macros + "deleted X minutes ago" + tap restore or hard-delete (with confirm); empty state: "No recently deleted meals"; (7) **`purgeSoftDeletedMeals` cron Cloud Function** runs hourly; uses Firestore transaction with `deletedAt < (now - 24h)` check at write time — handles restore-race safely (transaction sees `null` on restored doc and skips); (8) **Multi-device delete state LWW** per F5d (W4c rule); future bulk-delete UI uses same primitive; storage cost negligible (~10 docs steady state per power user). **F5d → A (LWW per W4c) with four pins**. B requires conflict-resolution UI Tropos doesn't have. C blocks edits which is hostile. D adds complexity for uncommon case. W4c's per-collection rule for meals (LWW by serverTimestamp + `clientMealId` dedupe) already specifies the answer. Pins: (1) **W4c rule applies as-is** — last-writer-wins by serverTimestamp; rare in practice (simultaneous same-meal edits across devices); (2) **No conflict UI in v1** — user re-edits to fix conflict via F5a free-form; (3) **Offline-edit-wins-over-newer-remote acknowledged as v1 limitation** — `serverTimestamp` assigned at sync time not original-edit time; offline edits queued for a day can overwrite newer remote edits on reconnect; mitigation via "this meal was edited on another device" notification deferred to v2; (4) **LWW future-proofs to multi-device Watch v2** — W4c rule applies to any device combination; future Watch + iPhone + iPad inherit same logic. **Critical implications:** (1) **`useMeals.editMeal(mealId, updates)` + `useMeals.restoreMeal(mealId)` new APIs**; (2) **Four new fields on Meal**: `updatedAt`, `revisionCount`, `userEditCount`, `deletedAt`; (3) **`Meal.userEditedFields[]`** (per F1d) interplay — manual edits via `editMeal` populate the array; (4) **Lazy migration** via `updatedAt`-presence signal (no recursive `mealSchemaVersion`); (5) **`purgeSoftDeletedMeals` cron CF** new hourly job; (6) **Trash UX**: inline toast + Settings archive; (7) **"Edited" pill component** (pencil icon + "Edited" label) on meal rows when `userEditCount > 0`; (8) **F2 `unitConfidence` clears on user edit**; (9) **F1c AI badge persistence** as historical fact across edits. **R1A intersection NOTE (PR #505 still in-flight)**: (a) **soft-deleted meals must be hard-deleted regardless of `deletedAt` status** on R1A's user-keyed sweep — R1A inventory should already cover the `meals/{uid}/` subtree but flag the `deletedAt`-marked meals explicitly; (b) **`purgeSoftDeletedMeals` cron CF must check user's `deletionStatus`** before purging — avoids racing with R1A's deletion executor on mid-deletion users; document the deletionStatus check in the CF implementation. **No Watch impact in v1** (W1a deferred Watch meal logging entirely); future Watch v2 meals inherit same F5d LWW. **No PR-L impact** (meal edits are per-user under existing W4c reconciliation per-collection rule). Fourth decision in the F (Food parser) arc — slot F4 (voice food input) reserved for future grilling.
