### Social arc (S1–)

Decisions on Tropos's social layer — crews data model, naming, privacy, invite security, future expansion. Numbered S1+ to keep separation from Q / W / RP / F arcs. Distinct concern: this arc focuses on what Tropos's social positioning IS (private friend groups, not Strava-clubs) and how the data model + access controls enforce that.

| #   | Decision                                                             |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| S1  | Crews / Groups data model & naming                                   | **Reference apps:** Strava — Clubs (large interest-based communities, 100+ members, public + searchable). Nike Run Club — Groups (small private friend groups, ~8-12 members typical). WhatsApp / iMessage — Groups (canonical private group pattern, no public discoverability). Discord — Servers (blends both but only because access control is sophisticated). **Pattern: most fitness apps pick ONE of "private friends" or "public discoverable community," not both.** Tropos's "calm + adaptive" positioning matches the private-friends model. **Context shift mid-grill: user removed launch-pressure constraint** ("happy to delay launch to improve") — this inverted S1a from B (keep `/groups/`) to A (rename to `/crews/` now while user base is small). **S1a → A (rename `/groups/` → `/crews/` Firestore collection) with four pins**. With launch pressure removed, pre-launch is the best moment to do the rename: small user cohort, minimal external tooling, easier rollback, sets clean precedent (data shape matches UX vocabulary forever after). Pins: (1) **`firestore.indexes.json` migration** in the rename PR — validate every indexed query continues to work on `/crews/`; pre-flight check before flipping the dual-write to read from `/crews/`; (2) **Force-update prompt for old clients per RP1c off-ramp** — after ≥4 weeks of dual-write + low divergence + min-supported-client-version bump, clients still writing to `/groups/` see a forced update; refusing to update orphans their data; accepted RP1c contract; (3) **Rollback playbook documented before migration starts** — runbook entries for disable-v2-client / revert-dual-write-CF / treat-`/groups/`-as-source-of-truth; roll-forward is default, rollback is safety net; (4) **Cross-system audit before migration starts** — sweep Stripe webhooks, BigQuery exports, internal admin tools, analytics dashboards for `groups` references; documented prerequisite for the migration PR. **S1b → A (delete orphaned `useGroups.ts`) with four pins**. `useGroups.ts` (145 lines) has zero callers in the codebase — all consumers use `useCrews.ts`, which wraps the same collection. Dead code = drift risk + reviewer confusion + bundle bloat. Pins: (1) **CLAUDE.md deprecation note prevents re-introduction** — "Crew/group data lives at `/crews/` (post-rename) wrapped by `useCrews`. Do NOT create a `useGroups` hook — historical orphan deleted in PR-XXX"; (2) **Pre-delete grep for `import.*Group.*from.*useGroups`** — if any callers exist, migrate them to `Crew` type from `useCrews` first; (3) **Delete associated test files in the same PR** (check `__tests__/useGroups*.test.ts` — likely none); (4) **Brief git log review in deletion PR description** — surface original commit message; if intent was forward-compat for a planned still-pending feature, hold the deletion until that feature lands. **S1c → A (small private friend groups only) with ten pins**. Tropos positioning is supportive personal fitness, not viral social network. Public discoverable Clubs (B) are a different product (Strava-style). One-model-for-both (C) requires sophisticated access controls + moderation that team scale doesn't justify. Two separate models (D) doubles engineering surface without clear demand. Pins: (1) **25-member hard cap per crew** enforced via Firestore security rule on `/crews/{crewId}/members/{userId}`; (2) **Invite-only via shareable link** — no public crew search endpoint; (3) **Ownership transfer to next-oldest member** (by `joinedAt`) when creator leaves; (4) **Auto-delete when all members leave** — cron Cloud Function cleanup (defer the CF to v2 if not built; rely on manual cleanup short-term); (5) **Crew-internal leaderboards are fine** (already partially built per `useCrews` `CrewLeaderboardEntry` interface) — just no public-facing crew discovery; (6) **Workplace / larger-group use cases deferred to a future `clubs` collection** — current 25-cap intentional; re-evaluate based on user request signal post-launch; (7) **Explicitly NO `isPublic` field on Crew documents** — privacy is _structural_ (invite-only links, no public search endpoint), not a flag; prevents accidental public-leak via misconfigured flag; (8) **Server-generated secure random invite tokens** (e.g., 32-char alphanumeric) stored in `/crews/{crewId}.inviteToken` — NOT the raw crew ID; creator can "rotate invite link" via UI to invalidate old shares; (9) **One-tap join via valid invite link, no approval required**; **member removal restricted to crew creator only** (matches existing `firestore.rules` pattern); (10) **`bannedUids: string[]` array on the crew doc** — creator can remove a member AND add their UID to bannedUids; banned UIDs can't re-join even with valid invite link; Firestore rule validates against this on join. **S1d → B (dual-write migration per RP1c pattern, now active) with six pins**. With S1a flipped to active rename, dual-write is the migration shape — consistent with RP1c's established v1 → v2 discipline. Pins: (1) **Top-down hierarchical migration order** — migrate `/groups/{id}` → `/crews/{id}` first; then for each migrated parent, migrate sub-collections (`/groups/{id}/members/{uid}` → `/crews/{id}/members/{uid}`); idempotent per RP3 (checkpoint per batch); (2) **Pre-migration sub-collection audit** — list all sub-collections under `/groups/` (likely `members/` + possibly others); each gets a migration step; documented in the migration PR description; (3) **Post-migration validation Cloud Function** — compares doc counts in `/groups/` vs `/crews/` by `crewId`; flags any mismatch; required gate before the off-ramp; mismatch → halt, investigate, fix, retry; (4) **Off-ramp flip mechanism** — at the moment of off-ramp (≥4 weeks <1% divergence per RP1c), dual-write CF flips to single-write `/crews/` only; new writes during dual-write existed in both, post-off-ramp only hit `/crews/`; (5) **`/groups/` preserved read-only for 8 weeks past deprecation** for forensic queries; then deleted; (6) **Data-export dual-collection-aware during the window** — exports query both `/groups/` and `/crews/`, dedupe by `crewId`; post-window, exports query `/crews/` only; coordinates with R1A's account-deletion-export work (PR #505). **Critical implications:** (1) **`groups` → `crews` migration PR is now active**, not deferred — significant new scope (~3-4 weeks engineering per RP-3 reference); (2) **Invite-link security model is first-class** — server-generated rotatable tokens + bannedUids array; new Cloud Function endpoints for token generation + rotation; (3) **`useCrews` hook updates** to read/write `/crews/` collection; the previously-planned "internal-vs-external naming" header comment is no longer needed since names align; (4) **Firestore security rules rename** `/groups/{crewId}` → `/crews/{crewId}` + 25-member cap enforcement + invite-token validation + bannedUids validation on join; (5) **Hard cap 25 members per crew** enforced at security rule + client UI levels; (6) **CLAUDE.md updates** — pin `crews` as canonical name across collection + hook + type + UI; pin no-isPublic structural privacy; pin invite-token security model; pin "do NOT create useGroups hook" deprecation note; (7) **`useGroups.ts` deletion PR** — small scope (~145 lines + any tests), zero functional impact, blocks nothing; can ship as part of the migration PR or standalone; (8) **Future `clubs` collection design** is deferred but anticipated — clean architectural exit if/when public Clubs become a product direction. **Side flag**: F2c was locked as "C-target-A-stopgap" partly under launch-pressure framing. With launch pressure removed, F2c may want revisiting — building C (Cloud Function cache + global share) directly is cleaner than the OFF-direct stopgap. Logged but not re-opened; user explicitly accepted the prior lock as sub-optimal-but-fine for that decision. **No Watch impact** (W7 routes notifications via APNs; Watch doesn't read crew data directly). **PR-L impact**: the migration reuses PR-L's reconciliation pattern but doesn't change PR-L's scope.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| S2  | Activity feed shape (useSocialFeed, useDiscoverFeed, kudos, follows) | **Reference apps:** Strava — feed = followers + clubs you've shared to; kudos by anyone who can see; discovery via "Local Heroes" / "Featured Athletes" (public layer Tropos lacks per S1). Nike Run Club — feed = followers + groups; kudos by anyone in group; no broad discover layer. Apple Fitness — sharing is opt-in friends-only; no discover; closest to Tropos's positioning. Strong / Hevy — workout sharing optional, follower-only. **Pattern: most fitness apps converge on "followers + shared-to-groups" for the feed**; public discovery exists only on apps with a viral-growth social layer. Tropos's S1 positioning sits closer to Apple Fitness — opt-in friends-only. Stress-tested across one pass; 17 pins. **S2a → A (followers + shared-to-crews union) with four pins**. Pure follows (B) ignores crews; pure crews (C) ignores follow connections; configurable (D) is over-engineered for v1. A: activity appears in feed if (you follow the author) OR (the author shared it to a crew you're in). Pins: (1) **Deduplicate by `activityId`** at feed-query time — single appearance regardless of how many visibility paths qualify; (2) **Denormalised `audienceUids: string[]` on each activity at save time** — union of (author's followers at save) + (members of each shared-to crew at save); single Firestore query `activities WHERE audienceUids CONTAINS myUid ORDER BY createdAt DESC` with composite index on `(audienceUids, createdAt)`; (3) **Save-time snapshot, no recompute on graph changes** — new followers don't backfill old activities (matches Twitter/Strava: see what's posted AFTER you follow); (4) **Crew-leave doesn't retroactively hide** — already-seen activities stay in feed; matches WhatsApp's leaving-group pattern. **S2b → C (`in_your_crew` + `friend_of_friend`) with four pins**. Pure `in_your_crew` (A) too sparse for new users; `recent_post` (B's current behaviour) meaningless without a public surface per S1; disable entirely (D) loses useful onboarding mechanic. C: 2-hop traversal from existing connections — privacy-preserving (no public layer required) and richer as network grows. Pins: (1) **Max 50 candidates per query, ranked by mutual-connections count** (people followed by most of YOUR follows rank higher); exclude already-followed, banned UIDs (cross-crew per S1c-pin-10), previously-rejected suggestions; (2) **User-facing copy opaque** ("Suggested" or "Friend of friend," NOT "via [name]") — prevents follow-graph leak; reason field stays server-side metadata for analytics; (3) **Fallback to `in_your_crew` only when user has 0 follows**; **if both empty (no crews, no follows) show onboarding CTA**: "Find a friend by invite link, or join a crew"; (4) **Cross-crew ban awareness** — if a user is in `bannedUids` of any crew you're in, exclude them from your discover feed regardless of other connections; per-crew bans are user-level signals that ripple across discover. **S2c → C (followers-only default + per-activity crew-share opt-in) with five pins**. Public-default (A) breaks S1's private positioning; crew-only default (B) too narrow (follows should see); per-activity picker (D) adds friction at save. C: default = visible to followers; crew-share is per-activity opt-in (checkbox at save time). Mirrors Apple Fitness friends-only-by-default + share-to-workout-group. Pins: (1) **Explicit `visibilityMode: 'private' \| 'followers' \| 'crews'` enum** on each activity — `private` sets `audienceUids: [authorId]` only; `followers` snapshots author's followers; `crews` snapshots followers ∪ members of shared-to crews. Default = `followers`; (2) **Per-activity escape to `private`** via save-screen toggle; **`crews` mode auto-set when user checks "Share to [Crew name]"** at save (records `sharedToCrewIds: string[]`); (3) **Edit-activity flow can remove crew shares post-save** — removes from feeds going forward but doesn't unreveal historical impressions (standard social-edit model); (4) **Empty audience case** (0 followers + 0 crews) = visible to author only via the self-feed query (which reads author's own activities independently of `audienceUids`); (5) **Schema migration backfills existing activities** (per RP4 conventions) — `audienceUids = author's follower snapshot at backfill time`, `visibilityMode = 'followers'`, `sharedToCrewIds = []`; users see existing feeds as before; **visibility badge shown only to author** on their own activities ("Shared with crews" or "Private" near timestamp); viewers infer from feed membership. **S2d → A (anyone who can see can kudos) with four pins**. Mutuals-only (B) is asymmetric and frustrating for one-way fan relationships. Crew-only (C) is too narrow. Per-activity configurable (D) adds friction without payoff. A: kudos gated by activity visibility, not crew membership. Pins: (1) **Kudos respects `audienceUids` only** — cross-crew bans don't affect kudos (separate feature: global per-user block deferred to v2); (2) **Rate-limit kudos at 50/hour per user** via `rateLimiter.js` with new `kudos` action key (existing transaction pattern); (3) **Un-kudos toggle** — same heart tap reverses; each toggle counts against the rate limit; (4) **Batched kudos notifications via W7 APNs routing** — first kudos = immediate ping; subsequent kudos within 1 hour aggregated ("X and 9 others kudos'd your run") via hourly Cloud Function aggregator. **Critical implications:** (1) **Three new fields on every activity**: `audienceUids: string[]` (audience snapshot), `visibilityMode: 'private' \| 'followers' \| 'crews'`, `sharedToCrewIds: string[]` (which crews shared to, used when `visibilityMode === 'crews'`); (2) **Composite Firestore index on `(audienceUids, createdAt)`** for the main feed query; (3) **`firestore.rules` for activities update**: read allowed when `request.auth.uid in resource.data.audienceUids` (replaces current per-follower / per-crew check); (4) **`socialApi.ts:suggestPeople()` rework** — replace `recent_post` reason with `friend_of_friend`; 2-hop traversal with ban-aware filtering; sort by mutual-connections count; bounded to 50 results; (5) **`useDiscoverFeed` rework** — handle empty-state onboarding CTA when 0 follows + 0 crews; (6) **`useSocialFeed` query change** — `audienceUids CONTAINS myUid` single read; per-card kudos + author-data already denormalised; (7) **Schema migration** backfills existing activities (audienceUids from author's follower list at backfill + visibilityMode 'followers' + sharedToCrewIds []); (8) **`rateLimiter.js`** gains `kudos` action key (50/hour cap); (9) **Cloud Function aggregator** for batched kudos notifications — hourly per author, sends digest if >1 kudos in window. **R1A intersection NOTE: account deletion (PR #505) is STILL IN-FLIGHT, not yet merged**. When R1A lands, it will need to: (a) remove the deleted user's UID from all `audienceUids` arrays containing it (cross-doc cleanup pattern at scale), and (b) remove their authored kudos/comments. This adds a new requirement on R1A's deletion executor scope — flag for the R1A author. Document this dependency in R1A's deletion inventory. **No Watch impact** (W7 routes notifications via APNs; Watch doesn't render social feeds). **PR-L impact**: activities continue under W4c's append-with-LWW-metadata rule; new `audienceUids` is metadata (LWW by serverTimestamp) per existing per-collection rules.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| S3  | Notifications policy for social events                               | **Reference apps:** Apple Fitness — minimal notifications, mostly inline, no separate notification center (matches Tropos's calm positioning). Strava — bell drawer with kudos batching, follow events default-on, paginated notification list. NRC — similar bell + per-event opt-ins. Calm / Headspace — calm-by-default, opt-in per category. **Pattern: viral-growth social apps (Strava, NRC) use bell drawer + default-on broad notifications; calm-positioning apps (Apple Fitness, Headspace) minimise the surface — inline only, opt-in per category.** Tropos's brand voice points to the second pattern. Stress-tested one pass; 12 pins. **S3a → D (calm-by-default category opt-ins) with four pins**. W7 reserved Watch-local triggers for in-run events only and routed everything else via APNs; social events follow the same calm-by-default philosophy. Default-on: kudos + comments (matches current implicit behaviour). Default-off: follows + crew-joins (opt-in via Settings). Always-on: `crew_owner_transfer` (genuine state change the user needs to know about — "you're now the creator of [Crew]"). Pins: (1) **No first-launch nudges to enable opt-in categories** — users discover follow/crew notifications in Settings naturally; first-week silence is correct for a non-viral product; (2) **No @mentions in v1** (defer to v2) — comment notifications fire on activity author only, no mention-mechanic; (3) **Skip self-notification when `sourceUid === targetUid`** — user commenting/kudosing their own activity doesn't trigger a notification; (4) **Ownership-transfer notification copy = "You're now the creator of [Crew] · Open"** — neutral, informative state-change, deep-links to crew settings; always-on category cannot be disabled (read-only "Always on" row in Settings). **S3b → B (batched per event-type) with four pins**. Real-time per-event (A) is the shame-ping pattern W7c rejected. Daily-digest-only (C) loses real-time engagement (kudos right after posting is the dopamine moment). Hybrid (D) over-engineers. B mirrors S2d's hourly kudos aggregator and extends the same pattern to comments + follows; crew events are rare enough to fire individually (no batching). Pins: (1) **Aggregator runs as a scheduled cron (hourly)**, not on-event — first-event-per-hour-per-type sends immediate; subsequent events queue for next aggregation window (one ping per hour max per type, anti-shame-ping pattern); (2) **Comments batched as "X and 2 others commented on your activity"** — single notification with author count; tap deep-links to activity with all comments visible; (3) **Follows use same hourly aggregator** — "X and 9 others followed you" notification; (4) **Single CF invocation per hour processes all users' pending notifications** (single-pass, batched Firestore reads) — cost ~$0.01/run × 24/day = ~$0.30/day, negligible. **S3c → D (no bell drawer, purely inline) with four pins**. Bell drawer (A/B/C) adds visual clutter, competes with calm-positioning, and re-implements what iOS Notification Center owns natively. Inline badges + contextual sheets provide the same info without a separate UI surface. Saves significant UI scope. Pins: (1) **Tap kudos count on activity card → kudos'rs sheet** (chronological list with authorName + photoURL) — inline archive without a bell; (2) **Profile page "Recent followers" section** (top 10 most-recent followers, paginated) — inline follow archive without a bell; (3) **Crew detail page "Recent activity" section** (joined / left events for that crew) — inline crew-events archive scoped to crew; (4) **OS notification-permission-denied one-time banner on Social tab** — "Enable notifications to see kudos and comments · Open Settings" with iOS Settings deep link; dismiss-once via localStorage flag; suppressed permanently after dismissal (Settings re-discovery only). **S3d → n/a** under S3c-D (no in-app bell drawer means no central read-state store needed; inline indicators use existing localStorage `lastSeen` pattern per surface). **Critical implications:** (1) **Single Cloud Function `socialNotificationsAggregator`** extends S2d's kudos batching to comments + follows + new event types; runs hourly via Cloud Scheduler; processes all users' pending notifications in one invocation; (2) **Three new notification types** in `notifications/{userId}/items/`: `'follow'`, `'crew_join'`, `'crew_owner_transfer'` (alongside existing `'comment'` and `'kudos'`); (3) **`notificationPreferences: { kudos: boolean, comments: boolean, follows: boolean, crewJoin: boolean }`** field added to user profile — `crew_owner_transfer` intentionally NOT in this map (always-on, can't be disabled); (4) **Settings page gains "Notifications" section** with per-category toggles plus a read-only "Always on" row for ownership-transfer; (5) **`useUnreadCount.ts` updates** to query `audienceUids CONTAINS myUid` (replaces stale `visibility` field query — blocked on S2 migration); (6) **`socialApi.ts` extensions**: new helpers `notifyOnFollow(targetUid)`, `notifyOnCrewJoin(crewId, joinerUid)`, `notifyOnCrewOwnerTransfer(crewId, newOwnerUid)`; existing comment-notification path routes through the aggregator now; (7) **Profile page** gains "Recent followers" section; (8) **Crew detail page** gains "Recent activity" section; (9) **Activity card** gains tap-kudos-count → kudos'rs sheet; (10) **One-time iOS permission banner** on Social tab when OS permission denied; (11) **No bell-drawer UI to build** — saves ~2-3 days of UI work + reduces brand-style friction; iOS Notification Center owns the bell natively (deep links open Tropos to relevant context). **R1A intersection NOTE**: account deletion (PR #505, still in-flight per S2's note) needs to add `notifications/{deletedUid}/items/` to the deletion inventory. Likely already covered by R1A's existing user-keyed sweep pattern (matches `users/{uid}/` subtree cleanup), but **flag explicitly** for the R1A author to confirm. **No Watch impact** (W7's APNs routing handles Watch delivery via Apple's wrist-raise + iPhone-locked logic; social notifications appear on Watch automatically when iOS routes them there). **PR-L impact**: notifications collection is per-user (`notifications/{uid}/items/`); no cross-device reconciliation conflicts; new helper functions follow standard append-only write patterns per W4c.
