| S4  | Block / report / moderation flows                                    | **Reference apps:** Strava — symmetric global blocks; report categories (harassment/spam/inappropriate); admin review (slow, manual). Apple Fitness — minimal moderation; closed-friends-only model means blocks rarely needed. Reddit — sophisticated tiered (auto-mods → community mods → admins); not relevant to Tropos's scale. Twitter/X — asymmetric blocks (widely disliked); aggressive auto-moderation. **Pattern: small-friends-network apps lean simple symmetric blocks + minimal moderation; viral apps need tiered automation.** Tropos's S1 small-private positioning maps to the first pattern. Existing infrastructure: `useBlockedUsers` hook with module-level cache (global symmetric blocks), `ReportModal.tsx` user-facing UI, `profanityFilter.js` CF (68 lines), `BlockAwareAvatar.tsx` UI, crew-level bans via `bannedUids` (S1c), admin queue shipped per commit dc7f83c. Stress-tested one pass; 18 pins. **S4a → D (both global blocks + per-crew bans, distinct intents) with five pins**. Pure global symmetric (A) loses creator authority over their crew. Asymmetric (B) is Twitter pattern users hate. Scoped (C) over-engineered. D preserves the current state: global blocks (user-controlled, symmetric, "I don't want this person anywhere") + per-crew bans (creator-controlled, scoped, "Remove from crew"). User-facing copy distinction: "Block" vs "Remove from crew" (the latter also adds to `bannedUids` per S1c). Pins: (1) **Blocked users replaced by "Blocked user" placeholder in crew member lists** — A knows the count is correct but doesn't see B's identity; (2) **Leaderboards exclude blocked-pairs in BOTH directions** — if A blocks B, neither appears in the other's leaderboard view (single-digit entries acceptable); (3) **Blocking does NOT auto-remove from any crew** — bans are crew-level, blocks are personal-level, separate intents; (4) **Mutual block redundant but harmless** — symmetric enforcement already covers both directions; no dedup needed; (5) **Block takes effect on next render** — feed/activity views filter on next state update; already-open detail screen shows "Reload to see updates" banner OR auto-reloads. **S4b → C (two-tier categories) with four pins**. Generic (A) gives admins nothing to triage. Fixed top-level (B) fine but two-tier provides better triage with minimal extra friction. Apple Store categories (D) overkill. Pins: (1) **Single-screen category + sub-reason picker** (not modal-stacked) — five top-level categories (Harassment / Spam / Inappropriate Content / Impersonation / Other) × 2-4 sub-reasons each; (2) **Admin can reclassify during review** — both `reporterCategory` + `reviewerCategory` stored for analytics (reveals common mismatches to improve picker); (3) **Reports merged by `targetContentId` in admin queue** — single entry per content with aggregated reporter list + category distribution; reduces noise, clearer severity signal; (4) **Freeform note max 500 chars** with profanity-filter redaction — if flagged, admin sees "[Note flagged · click to view]" by default (raw note expandable on click); protects admin reviewers from PII/threats in freeform field. **S4c → D (user chooses at report time) with four pins**. A (auto-hide always) doesn't let user pick. B (queue-only, nothing visible) feels broken. C (auto-hide + auto-block) too aggressive — Block is personal-level, opt-in required. D respects user intent. Pins: (1) **Three checkboxes**: Report (default-ON), Hide from feed (default-ON), Block author (default-OFF); reasoning — reporter is annoyed enough to hide; Block is heavier, requires explicit opt-in; (2) **Any combination valid** — Submit disabled only if all three unchecked; supports "just hide, don't tell admin" and "just block, no admin attention" cases; (3) **Block + Hide take effect immediately on Submit; Report queued for admin separately** — user-controlled vs admin-controlled actions have different timelines; (4) **Hide can be unchecked while Report is checked** — informant case where reporter wants Tropos to know but content doesn't directly bother them. **S4d → C (tiered automation + manual review) with five pins**. Pure manual (A) doesn't scale. B (auto-mod + manual edge cases) fine but misses high-severity protection. D (outsource) expensive overkill. C extends existing profanity filter as high-severity gate. Pins: (1) **Severity computed server-side on report submission** — profanity filter run against target content + category mapping; severity field set on `reports/{id}`; **never block content without ALSO queuing for review** — auto-hide is reversible safety mechanism; (2) **High-severity (slur/threat/explicit) auto-hides immediately** via `flagged: true` field on activity/comment + 48h manual review SLA; **low/medium severity queues for review only** with 7-day SLA; SLA breach = dashboard red alert (no user-facing change, no auto-escalation — admin staffing responsibility); (3) **`reports.reporterUid` NEVER shown to target user** (privacy + retaliation prevention); rate-limit reporting at 20/day per user via `rateLimiter.js` new `report` action key; (4) **`auto_hide_rate_per_day` dashboard anomaly detection** — alert if rate exceeds historical baseline by 3x (signals bad severity model); admin can bulk-unhide if false-positive cascade detected; (5) **`globalRestrictedUids` separate collection** for repeat offenders — restricted users CAN'T send kudos (rate-limit set to 0), can't comment on activities, can't share to crews, profile shows "Restricted user" badge; **three actioned reports = restricted**; **reversible after 30 days of clean behaviour** (admin-controlled lift); not a permanent ban, rehab pathway. **Critical implications:** (1) **`reports` Firestore collection** schema: `{ reporterUid, targetUid, targetContentType: 'activity' \| 'comment' \| 'profile', targetContentId, reporterCategory, reporterSubReason, reviewerCategory?, freeformNote?, createdAt, severity: 'high' \| 'medium' \| 'low', status: 'pending' \| 'reviewed' \| 'actioned' \| 'dismissed' }`; (2) **`flagged: true` field on activities/comments** when auto-hidden — flagged content hidden from all feeds except author's self-feed (so author isn't ghosted, sees "Under review" placeholder); (3) **`globalRestrictedUids` collection** schema: `{ uid, restrictedAt, restrictionEndsAt, lastActionedReport, strikes: number }`; (4) **`ReportModal.tsx` extension** for two-tier picker + three-checkbox submission + 500-char freeform note; (5) **Admin queue UI** (already shipped per dc7f83c) extends to show: severity, auto-hide status, reviewer assignment, merged-by-content reporter list, reclassification field, redacted freeform notes (click to expand); (6) **`rateLimiter.js`** gains `report` action key (20/day cap); (7) **Severity computation Cloud Function** runs profanity-filter against target content on report submission + maps to severity tier; sets `flagged: true` on the target document if severity = high; writes to admin queue regardless; (8) **`globalRestrictedUids` enforcement** at write time — Cloud Functions check this collection before accepting kudos/comment/share-to-crew operations; restricted users get `permission-denied` error with user-friendly copy ("Your account is restricted · Contact support"); (9) **Settings page "Privacy & Safety" section** lists blocked users + "Why am I restricted?" link (for restricted users only); (10) **Auto-hide UX** shows "This content is under review" placeholder; author sees same placeholder on self-feed so they know it's been hit, but no separate notification (avoids drawing attention to flagged content). **R1A intersection NOTE (PR #505 still in-flight)**: account deletion needs to handle: (a) **preserve reports for forensic admin trail** but anonymise `reporterUid` to `__deleted__` (target UID stays for content-context); (b) **`blockedUids` cross-doc cleanup** — remove deleted user from all `blockedUids` arrays on other users' profiles (same pattern as S2's audienceUids); (c) **`bannedUids` preserved as historical signal** — don't unban dead-user UIDs (there might be stale content references). Add to R1A inventory. **No Watch impact** (W7 APNs routing; moderation actions don't fire user-visible Watch notifications). **PR-L impact**: `reports` collection follows W4c's append-only-with-metadata-LWW pattern; `flagged` field on activities/comments is metadata LWW. |
| S5  | Profile shape & privacy controls                                     | **Reference apps:** Strava — public-by-default profiles, real names encouraged, profile search exists, aggregate stats visible to anyone. Apple Fitness — friends-only profiles, no search, closed-friends-only model (closest to Tropos's positioning). Nike Run Club — real names + photo verification, profile search by name. Hevy — per-user profile visibility (public or followers-only), no search. **Pattern: calm-positioning apps (Apple Fitness) restrict profile visibility + skip search; viral apps (Strava, NRC) open profiles + offer search.** Tropos's S1–S4 positioning follows Apple Fitness. Existing infra: `UserProfile` modular interfaces in `auth.tsx`; `users/{uid}/public/profile` doc with explicit field allow-list (displayName, photoURL); `PrivacySection.tsx` exposes `defaultVisibility` for activities (related to S2's visibilityMode). Stress-tested one pass; 17 pins. **S5a → B (two-layer: basic identity broad, stats followers-only) with four pins**. Pure public (A) breaks S1's private positioning. Three-tier (C) introduces confusing "private" state where user can't see themselves. Per-section configurable (D) over-engineered. B is the right model: basic identity (displayName + photoURL + handle + badges) broadly visible to anyone with profile URL; stats + activity history followers-only by default with opt-in toggle (per S5b). Pins: (1) **"Broadly visible" = anyone with the profile URL** — discovery happens via interactions (kudos, follow, crew), explicit share, or friend-of-friend (S2b); no public directory; (2) **Profile page's "recent activities" section filters by viewer's S2 `audienceUids` check** — non-followers see no activities even on profile page; same logic as feed; (3) **Profile views require authentication** — redirect to sign-in if unauthenticated; aligns with no-anonymous-auth pin (S1b/F2b); (4) **Blocked symmetric returns 404 not 403** — if requester is in target's `blockedUids` OR target is in requester's `blockedUids`, return "Profile not found" (gives no information; matches S4's reporter-privacy pattern). **S5b → B + C-opt-in (stats publicly toggleable) with four pins**. Minimal (A) too sparse — badges are earned achievements, showing them is part of motivation. Always-comprehensive (C) too open by default. Pro-tier-only (D) creates class system inconsistent with Tropos's calm voice. B as default + C as opt-in respects user choice. Pins: (1) **Single "Show my totals" switch covers all three stats** (totalKm + totalRuns + currentStreak) — single mental model, per-stat granularity over-engineered; (2) **Stats updated daily via existing `dailyPerformanceRefresh` Cloud Function** (02:10 UTC schedule) + immediate one-time refresh on `showStats` toggle change; (3) **Badges always visible in public profile doc** — achievements aren't metrics, different category; updates whenever new badge earned; (4) **Stats hidden until `totalRuns >= 5`** — avoid embarrassing-low-numbers UX; below threshold show "Your totals will show once you've logged 5 runs" copy in Settings. **S5c → A (no profile search) with four pins**. S1's positioning (no public crew search) applies symmetrically to profiles. Search (B/C) reintroduces the public-discoverability surface Tropos's positioning rejects. Opt-in directory (D) is the slowest slope to a Strava-style discovery layer — premature given v1 user base. A: invite-link sharing is primary discovery + friend-of-friend (S2b 2-hop). Pins: (1) **Settings → "My profile link"** with copy-to-clipboard + iOS share sheet integration; URL format `tropos.app/u/{handle}`; (2) **Handle changes redirect old → new for 90 days** via new `handleRedirects/{oldHandle}` Firestore collection with `{oldHandle, newUid, expiresAt}`; after 90 days, old handle frees for reuse; (3) **Inline handle availability check** in Settings on edit; suggestions on collision ("sarah-runner", "sarah-2"); restrictions: a-z0-9- characters only, 3-30 char length; (4) **Public profiles `noindex` by default** (robots.txt + meta tag) + **opt-IN via Settings → "Allow my profile to appear in search engines"** toggle (default OFF); most users stay private; SEO is opt-in. **S5d → B (anonymity allowed) + reserved handles with five pins**. Real names (A) feels heavy for fitness-journey product. Required verification (C) creates friction. B matches Tropos's calm voice: any displayName allowed, photo optional, "Athlete" placeholder fine. **displayName uniqueness NOT required** (multiple users can share "Sarah"); handle is unique. Pins: (1) **`displayName` freely changeable, no rate limit** — common for fitness apps; users like seasonal mottos; **`handle` constrained** (uniqueness via Firestore transaction; 90-day redirect on change per S5c); (2) **`profanityFilter.js` on displayName set** — if flagged, save fails with "This name isn't allowed · Try something else" copy; server-side enforced via Cloud Function; (3) **Unicode allowed (international names + emoji) but cap at 30 chars + strip zero-width / RTL-override chars** — anti-spoofing (prevents homograph attacks like the "Pаypal" Cyrillic-a spoof); server-side normalisation on save; (4) **Reserved handle list in `functions/reservedHandles.js`** as a constant — includes: `tropos`, `admin`, `support`, `official`, `help`, `mod`, `moderator`, `owner`, `system`; server-side enforcement on profile create + update; extendable; (5) **Reserved check applies to BOTH `displayName.toLowerCase().startsWith()` AND `handle.toLowerCase().startsWith()`** — prevents impersonation regardless of which field is set ("Tropos Support" as displayName blocked even if handle is "sarah"). **Critical implications:** (1) **`handle` field** on user profile with uniqueness enforcement via Firestore transaction (existing rateLimiter-pattern); (2) **`handleRedirects/{oldHandle}` Firestore collection** for 90-day redirect window on handle changes; (3) **`profilePrivacy: { showStats: boolean, allowSearchEngines: boolean }`** field on user profile (defaults: both `false`); (4) **`functions/reservedHandles.js`** Cloud Function module — server-side reserved list applied to both displayName + handle prefix checks; (5) **`users/{uid}/public/profile` doc schema update**: always-included = `displayName`, `photoURL`, `badges`, `handle`; conditionally-included (showStats=true AND totalRuns≥5) = `totalKm`, `totalRuns`, `currentStreak`; never-included = real name (if separate from displayName), email, fitness metrics (weight, height), private goals; (6) **Firestore rules update**: profile reads filter by symmetric blocked check (404 on either-side-blocks); (7) **`noindex` headers** on profile page routes by default; meta `<robots>` tag swaps based on `allowSearchEngines` field; (8) **Unicode normalisation on displayName save** — strip zero-width + RTL-override chars (security); (9) **`dailyPerformanceRefresh` Cloud Function extension** — also writes stats to public profile doc when `showStats=true` (existing CF, additional output); (10) **Settings UI extensions**: "My profile link" with copy + share sheet; "Show my totals" toggle; "Allow my profile to appear in search engines" toggle; inline handle-availability check on handle edit. **R1A intersection NOTE (PR #505 still in-flight)**: account deletion **frees the handle for reuse only after 90 days** (impersonation prevention — prevents an attacker from claiming a recently-deleted user's handle); existing `users/{uid}/public/profile` cleanup likely already in R1A inventory but **flag the 90-day handle hold as a new R1A requirement**. Plus `handleRedirects/{handle}` entries authored by the deleted user should also be cleaned up. **No Watch impact** (profile is iPhone-only; Watch doesn't render profile pages). **No PR-L impact** (profile doc is per-user, no cross-device reconciliation conflicts). Fifth decision in the S (Social) arc.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### Performance engine arc (P1–)

Decisions on Tropos's adaptive scoring engine — performance index weighting, pace tracking maturation, recovery score sourcing (proxy vs HRV/sleep), and how the engine couples to training-load suggestions. Numbered P1+ to keep separation from Q / W / RP / F / S arcs. Distinct concern: this arc focuses on the "adaptive" half of Tropos's "calm-adaptive" positioning — how the engine learns and feeds back into the user's plan.

| #   | Decision                                      |
| --- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| P1  | Performance engine tuning + adaptive coupling | **Reference apps:** Strava — Fitness/Freshness/Form (CTL/ATL/TSB) scores; pure observational; no auto-adjustment. Garmin Connect — VO2 Max, Training Status, Recovery Time; uses HRV when available; auto-suggests deload via "Training Suggestions." Whoop — strain + recovery scores; subscription-only; primary value-prop; mandatory HRV via wearable. TrainingPeaks — TSS-based; PMC chart observational; coach manually adjusts. **Pattern: scoring engines converge on observational + opt-in adaptive recommendations.** Tropos's current shape sits between Strava (observational only) and Garmin Connect (auto-suggests). Existing infra: `performanceEngine.ts` (392 lines), `performanceTypes.ts` (131 lines), `functions/performanceEngine.js` (524 lines); `PI_WEIGHTS = { load: 0.65, recovery: 0.25, adherence: 0.10 }`; `liftInLoad / runInLoad = 0.5 / 0.5`; `runPaceAdjustmentPct: 0` placeholder; `deloadRecommended: boolean` field exists; weekly rollup (Sun 23:15 UTC) + daily refresh (02:10 UTC) Cloud Functions. Stress-tested one pass; 16 pins. **P1a → B (telemetry-driven rebalance with operationalised triggers) with four pins**. Hardcoded forever (A) ignores improvement signal. User-configurable (C) over-engineered — users don't understand training metrics intuitively. A/B testing (D) requires infrastructure Tropos doesn't have. B is right but needs concrete triggers. Pins: (1) **Rebalance triggers**: rebalance when EITHER (i) ≥10% of `deloadRecommended: true` weeks are dismissed by users over a 30-day rolling window, OR (ii) `confidence: 'low'` for >40% of weekly rollups over a 30-day window; **rebalance is a quarterly review meeting** backed by the 30-day dashboard, not auto-tune; new `PI_WEIGHTS` ship via constant update + redeploy, no live config / no per-user override; (2) **Dismissal is signal not verdict** — triggers manual review where engineering investigates context; some users dismiss because they want to push through, not because the call was wrong; (3) **Rebalance proposals require follow-up signals** — subsequent week's actual performance (injury reports, voluntary volume drops post-dismissal) + user feedback channel ("this deload suggestion was wrong" via Settings → Feedback); dismissal alone isn't enough, the proposal needs ground-truth evidence; (4) **Cohort stratification by user tenure** — new-user (<8 weeks since signup) data weighted less heavily than established users' (≥8 weeks) data; quarterly dashboard breaks out both cohorts. **P1b → A (Watch v1 ship trigger, but DECOUPLED — pace data is iPhone-available today) with four pins**. The placeholder isn't waiting on pace data (iPhone GPS already produces it via `useGPS`) — it's waiting on the adjustment-vs-baseline computation logic to be built. So implementation is iPhone-implementable today, gated on engineering capacity rather than Watch ship. Pins: (1) **New `paceAdjustmentScore.ts` module** decoupled from Watch v1 — reads pace from existing run docs; populates `runPaceAdjustmentPct` field; (2) **Median (not mean) of last N runs in similar distance bucket** — outlier-resistant; single bad-GPS run doesn't skew the average; (3) **Distance bucketing**: `{≤5km, 5-12km, 12-25km, >25km}` — each bucket maintains its own median baseline; weekly aggregate weighted by run count per bucket; (4) **Rollout trigger**: feature-flagged validation cohort first; promote to all users when ≥50 users have ≥8 weeks of run history with pace data (gives meaningful baseline sample); below this threshold, `runPaceAdjustmentPct` stays 0 for everyone. **P1c → D (HealthKit opt-in toggle with proxy fallback) with four pins**. A (stay proxy forever) leaves signal on the table — Tropos's adaptive positioning benefits from HRV when available. B (HealthKit upfront) is friction; many users won't grant. C (Pro-only HRV) gates a core motivation feature behind paywall — recovery insights are too central to Tropos's positioning to Pro-gate. D respects user choice. Pins: (1) **Revocation graceful** — if user revokes HealthKit at OS level, app stops writing `recoveryScores/{uid}/{date}` documents; recovery score falls back to proxy-based for subsequent weeks; historical scores preserved as-is; one-time toast on next session "Apple Health access revoked · Using estimated recovery"; (2) **Watch HRV preferred + iPhone bedtime fallback** — if user has Apple Watch HRV data, use it; else use iPhone bedtime sleep-tracking data; if neither even with toggle enabled, log `recovery_data_unavailable_after_optin` telemetry + show tip "For HRV-based recovery, pair an Apple Watch"; (3) **Privacy invariant**: `recoveryScores/{uid}/{date}` stores derived SCORE (0-100) only, **NEVER raw HRV/sleep values** — computation happens client-side; only the score lands in Firestore; Cloud Function reads the score not the biometrics; pin in `docs/privacy.md`; (4) **Android equivalent deferred to v2** — for v1, HealthKit toggle is iOS-only; Android users always use proxy-based recovery; Settings copy: "Use Apple Health for better recovery scores (iOS only)"; future v2 ports to Google Health Connect with the same opt-in pattern. **P1d → C (suggest-only adaptive with apply-tap-through) with four pins**. Observational only (A) wastes the engine's predictive value. Auto-coupling (B/D) is paternalistic — users have plans and shouldn't have them changed without consent. C: PI surfaces "Deload recommended this week" as actionable banner on Programme page when `deloadRecommended: true` fires; user taps "Apply deload" → runScheduler/programEngine adjusts; tap "Not now" dismisses for the current week (fires telemetry per P1a). Pins: (1) **Deload mechanics defined** — drop one set per exercise (lift, same rule as W10 / Q10 race-taper) + reduce long run volume by 25% (run); **duration = 1 week by default; 2 weeks if `deloadRecommended` two weeks in a row** (cumulative fatigue signal); (2) **Race-taper exclusivity guard** — deload-suggest banner suppressed when `programState.runPlan.phase === 'taper'` (taper IS the deload; no double-deload); Programme page UI handles this exclusivity; (3) **Dismissal per-week re-evaluable** — dismissal is per current `weekKey` only; next week's rollup re-evaluates `deloadRecommended` independently; if still true, banner re-fires; dismissal-rate tracked via P1a telemetry doesn't suppress future banners across weeks; (4) **Reversible apply via `programState.preDeloadSnapshot`** — Programme page shows "Deload active · Restore normal plan" option for the affected weeks; restore reverts scheduler/program changes (original schedule restored from snapshot); snapshot cleared after deload duration ends. **Critical implications:** (1) **`PI_WEIGHTS` stays hardcoded constants** — change requires engineering rebalance per P1a triggers (no per-user override); (2) **Two new telemetry events for P1a triggers**: `pi_deload_recommendation_dismissed` (per-dismissal) + `pi_low_confidence_week` (from weekly rollup CF when `confidence === 'low'`); 30-day rolling rebalance dashboard computes rates with alerts at ≥10% dismissal OR >40% low-confidence; (3) **`paceAdjustmentScore.ts` module** new scope — iPhone-implementable today, decoupled from Watch v1 ship; computes median-per-bucket adjustment; (4) **`recoveryScores/{uid}/{date}` collection** stores derived score (0-100) only, NEVER raw biometric data; client-side HealthKit query → score computation → Firestore write; (5) **`programState.preDeloadSnapshot` field** captures pre-deload schedule for reversibility; cleared when deload duration ends; (6) **Race-taper exclusivity** — Programme page UI suppresses deload banner when `phase === 'taper'`; (7) **Cumulative deload duration logic** — second-consecutive-week `deloadRecommended` → 2-week deload instead of 1-week; (8) **HealthKit availability tip** when toggle enabled but no HRV source — "For HRV-based recovery, pair an Apple Watch"; (9) **`docs/privacy.md` update** — pin "raw HRV/sleep never persisted server-side; only derived scores stored" invariant; (10) **Settings UI extensions**: "Use Apple Health for better recovery scores" toggle (iOS only); "Feedback: this deload suggestion was wrong" link for the manual-feedback channel feeding P1a rebalance proposals. **R1A intersection NOTE (PR #505 still in-flight)**: account deletion needs to handle: (a) **`recoveryScores/{uid}/` cleanup** — new collection added to R1A inventory; (b) `performanceWeeks/{uid}/` likely already in R1A's existing user-keyed sweep but flag explicitly; (c) `programState.preDeloadSnapshot` field is stored within `programState/current` doc (covered by R1A's user-keyed programState sweep). **No Watch impact in v1** — Watch surfaces deload banner via W8a complication state machine, gaining a new "deload week" state (added later as P1d rolls out); Watch doesn't query HealthKit for recovery data (W11b's HealthKit JIT is for run-save only). **No PR-L impact** (`performanceDoc`, `recoveryScores`, `preDeloadSnapshot` are all per-user; no cross-device reconciliation conflicts). First decision in the P (Performance engine) arc.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| P2  | Performance feedback UX                       | **Reference apps:** Strava — CTL/ATL/TSB chart in dedicated section, no Home prominence, tap-to-drill-in. Garmin Connect — Training Status on Home + watch face widget + drill-in to recovery time. Whoop — strain + recovery scores prominent on Home + daily insight narrative; subscription-required. Apple Activity — Move/Exercise/Stand rings on Home + Watch face complications + iOS Widget. Canonical multi-surface pattern. **Pattern: apps with adaptive-coaching value prop surface scores prominently across surfaces.** Tropos's PI currently buried in Analytics tab; should follow Apple Activity / Garmin pattern. Existing infra: `PerformanceTab.tsx` in Analytics with PIGauge component + 8-week trend chart + sub-score visibility; `usePerformanceWeeks(12)` hook; `PerformanceIndexChart.tsx`. Stress-tested THREE passes; 34 pins total. **P2a → D (Home card + Analytics + iOS Widget) with ten pins**. PI is core to Tropos's "calm-adaptive" positioning. Burying in Analytics (A) means users rarely see it — defeats the value prop. Notification-only (C) loses passive visibility. B (Home + Analytics) is good but iOS Widget extension to home + lock screen is meaningful delight surface matching Apple Activity / Garmin. D is the right multi-surface answer. Pins: (1) **Home PI card uses compact tile pattern** (`rounded-xl`, `bg-muted`, `p-3`) — NOT a hero card; sized like Weight/Steps tiles; 2-col grid placement; doesn't compete with Health Score / Water hero cards; (2) **Empty state copy** for users with no `performanceDoc` yet: "Log a few sessions this week to see your Performance Index" + placeholder gauge with `—`; (3) **Widget refresh aligned with rollup cadence** — 02:30 UTC daily (post-`dailyPerformanceRefresh`) + 23:30 UTC Sunday (post-`weeklyPerformanceRollup`); avoids unnecessary refreshes when data hasn't changed; (4) **Multi-device widget inconsistency acceptable** per W19 pattern — `WidgetCenter.shared.reloadAllTimelines()` triggers on app foreground; brief lag tolerated; (5) **PI is personal-metric not social-dependent** — card always visible when `performanceDoc` exists; independent of follows/crews; (6) **Two widget families**: medium widget for home screen (PI + delta + 1-line insight) + circular complication for lock screen (PI number only); lock-screen variant is glanceable-on-wake; (7) **PI tile placement as peer to Steps/Weight metric tiles** in 2-col grid below action pills; structural pin, exact placement is design decision; (8) **"Updated [time]" caption + first-launch tip** "PI updates daily after midnight" — sets expectation about daily-refresh lag without surprise; (9) **Widget bundle minimal** — renders PI number + delta from `performanceDoc` snapshot only; no charts, no images, no large data structures; ~30MB iOS Widget memory budget respected; reuses `tropos-shared` compact PI types per W7 contract; (10) **Widget configuration deferred to v2** — v1 ships fixed layout; reduces scope. **P2b → C (per-sub-score commentary) with ten pins**. Number+gauge only (A) is sparse. Single insight (B) is fine but per-sub-score is more actionable — user knows whether to ease volume, take recovery, or improve adherence. AI Gemini-generated (D) is expensive (every weekly rollup → Gemini call) and sends training data to AI provider — privacy concern. C uses deterministic templates: on-device, free, privacy-preserving. Pins: (1) **`performanceInsights.ts` new template module** — template-based narrative generation per sub-score, deterministic, score-band-keyed; extends pattern from existing `nutritionInsights.ts`; (2) **3-5 template variants per score band** with deterministic hash selection from `(uid + weekKey + scoreBand)` — same week always shows same insight (consistent on re-views); different weeks rotate naturally; (3) **Tone is observational + actionable, never judgmental** — templates avoid "you failed" / "great job!" extremes; examples documented in style-guide comment in `performanceInsights.ts` for future contributors; (4) **First-week + <4-weeks baseline-establishing copy** — "First week logged — your baseline is forming. Keep going to see trends." All three sub-scores show this until ≥4 weeks of data; (5) **Deload-week-specific copy keyed on `loadBand === 'deload'`** — "Deload week — load intentionally lower. Recovery metrics should improve." Aligns with P1d's deload-recommendation flow; (6) **Home card shows lowest-sub-score insight only** (compact tile constraint) — surfaces the sub-score most needing attention; full per-sub-score breakdown on Analytics tab; (7) **Templates as PR-reviewed constants** in `performanceInsights.ts` — no user-generated content; lint + PR review catches issues; adding template requires code change not config; (8) **A/B testing infrastructure deferred to v2** (consistent with P1a's no-A/B-infra position); ship one template set v1, iterate based on telemetry; (9) **English-only in v1** (consistent with A1/F1/F4 i18n deferrals); localization infrastructure deferred to v2 as single coordinated effort across the app; (10) **Score band thresholds documented**: `[0-39 low / 40-69 medium / 70-100 high]` inclusive; consistent across load, recovery, adherence sub-scores; insight TEXT not persisted — only scores; historical weeks regenerate insight text against CURRENT template set on each render (narrative is interpretive, not historical record). **P2c → C (tap PI → expanded breakdown) with eight pins**. Hidden (A) hides too much. Always-numbers (B) exposes detail without context. Always-cards (D) too dense for small Home surface. C is progressive disclosure — PI is glanceable signal on Home/Widget; tap reveals breakdown for users wanting detail. Pins: (1) **Whole card is the tap target** (`<button>` wrapping contents) — matches Tropos's pressable-card convention from StackedCTACards; (2) **Tap navigates to existing Analytics tab → PerformanceTab section** with programmatic scroll to per-sub-score breakdown anchor; reuses existing surface; (3) **Standard navigation stack for back** — back returns to Home with Home card in scroll position; iOS back-gesture works; (4) **iOS Widget tap deep-links directly to Analytics** (skips Home) per Apple's WidgetKit deep-link pattern — widget is the "I want to see this NOW" surface; (5) **Widget tap respects auth-required flow** — opens app; if signed out, normal Login screen first, then Analytics on successful auth; standard iOS auth-required-deep-link pattern; (6) **Deep link uses URL fragment `/analytics#performance`** — React Router fragment-aware; auto-scrolls/selects PerformanceTab; (7) **Sub-score card tap reveals INLINE expansion within PerformanceTab** (NOT a new screen) — chevron-down accordion pattern reveals sparkline + insight history; matches iOS settings-style; (8) **Active-run state preempts widget tap routing** — if user is mid-active-run, app brings them to Run screen instead of Analytics; existing Run state machine already prioritises active-run routing; workout uninterrupted. **P2d → B (vs last week + 12-week rolling average) with eight pins**. Last week only (A) is current but missing context. Personal best (C) is motivation-y but easily demoralising — PB was 6 months ago when peaking; current 50%-of-PB feels like failure. Cohort comparison (D) is viral-app feature inconsistent with Tropos's calm positioning + raises privacy concerns. B: self-comparison via 12-week rolling average — Tropos competes against past-you, not other users (matches Apple Activity over Strava). Pins: (1) **Available-weeks-up-to-12 rolling average** — user with 5 weeks shows 5-week average; tooltip "Average over your last 12 weeks (or fewer if newer)" — honest about sample size; (2) **Positive delta uses success-green** (#4DB872); **negative delta uses muted-foreground** (NOT red — calm positioning, decline isn't framed as failure); zero shown as `—` no color; (3) **Average computed only from weeks with `confidence >= 'medium'`** — inactive weeks excluded; tooltip "Average over your last 12 active weeks"; honest representation for return-from-break users; (4) **Home card stays simple** (PI + delta only, no average) — average context surfaces only on Analytics where users seek deeper analysis; (5) **Dashed muted-gray average line vs solid colored PI series** on Analytics chart — different line styles distinguish visually; standard chart pattern; (6) **Visual hierarchy on Analytics**: PI number large+bold (headline), delta arrow+value medium, "Average X over 12 weeks" small caption below (tertiary); average is context not headline; (7) **Each sub-score card shows 8-week sparkline** (reuses Recharts existing pattern from `PerformanceIndexChart.tsx`) — helps spot trends per sub-score independently of overall PI trend; (8) **Declines >10 points week-over-week surface contextual diagnostic insight** "PI dropped by X — check your load and recovery scores" — replaces default lowest-sub-score insight when `delta < -10`; helps user diagnose dip without alarming small fluctuations. **Critical implications:** (1) **Home PI card component** new — compact tile with PI gauge + delta arrow + insight one-liner; taps to Analytics; (2) **iOS Widget WidgetKit two families** — medium for home screen + circular complication for lock screen; both consume `performanceDoc` via shared snapshot; (3) **`performanceInsights.ts` new lib module** — template-based deterministic narrative generation per sub-score, on-device, privacy-preserving; (4) **`PIBreakdownView` component** new on Analytics tab — three sub-score cards (load, recovery, adherence) with score + sub-insight + 8-week sparkline + inline expansion; (5) **`PerformanceTab.tsx` extension** — gains per-sub-score insight cards + 12-week rolling average dashed line on trend chart; (6) **No Gemini for performance insights** (privacy + cost) — insights are deterministic template-based; (7) **No cohort comparison** — anonymous benchmarking deferred indefinitely (positioning concern not just v2 timing); (8) **No personal-best comparison v1** — risks demoralising users coming back from injury / lifestyle change; re-evaluate with telemetry; (9) **Telemetry events**: `pi_card_viewed` (Home), `pi_card_tapped` (drill to Analytics), `pi_widget_added` (iOS Widget add); informs v2 redesign decisions; (10) **`tropos-shared` package extends `TodayRunSnapshot` with PI fields** per W7 contract — iOS Widget + Watch Today screen + iPhone Home card all consume same compact PI types. **R1A intersection**: no new collections from P2; existing `performanceWeeks` / `performanceDoc` cleanup already in R1A inventory per P1. **No PR-L impact** (performance docs per-user; no cross-device reconciliation). **Watch impact**: P2's iOS Widget is the wrist-equivalent of W19's Smart Stack widget — both consume same `performanceDoc` data; Watch gains "Deload week" state per P1d + W19 when P1d rolls out. Second decision in the P (Performance engine) arc. |

### Auth & onboarding arc (A1–)

Decisions on Tropos's authentication providers, onboarding flow length, re-authentication policy for destructive actions, and the iPhone-side sign-out experience. Numbered A1+ to keep separation from Q / W / RP / F / S / P arcs. Connects to W11 (Watch onboarding), S1b/F2b (no anonymous auth), R1A's `assertRecentAuth` (PR #505), W12d (Watch sign-out pattern).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
