| A1  | Auth & onboarding flow                       | **Reference apps:** Strava — 3 providers (Email/Google/Apple); ~5-step onboarding; FaceID for delete. Apple Fitness — Apple Sign-In only (locked to Apple ecosystem). Nike Run Club — Email + Apple + Google; 7-step onboarding; password for sensitive actions. Hevy / Strong — Email + Apple + Google; 4-step onboarding; password for delete. **Pattern: fitness apps converge on 3 providers + 4-7 step onboarding + password/FaceID for destructive actions.** Tropos's existing 13-step onboarding is on the heavy side relative to peers. Existing infra: `signIn / signUp / signInWithGoogle / signInWithApple` in `auth.tsx`; 13-step `Onboarding.tsx`; `onboardingComplete: true` flag; R1A's `accountDeletionAuth.js` with `checkRecentAuth` 300s threshold. Stress-tested across two passes; 24 pins total. **A1a → A (all three providers equal, iOS ordering Apple/Email/Google) with six pins**. Apple's App Store guideline 4.8 requires Sign in with Apple as an option if you offer third-party sign-in; Tropos already complies. Ordering: Apple top (native FaceID one-tap on iOS), Email middle (universal), Google bottom. Pins: (1) **Feature-detect `window.AppleID?.auth` on Login page load** — if unavailable on web (e.g., Firefox), hide the Apple button + show tip "Apple Sign-In not available on this browser"; iOS native plugin always works; (2) **Respect Firebase Auth's one-account-per-email model** — collision on email = surface `auth/account-exists-with-different-credential` link-Apple-to-Email flow; (3) **Capture Apple displayName + email IMMEDIATELY on first sign-in** to user profile (Apple's API only returns these on first sign-up; subsequent sign-ins return userIdentifier only — never overwrite to undefined); (4) **Hide-my-email relay supported as-is** — users wanting a different email use Settings → "Change email" (re-prompts auth + verification); account recovery for hide-my-email users requires Apple ID itself (document for support); (5) **Google One Tap deferred to v2** — v1 uses standard `signInWithGoogle`; (6) **Re-auth dialog surfaces current email for OAuth multi-account safety** ("Confirm sign-in for jane@example.com"); user's escape hatch is Google's / Apple's account chooser. **A1b → C (all 13 steps with Skip + sensible defaults) with seven pins**. Mandatory 13 (A) is heavy. Reduce to 5-6 (B) loses personalisation Tropos's adaptive engine depends on (recovery durations per Q10, race goal logic, body-metric-driven TDEE). Progressive disclosure (D) is the better UX long-term but requires complex re-prompt logic. C keeps the rich data + a Skip path. Pins: (1) **Per-step defaults pinned**: displayName = `Athlete-${randomHex(4)}` (e.g., "Athlete-3a7f"); age = 30; gender = "prefer not to say"; body metrics = empty; primary goal = "general fitness"; experience = "intermediate"; days/week = 3; equipment = "full gym"; preferred split = "full body"; run frequency = "occasional"; injuries = none; (2) **Contextual tips banner system** for skipped data ("Add body metrics in Settings for personalised calorie targets" / "Set a race goal to unlock taper week logic") — small persistent banner, dismiss-once flag in localStorage; (3) **Every onboarding-step value editable in Settings post-onboarding** — Settings layout groups them logically (Body Metrics, Training Preferences, Run Setup, Injuries); (4) **Telemetry events for completion patterns**: `onboarding_step_skipped` (per step), `onboarding_completed`, `onboarding_abandoned`; aggregate dashboard tracks completion rate + per-step skip rate; informs v2 redesign decision; (5) **A/B test infrastructure deferred to v2** — v1 ships C uniformly; (6) **Pre-fill from existing data on re-encountered onboarding** — if user already has body metrics / training preferences set (account migration, recovery edge case), pre-fill those values in the corresponding onboarding step; skip-by-default if all data present; (7) **Partial onboarding state persisted to Firestore per step** — each step's submit writes immediately; on re-sign-in, user resumes from the step they last completed; `onboardingComplete: false` until final step; no data loss on mid-onboarding sign-out. **A1c → D (time-based re-auth + FaceID/TouchID with layered fallback) with six pins**. A (re-auth for every sign-out) is too aggressive. B (only for account deletion) is too narrow. C (iOS-only FaceID) ignores web users. D works universally: re-auth required for destructive actions if `auth_time > 300s` ago (matches R1A's existing config). Destructive actions: account deletion, email change, password change, payment changes (Stripe/IAP), sign-out from all devices (v2). Pins: (1) **WebAuthn capability check on init** — if unavailable, fall through to password / Apple Sign-In / Google Sign-In re-auth; `assertRecentAuth` doesn't care HOW re-auth happened, just that `auth_time` is fresh; (2) **OAuth re-auth re-fires the provider dialog** (re-launches Apple Sign-In or Google Sign-In); tokens refresh, `auth_time` updates; (3) **Email change for OAuth users (Apple/Google)** not directly possible — show "Sign in with a different provider to change your email" link; **Email change for password users**: re-auth + verification email to new address + confirmation link → email actually changes; (4) **FaceID prompt fires only when `auth_time > 300s` ago** — within 5min window of last re-auth, no re-prompt for sensitive actions in the same session; (5) **Layered fallback**: FaceID → device passcode → password / provider re-auth (respects iOS Settings if FaceID disabled at OS level); (6) **Web re-auth uses redirect-based flow** (Apple/Google providers) — no popup-blocker issues; WebAuthn doesn't require popups (platform authenticator); R1A's `assertRecentAuth` scope grows from account-deletion-only to email change + password change + payment changes + sign-out-all-devices (v2). **A1d → B (pre-flight pending-writes + standard sign-out) with six pins**. Mirrors W12d's Watch sign-out pattern symmetrically on iPhone. Pins: (1) **`offlineQueue.getPendingCount()` new API** — `>0` triggers warning sheet on Sign out tap; (2) **Adaptive warning copy by severity**: 1-2 pending = "1 item not yet synced · Sign out anyway?"; 3-9 = "X items not yet synced · Sign out anyway?"; 10+ = "X items not yet synced · This may take a moment to recover. Sign out anyway?"; (3) **5s in-flight sync wait before warning** — if pending count drops to 0 within 5s, sign-out proceeds without warning; otherwise prompt; (4) **Sign-out clears local residue**: `localStorage` entries with `tropos-` prefix + Firestore cache + keychain entry (Watch keychain unaffected — symmetric with W12d's "keychain cleared on Watch only" pin); (5) **Re-sign-in restores all profile data from Firestore** — no local persistence needed; settings preferences cached locally repopulate from server-side `profilePreferences` fields; no "your data is missing" panic moment; (6) **Pending-writes detection works regardless of app foreground/background** — `offlineQueue.getPendingCount()` reads from local state persisted across backgrounding (localStorage / IndexedDB). **Multi-device sign-out from all devices deferred to v2** — would use Firebase Admin `revokeRefreshTokens(uid)`; v1 sign-out is per-device. **Critical implications:** (1) **Login screen feature-detection** for Apple Sign-In browser availability + fallback tip; (2) **`auth/account-exists-with-different-credential` collision flow** + link-Apple-to-Email UX; (3) **Apple Sign-In first-launch handler** captures `displayName` + `email` immediately (Apple-policy quirk); (4) **Contextual tips banner system** post-onboarding for skipped data; (5) **`onboarding_*` telemetry events** for completion-pattern analysis (informs v2 redesign); (6) **`webauthn.ts` new module** — capability check + FaceID/TouchID re-auth + layered fallback; (7) **`requireRecentAuth(actionName)` helper API** — single callable that gates destructive actions via R1A's `assertRecentAuth`; (8) **`offlineQueue.getPendingCount()`** new API on existing module; (9) **iPhone sign-out flow** mirrors W12d's Watch pattern (5s in-flight-sync wait + adaptive warning + clear-local-residue); (10) **Settings page extensions**: groups for Body Metrics + Training Preferences + Run Setup + Injuries (mapping to onboarding step categories); each section has the same field set as its corresponding step; (11) **Resume-from-step onboarding** for users who sign out mid-flow; (12) **Pre-fill onboarding from existing data** for migration/recovery edge cases; (13) **Re-auth dialog surfaces current email** for OAuth multi-account safety. **Out of scope (deferred to v2)**: account recovery when user loses access to all three providers simultaneously; multi-device session dashboard; passkey support; "Sign out from all devices" via `revokeRefreshTokens`; adaptive cohort onboarding; Google One Tap. **R1A intersection NOTE (PR #505 still in-flight)**: `assertRecentAuth` scope grows from account-deletion-only to also gate: email change, password change, payment changes, sign-out-from-all-devices (v2). Same `checkRecentAuth` helper, more callers. Flag for R1A author to confirm extension scope. **Watch impact**: A1d's iPhone sign-out flow is the **symmetric counterpart to W12d's Watch sign-out** — both use pre-flight pending-writes pattern. No new Watch work. **No PR-L impact** (auth state is per-device Firebase Auth managed; tokens cleared per-device on sign-out). First decision in the A (Auth + onboarding) arc. |
| A2  | Account recovery for triple-provider lockout | **Forward-planning grill for v2** — A1 explicitly deferred this to v2 ("user loses access to all three providers simultaneously — extreme edge case; punt to v2"). Grilling now to pin design intent ahead of build. **Problem**: user signed up with Email + Apple + Google. Loses access to all auth providers simultaneously — forgot password, locked out of Apple ID, Google account compromised. Standard provider recovery paths fail. Tropos's adaptive engine compounds value over months (training history, social data, performance baselines) — high-impact data loss with no recourse if recovery isn't designed. **Reference apps**: Strava (backup email optional + magic link + no behavioral checks). MyFitnessPal (backup email mandatory + password-reset-email only). Apple iCloud (recovery contacts + recovery key + 14-day waiting period). Google Account (multiple options + behavioral checks). WhatsApp / Signal (phone-only + SIM rotation + no email path). **Pattern: account-recovery converged on email + phone hybrid with behavioral abuse protection.** Tropos is small-team scale where simpler is fine but data-value-lost risk is high. Stress-tested one pass; 16 pins (4 sub-decision + 12 stress-test). **A2a → C (hybrid email OR phone) with three pins**. Email-only (A) fails when user changes email; phone-only (B) fails when user changes carrier; security questions (D) are weak (data brokers + public records). C matches Apple/Google pattern: user provides at least one contact at recovery-setup time, can add the second later, either works for recovery. Pins: (1) **Apple hide-my-email relay works long-term** (per Apple's contract — forwarding persists); recovery via Apple-relay backup email functions as long as forwarding remains active; **edge case for support**: if user revokes Tropos from Apple Sign-In, relay forwarding may break — they're locked out; surface tip during recovery-setup for Apple-relay users; (2) **Phone-number-change sends SMS to OLD phone** (if still reachable): "Your phone number was changed for Tropos" — prevents silent takeover via SIM-port attack; legit user spots port attempt before it's used for recovery; (3) **Validate `backupEmail != primaryAuthEmail`** at recovery setup for password-auth users; if user only has one email, force phone-based recovery OR show "Recovery email must differ from your sign-in email" + suggestion to add secondary; prevents the "same-email-as-both" useless config. **A2b → D (lazy prompt at destructive-action time) with two pins**. Mandatory at signup (A) creates friction and amplifies onboarding drop-off. Optional at signup (B) has 80%+ skip rates per industry. Post-onboarding (C) is disconnected. D is most powerful: re-auth flow checks if recovery is configured before destructive action; if not, prompt "Add a recovery contact before continuing — you may need it to recover access if you lose all your sign-in methods"; users see immediate relevance → higher conversion. Pins: (1) **Account deletion EXEMPT from recovery-setup prompt** — user is explicitly leaving; R1A's re-auth flow handles deletion; recovery-setup applies to all OTHER destructive actions (email change, password change, payment changes, sign-out-from-all-devices); (2) **"Remind me later" stores 7-day timestamp**; next destructive action within 7d skips the prompt; after 7d re-prompts; permanent dismiss only by configuring at least one contact. **A2c → C (magic link + OAuth provider notification) with three pins**. Immediate full access (A) enables takeover attacks if backup email compromised. 7-day cool-down (B) is hostile to legitimate users (data-locked for a week). Manual support (D) doesn't scale + adds latency. C balances: legitimate user gets fast recovery + attack-victim user gets early warning via OAuth providers they still control (Apple emails "someone is recovering this account" → legit user intervenes). Pins: (1) **OAuth-provider notification fires only when providers linked** — email-only users rely on backup-email-only verification (acknowledged risk); mitigation: encourage adding second auth provider during recovery-setup flow ("Adding Apple or Google sign-in makes recovery safer"); (2) **OAuth notifications rate-limited to 1 per provider per 24h per recovery context** — multiple rapid recovery attempts within a day consolidate into single notification "Multiple recovery attempts on your Tropos account today"; no spam; (3) **Revoke link works 7 days post-recovery and restores pre-recovery state** — revoke action does (a) `revokeRefreshTokens(uid)` via Firebase Admin kills recovered session globally, (b) restores ALL pre-recovery auth state (password reset; user must use OAuth to sign in + manually reset password), (c) logs forensic event for admin review; defense in depth even after attacker "succeeded". **A2d → B (rate-limit + behavioral checks) with three pins**. Rate-limit alone (A) lets sophisticated attackers spread attempts over days. Behavioral checks (impossible-travel) catch most common attack pattern (compromised email → recovery from different country than user's recent activity). IP allow-list (C) too restrictive for travel scenarios. Pins: (1) **Rate-limit 3 attempts per 24h per recovery contact** via `rateLimiter.js` new `recovery_attempt` action key; beyond 3 error: "Too many recovery attempts · Try again tomorrow or contact support"; (2) **Impossible-travel uses 30-day ROLLING baseline of user's actual locations** (both successful logins + OAuth provider sign-ins); nomad's baseline is wide so flag triggers only for truly anomalous (never-seen country, impossibly-short time window between attempts); reduces false positives without weakening check; (3) **Device-theft defense via OAuth-provider notification** (per A2c): even with phone + email accessible on stolen device, attacker must ALSO control Apple ID / Google account; defense holds against device-theft alone, falls only on multi-account compromise; **magic link expires 15 minutes**, **single-use semantics** (click consumes immediately; subsequent clicks return to active session if open, else expired-message). **Cross-cutting** (1 pin): **`recoveryAttempts` collection retains forensic data 12 months post-attempt**; auto-purge via cron CF after 12 months UNLESS attempt associated with fraud investigation (manual admin flag); retention policy documented in privacy policy. **Critical implications**: (1) `recoveryContacts: { email?: string, phone?: string }` field on user profile — at least one required to perform recovery, both optional in storage; (2) `recoveryAttempts/{recoveryId}` Firestore collection — `{ uid, contactUsed, ip, geolocation, ipVelocityFlag, succeeded, createdAt, revokedAt?, fraudFlag? }`; (3) Recovery setup UX inside re-auth flow for destructive actions when not configured; (4) Magic-link Cloud Function with JWT 15-min expiration + `recovery_attempt_id`; (5) OAuth-provider notification email templates "Someone is recovering your Tropos account · [Revoke recovery]"; (6) Phone-change confirmation SMS to OLD number (anti-port-attack); (7) Impossible-travel check using IP geolocation against 30-day rolling baseline; (8) Rate limit via `rateLimiter.js` new `recovery_attempt` action key (3/day); (9) Settings → "Account Security" → "Recovery contacts" subsection (view + edit + delete + view recent attempts + revoke active sessions); (10) Revoke link Cloud Function (7-day window post-recovery); (11) Email change for password users intersects — updating email may invalidate recovery contact if matched (surface confirmation); (12) Provider sign-in remains primary path — "Forgot password?" first guides user through provider recovery before exposing Tropos's recovery flow (last-resort framing prevents recovery being the easy path for attackers). **R1A intersection NOTE (PR #505 still in-flight)**: (a) `recoveryContacts` field on user profile gets cleared on account deletion (covered by R1A's user-keyed sweep); (b) `recoveryAttempts/{recoveryId}` collection — **preserve attempts for forensic admin trail** post-deletion, anonymise `uid` to `__deleted__` (same pattern as S4's `reports` + S3's reporter-anonymisation); add to R1A inventory; (c) **deletion executor must check `recoveryAttempts` for active sessions and revoke them before proceeding** — prevents recovered-account ghosts from re-emerging post-deletion. **Out of scope (deferred further beyond v2)**: Apple iCloud-style trusted-contacts vouching (asking friend to verify); YubiKey / hardware security key recovery (power-user feature); in-person identity verification (operationally infeasible at Tropos team size). **No Watch impact** (account recovery is iPhone/web only). **No PR-L impact** (recovery state is per-user, no cross-device reconciliation). Second decision in the A (Auth + onboarding) arc. **v2-scoped — designed ahead of build to inform architecture.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| A3  | Passkey support (FIDO2 / WebAuthn)           | **v2-scoped forward-planning grill** — extends A1c's WebAuthn re-auth module to primary sign-in via passkeys. Passkeys replace passwords with cryptographic key pairs bound to a device — Apple / Google / Microsoft all pushing this as the password-replacement future. **Reference apps**: Apple iCloud / Apple ID (passkey support since iOS 16, coexists with password, iCloud Keychain sync). Google Account (passkey support 2023+, "skip password" prompt on signed-in devices, coexists). GitHub (multiple passkeys + password coexist). Microsoft accounts (aggressive passwordless toggle). Strava / MyFitnessPal / fitness apps (no passkey support yet — lagging consumer category). **Pattern: tech giants converged on passkey + password coexistence; consumer fitness apps slow to follow.** Tropos can ship early as a differentiator. Stress-tested one pass; 17 pins (4 sub-decision + 13 stress-test). **A3a → A (coexist with password indefinitely) with four pins**. Passkey-primary-password-degraded (B) creates UX cliff for users who lose access to their passkey-bearing devices. Passkey-only-for-new-signups (C) splits the user base into two cohorts with divergent flows. Migration deadline cutover (D) is hostile and risks data loss for users who miss the deadline. A is conservative + matches Apple/Google's approach: passkeys are an option, password remains available. Pins: (1) **Maintenance burden incremental not multiplicative** — Firebase Auth handles multi-provider natively; passkey is one more credential type; single `useAuth` hook + provider-agnostic re-auth via A1c's WebAuthn module; (2) **Login screen shows passkey button ONLY when client detects a registered passkey** via locally-cached `passkeysCount > 0` — users who never set up passkey never see the option (no mental-model confusion); users with passkey see it surfaced as primary path naturally; (3) **WebAuthn handles multi-credential disambiguation natively** — iOS FaceID prompt shows "Choose account" for multi-account-per-device users; iOS platform API, no Tropos work needed; (4) **"Safer + faster sign-in" framing is accurate marketing** — passkeys are origin-bound (phishing-resistant); real security benefit, not aspirational claim. **A3b → C (hybrid passkeys + A2 backup) with three pins**. Pure Keychain/Password Manager sync (B) assumes users have a single ecosystem (all-Apple or all-Google); real users mix devices. If a user loses ALL passkey-bearing devices (theft, fire, water damage), they need a recovery path that's not device-bound. A2 (email/phone) is that path. Same recovery as password users (A) doesn't acknowledge passkey users may want passkey-specific recovery flow nuances. Printable recovery key (D) adds operational complexity for marginal user-base. Pins: (1) **A2 recovery contact MANDATORY at passkey-first signup** — exception to A2b-D's lazy-prompt default; passkey adoption is the specific trigger that makes recovery essential; cannot complete passkey signup without configuring email or phone backup; (2) **A2 recovery for passkey-only users grants temporary session + prompts to register a NEW passkey on the current device**; old passkeys remain in Settings → Sign-in methods (revocable); new passkey replaces functionally without erasing audit trail; (3) **iCloud-Keychain-synced passkey appears as the SAME `credentialId` across Apple devices** — server-side CF sees one credential; Settings lists one entry with `lastUsedAt` + `lastUsedGeo` updated per device's most-recent use ("Used most recently from iPad"); NOT duplicate entries per device. **A3c → C (Settings list with metadata + timestamps + geo) with three pins**. No UI (A) leaves users blind to their own auth state — surprises like "wait, I have a passkey on my old phone?" become unresolvable. Basic list (B) is the minimum. Biometric-tier metadata (D) adds technical detail most users don't understand. C balances: each passkey shows device label (auto-detected from User-Agent + iOS device name via Capacitor: "iPhone 15 · Safari") + last-used timestamp + approximate geo ("Sydney, Australia") + Revoke button. Pins: (1) **Geo shows city-level only** (never exact coordinates or addresses); tooltip notes "Approximate location based on IP"; VPN users may see misleading geo (acceptable trade-off); (2) **Passkey list strictly per-user** — Firestore rule `request.auth.uid == resource.data.uid` enforces access; standard pattern; (3) **"Revoke all passkeys" bulk action** in Settings → Sign-in methods; confirms then revokes all passkeys + signs out all sessions globally via Firebase Admin `revokeRefreshTokens(uid)`; user must sign in via fallback (Email/Apple/Google) on next access. **A3d → A (iOS first, web later) with three pins**. iOS native passkey UX is mature (iOS 16+) with seamless FaceID integration; Capacitor's passkey plugin landscape is more straightforward on iOS native. Web-first (B) inverts the priority since Tropos's primary install is iOS. Parallel (C) doubles initial scope. iOS-only forever (D) abandons web users — not aligned with Tropos's web-app support. Pins: (1) **Validation criteria for web rollout** = (a) >100 passkey registrations across user base AND (b) <5% passkey sign-in failure rate over 30 days AND (c) zero critical security incidents related to passkey; all three required before queueing web rollout work; (2) **iOS-passkey users accessing web during iOS-only phase fall back to email/Apple/Google sign-in on web** — passkey isn't available on web yet; once web rollout ships, existing iOS passkey works on web automatically via cross-platform WebAuthn shared `credentialId`; (3) **iOS <16 capability check hides passkey button on incompatible devices** — Capacitor's iOS plugin detects iOS version + WebAuthn availability; older-iOS users use existing methods. **Critical implications:** (1) **`passkeys/{passkeyId}` Firestore sub-collection** under user — `{ uid, credentialId, publicKey, deviceLabel, createdAt, lastUsedAt, lastUsedIp, lastUsedGeo, revokedAt? }`; (2) **`passkeysCount` field on user profile** — denormalised count for quick "does this user have any passkeys?" check; updated on register/revoke via Firestore transaction; (3) **Passkey registration flow** (Settings → Sign-in methods → "Add passkey"): WebAuthn.createCredential with iOS FaceID prompt + server-side attestation verification + auto-detected device label (User-Agent + Capacitor API); (4) **Passkey sign-in flow** (Login screen): WebAuthn.getCredential with iOS handling FaceID + multi-credential selection; (5) **Login screen layout (post-A3, iOS)**: Passkey conditional (top, when `passkeysCount > 0`) → Apple Sign-In → Email → Google — extends A1a ordering with passkey-when-available slot; (6) **Telemetry events**: `passkey_registered`, `passkey_sign_in_attempted`, `passkey_sign_in_succeeded`, `passkey_revoked`, `passkey_recovery_via_a2`; (7) **Apple Sign-In + Passkey multi-method coexistence works** — user with Apple Sign-In can ALSO register passkeys; same for Google; email-auth users gain optional passkey; (8) **Passkeys bound to UID not email** — email change doesn't invalidate passkeys; (9) **Cross-device QR-code passkey sign-in deferred to a later iteration** — iOS-native + iCloud-Keychain-sync covers majority of cross-device cases. **Out of scope (deferred beyond v2)**: Cross-device QR-code passkey sign-in; hardware security key (YubiKey) registration (power-user feature, defer with A2's similar deferral); passwordless toggle (force-disable password fallback per user — adds risk surface, defer until passkey adoption data justifies); migration encouragement banners (push password users toward passkeys — defer until adoption metrics inform; coexist-quietly is the v2 default). **R1A intersection**: `passkeys/{passkeyId}` sub-collection cleaned up on account deletion (covered by R1A's existing user-keyed sweep); **no new forensic-preservation requirement** — passkeys don't have audit-trail value post-deletion (unlike `reports` from S4 or `recoveryAttempts` from A2); add `passkeys/` subtree to R1A's deletion inventory checklist. **Connections**: A1c WebAuthn module reused for passkey registration + sign-in (single shared module, already pinned for re-auth in A1c); A2 recovery is canonical fallback for all-devices-lost scenarios across both password + passkey users; A1a ordering principle extends to slot passkey above Apple Sign-In when registered (most native + fastest). **No Watch impact** (passkeys are iPhone/web only). **No PR-L impact** (per-user state). Third decision in the A (Auth + onboarding) arc. **v2-scoped — designed ahead of build to inform architecture.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| A4  | Multi-device session dashboard               | **v2-scoped forward-planning grill** — final A arc grill, closes A1's v2 deferral list (multi-device session dashboard + sign-out-from-all-devices both punted to v2). **Problem**: Firebase Auth doesn't natively track active sessions per device; users have no visibility into where they're signed in, can't selectively sign-out a specific device. Real-world need: stolen phone, borrowed laptop, suspected account compromise. **Reference apps**: Google Account ("Your devices" dashboard with per-device + bulk sign-out, full session metadata). Apple ID (Settings shows trusted devices + per-device sign-out via dashboard). Strava (bulk sign-out only, no per-session control). GitHub (Sessions tab in Settings with per-session revocation + bulk). MyFitnessPal / fitness apps (no session dashboard, bulk-only on password change). **Pattern: tech giants offer per-session control + bulk; fitness apps lag with bulk-only.** Tropos ships competent session dashboard at v2. Stress-tested one pass; 18 pins (4 sub-decision + 14 stress-test). **A4a → A (Firestore sub-collection) with four pins**. Standard pattern, supports per-session metadata, scales, matches A3 passkeys pattern. Single field on profile (B) is too coarse (atomic array updates awkward). Custom claims (C) wrong storage tier (1KB limit). Cloud Logging / BigQuery (D) is analytics-tier not real-time UI source. Pins: (1) **Read costs negligible** — typical user has <10 sessions; 10 doc reads on Settings view is trivial; power users with 20+ still trivial; (2) **CRITICAL: throttle `lastUsedAt` writes to once per 6 hours per session** — without throttle, 1000 users × 3 sessions × 24 refreshes/day = 72K writes/day vs Firestore free tier 20K/day limit; with throttle, 12K/day fits free tier; UX impact negligible (6-hour staleness on "last used" timestamp is fine for the use case); (3) **Concurrent sign-in race harmless** — each sign-in creates session entry with unique UUID `sessionId`; concurrent writes to different docs, no race; (4) **Sub-collection choice rationale** — Firestore rules `request.auth.uid == path[1]` simpler at sub-collection level; matches A3 passkeys pattern; collection-group query available for cleanup CF. **A4b → D (full metadata including refresh-token-ID + revokedAt) with two pins**. Each session entry needs enough metadata to display meaningful dashboard row AND support per-session revocation. Schema: `{ uid, deviceLabel, platform: 'ios' \| 'android' \| 'web', firstUsedAt, lastUsedAt, lastUsedIp, lastUsedGeo, refreshTokenId, revokedAt? }`. Pins: (1) **Storing `refreshTokenId` (not the token itself) is safe** — ID is opaque identifier used for linking session entry to Firebase Auth credential; doesn't grant access alone; (2) **Device label XSS validation** — strip HTML tags + cap 64 chars before storage; cosmetic-only field, not security-relevant (User-Agent + Capacitor device API can return arbitrary strings; spoofing has no impact beyond cosmetic but XSS in Settings display would be a real risk). **A4c → C (hybrid bulk + per-session) with three pins**. Bulk-only (A) misses "kill stolen phone, keep my laptop" use case. Per-session-only (B) misses "everything signed out NOW" panic case. Defer (D) leaves A1d's v2 promise unfulfilled. C provides both — bulk for emergency via Firebase Admin `revokeRefreshTokens(uid)` (server-side enforced regardless of device state); per-session via Firestore `revokedAt` field + client-cooperative sign-out (target device's onSnapshot listener sees its own session marked revoked → signs out locally + clears cache). Pins: (1) **KNOWN LIMITATION — client-cooperative sign-out requires target device online to take effect**; once online, listener catches up + signs out; for emergency (e.g., stolen phone), bulk sign-out-everywhere is the correct tool; (2) **Bulk action also writes `revokedAt` to all session entries in same transaction** — cosmetic consistency (session list shows revoked state immediately); bulk requires re-auth per A1c's `auth_time > 300s` gate; (3) **Race conditions idempotent** — both writes set `revokedAt: serverTimestamp`; either succeeds, both leave session in revoked state; no conflict on simultaneous revoke writes. **A4d → B (auto-cleanup >90 days inactive) with three pins**. Never-expire (A) means user accumulates stale entries over years — list becomes unmanageable. Per-API-call timestamp update (C) adds write overhead to every operation. Manual cleanup only (D) is friction. B balances: 90 days of inactivity = session is stale; auto-cleanup via cron CF; `lastUsedAt` updated only on auth events (sign-in, token refresh with 6-hour throttle) not every API call. Pins: (1) **`auto_cleanup_stale_sessions` cron CF uses collection-group query** `sessions WHERE lastUsedAt < now - 90 days` (composite index required) + batched delete; daily cost bounded by stale-count, not total users; low cost; (2) **Cleanup only deletes session metadata, not user's actual data** — user can return any time; first action creates fresh session; no data loss concern; (3) **90 days matches industry pattern** (Google: 28 days for similar trust signals; Apple iCloud: 30 days for "trusted devices"); 90 days is conservative for Tropos; **review at 60 days post-launch based on telemetry**; adjust if needed. **Cross-cutting (2 pins)**: (1) **Geo tooltip explains "location based on IP at last sign-in"** — travel scenarios may show stale geo; user who sees unfamiliar geo can revoke + re-sign-in to update; (2) **Bulk sign-out kills active A2 recovery session** — `revokeRefreshTokens` revokes ALL tokens including recovery; user must re-initiate recovery if needed; acceptable (bulk is explicit user choice). **Critical implications:** (1) **`users/{uid}/sessions/{sessionId}` Firestore sub-collection** with schema above; (2) **Session creation on every successful sign-in** — refresh updates `lastUsedAt` (6-hour throttle); (3) **Per-session "Revoke" mechanism**: CF writes `revokedAt: serverTimestamp` → target device's onSnapshot listener triggers local sign-out flow (clears cache, redirects to Login per A1d); (4) **Bulk "Sign out from all devices" mechanism**: CF calls `revokeRefreshTokens(uid)` via Firebase Admin → all current tokens invalidated server-side → each device's next API call fails with `auth/user-token-expired` → forces re-auth; CF also writes `revokedAt` to all session entries in same transaction (cosmetic); (5) **Settings → "Sign-in methods" → "Active sessions" subsection** — table of device label + platform icon + last-used timestamp + city-level geo + Revoke button per row + "Sign out from all devices" bulk action; (6) **Geo shows city-level only** with "Approximate location based on IP" tooltip (matches A3c); (7) **Device label auto-detected** from User-Agent + Capacitor device API (mirrors A3 passkey labeling); (8) **Privacy invariant** pinned in `docs/privacy.md` alongside other auth-event-tracking invariants; aggregate retention follows R1A's user-keyed sweep; (9) **Telemetry events**: `session_created`, `session_revoked_per_device`, `session_revoked_bulk`, `session_auto_cleaned`; (10) **Per-device session revocation does NOT update `auth_time` for other devices** — only revoked device loses access. **Connections**: A1d's iPhone sign-out flow writes `revokedAt` to its own session entry as part of sign-out process; W12d's Watch sign-out similarly writes `revokedAt` to Watch session entry; A2 recovery success creates new session entry for recovery device + revokes all previous sessions (per A2c's revoke-link mechanism aligning with A4's per-session API); A3 passkey sign-in creates session entry like any other auth method (passkey-specific `authMethod: 'passkey'` field optional for telemetry); A3 bulk passkey revocation also revokes all sessions (per A3c's "Revoke all passkeys" + global sign-out). **R1A intersection**: `users/{uid}/sessions/` sub-collection cleaned up on account deletion (covered by R1A's user-keyed sweep); **no forensic preservation needed** (transient operational data unlike `reports` or `recoveryAttempts`); add `sessions/` subtree to R1A's deletion inventory checklist. **Out of scope (deferred beyond v2)**: Trusted devices concept (device-vouching, "I trust this Mac, skip 2FA") — adds complexity, defer; session-specific permission tiers (read-only vs full) — over-engineered; cross-account session merging — not relevant; push notification on new session creation ("New sign-in on iPad · Was this you?") — useful safety feature but adds notification volume, defer to v3 if user demand emerges. **No Watch impact** (Watch sessions are tracked but Watch app doesn't render the dashboard; iPhone Settings is the surface). **No PR-L impact** (per-user state). Fourth decision in the A (Auth + onboarding) arc — **final A arc grill, closes A1's v2 deferral list**. **v2-scoped — designed ahead of build to inform architecture.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

### Subscription arc (Sub1–)

Decisions on Tropos's monetisation model — trial mechanics, cross-platform billing (Stripe + Apple IAP), grace periods for failed payments, cancellation behaviour. Numbered Sub1+ to keep separation from Q / W / RP / F / S / P / A arcs. Distinct concern: this arc focuses on payment flow policy on top of the substantial existing subscription infrastructure (proPlans.ts, proFeatures.ts, subscription.ts, purchaseProvider.ts, useProCheckout.ts, ProModal.tsx, Upgrade.tsx). Intersects with F1b (Pro-gated image-AI), P1c (HealthKit intentionally NOT Pro-gated), A1c (re-auth for payment changes).

| Sub1 | Stripe / Apple IAP subscription flow | **Reference apps:** MyFitnessPal Premium (1-month free trial + Stripe+IAP + cancel-at-period-end). Whoop (no trial, subscription required upfront, primary value-prop). Strava Premium (1-month trial + Stripe+IAP + cancel-at-period-end). MacroFactor (7-day trial + IAP only on iOS + cancel-at-period-end). Notion / Linear / typical SaaS (14-day trial + Stripe + pro-rated refunds). **Pattern: fitness apps converge on 7-day OR 1-month trial + Stripe + IAP + cancel-at-period-end + no pro-rated refunds.** Tropos sits inside this range. Existing infra: `proPlans.ts` (pricing single source of truth — monthly + yearly), `proFeatures.ts` (typed registry — 6 Pro feature keys: performance_engine, ai_food_logging, ai_coaching, adaptive_macros, adaptive_tdee, advanced_insights), `subscription.ts` (tier/trial/access logic + SCAN_LIMITS free=10 pro=300), `purchaseProvider.ts` (Stripe + Apple IAP product IDs), `useProCheckout.ts`, `ProModal.tsx`, `Upgrade.tsx`. Stress-tested one pass; 20 pins total. **Sub1a → B (7-day free trial) with four pins**. No trial (A) hostile for a feature-heavy adaptive engine where value compounds over time. 14 days (C) reasonable; 30 days (D) too generous — most users decide in a week. 7 days matches MacroFactor + Apple App Store's preferred trial length (Apple's review process favours conservative trials). Pins: (1) **`hasUsedTrial` flag is per-Firebase-UID** (not per-email); new accounts via new email = new trial; **mitigation**: rate-limit account creation by IP via existing pattern + flag suspicious patterns (>3 accounts same IP in 7 days) for admin review; acceptable v1 leak at small user base; (2) **Payment method captured at trial start** — Apple IAP confirm sheet shows "Subscription starts 7 days from today" + Stripe checkout collects card upfront; user agreed to conversion when starting trial; App Store policy compliant; (3) **Trial starts ONLY when user explicitly taps "Start Pro trial"** from ProModal or Upgrade page (not on account creation); new users default to free tier until upgrade attempt; (4) **Trial cancellation pre-conversion = no charge** (industry-standard); user cancels day 6 → no payment processed → reverts to free at day 7. **Sub1b → C (platform-tied + Firebase Auth UID reconciliation) with three pins**. Single-platform (A) misses revenue (iOS users likely majority but web matters). Manual sync (D) operationally complex. C: iOS user upgrading via in-app paywall → Apple IAP (App Store mandate); web user upgrading via Tropos web → Stripe; Pro status reconciled in Firestore via Firebase Auth UID — Pro on one surface = Pro everywhere for the same account. android_iap`); on upgrade, `source`updated to current platform's source; old canceled subs remain in payment-platform records but Tropos reads only the current`source`. **Sub1c → B (3-day grace period for Stripe; Apple defers to 16-day grace) with three pins**. Hard cutoff (A) hostile; 7+ days (C-D) too generous + encourages abuse pattern (cancel-then-resub games). 3 days = card decline → notification email → user has time to fix → no Pro disruption for transient issues; aligns with Stripe's default dunning timeline. Pins: (1) **Apple IAP defers to Apple's 16-day grace** (Apple's server-side retry logic); Tropos doesn't layer 3-day on top; **Stripe failures use Tropos's 3-day grace**; different mechanisms per platform — intentional asymmetry, not a bug; (2) **Trial-conversion failure handled via platform-specific grace** — Apple 16d (Apple retries) or Stripe 3d (Tropos dunning); if grace expires without payment, subscription downgrades to free; **`hasUsedTrial: true`flag remains set** (no second trial); (3) **Webhook from Stripe fires on successful payment** → Cloud Function clears grace state + restores Pro access instantly; no manual intervention needed. **Sub1d → B (cancel-at-period-end) with three pins**. Immediate cancellation (A) hostile and against industry norm. Pro-rated refunds (C/D) operationally complex + Apple IAP doesn't support pro-rated refunds (Apple handles refunds via Customer Service, Tropos can't initiate). B is industry standard: cancel anytime, Pro features remain until paid period ends, no refund. Stripe + Apple IAP both natively support this cancellation model. Pins: (1) **Cancel-at-period-end requires fresh`auth_time`per A1c-D** (destructive payment action); actual refund (rare admin-initiated case) goes through Stripe Dashboard or Apple Customer Service, not in-app flow; (2) **Re-subscribe before period-end reverses cancellation, no new charge, no new trial** — Stripe:`subscription.update({ cancel_at_period_end: false })`; IAP: user uses App Store re-enable flow; standard pattern; specific numbers in`proPlans.ts`, not grilled here); discount motivates yearly conversion (long-term retention bias); (2) **NO trial-extension offers in v1** — pure 7-day trial then convert-or-free; re-engagement campaigns deferred to growth-marketing phase post-launch; (3) **Apple Family Sharing IS supported automatically via IAP** — Apple handles entitlement propagation; family members get Pro access via their own Apple ID; document in FAQ; Stripe family/team subs deferred to v2. **Critical implications:** (1) **7-day trial defined in both Stripe + Apple IAP**: Stripe `trial_period_days: 7`+ Apple IAP introductory offer (free for 7 days, then converts to paid); (2) **Trial telemetry**:`trial_started`, `trial_converted`, `trial_canceled`events; track conversion rate per acquisition source; (3) **One trial per user lifetime** — backend tracks`hasUsedTrial` flag; subsequent upgrade attempts skip trial period; (4) **`users/{uid}.subscription`field schema**:`{ tier: 'free' \| 'pro', source: 'stripe' \| 'ios_iap' \| 'android_iap', expiresAt, willRenew, trialEndsAt? }`; (5) **Webhook resilience**: both Stripe + Apple IAP webhooks idempotent (use event IDs as dedupe keys); replay-tolerance for missed deliveries; (6) **Server-side validation**: Apple receipt validation via verifyReceipt or App Store Server API; Stripe events validated via webhook signing secret; (7) **Grace period UX**: 3 days before downgrade after Stripe payment failure — Day 0 email "We couldn't process your payment · Update your card", Day 1-2 same email + in-app banner, Day 3 downgrade to free + final email "Your Tropos Pro has paused"; (8) **Cancellation flow** (Settings → Subscription → Cancel): confirm sheet shows period-end date; Stripe → `subscription.update({ cancel_at_period_end: true })`; IAP → user redirected to App Store subscription settings (Apple UI mandate); Reconciles existing discrepancy between `proFeatures.ts` (6 typed keys: `performance_engine`, `ai_food_logging`, `ai_coaching`, `adaptive_macros`, `adaptive_tdee`, `advanced_insights`) and `subscription.ts` `featureAccess` map (4 free + 4 pro flags). P2 also made PI a hero Home card surface, which conflicts with `performance_engine` being Pro-gated. **Reference apps**: MyFitnessPal Premium (moderate scope — advanced food search, custom macros, premium analytics, ad-free). MacroFactor (comprehensive paywall — everything Pro except basic logging). Strava Premium (narrow paywall — segments, training plans, Beacon, HR analysis). Whoop (subscription-only, no free tier). Apple Fitness+ (subscription = full content). **Pattern: fitness apps vary wildly — comprehensive paywall maximises revenue; narrow paywall preserves free-tier value.** Tropos's positioning suggests narrow paywall preserves "calm-adaptive" promise for everyone. Stress-tested one pass; 18 pins (4 sub-decision + 14 stress-test). **Sub2a → C (PI fully free; only AI-augmented Pro) with three pins**. P2 made PI a hero Home card + iOS Widget + Watch Smart Stack — gating that behind Pro hides Tropos's WHOLE adaptive-positioning from free users. PI computation is server-side cost-zero (existing CFs already run for everyone for analytics). P2b deliberately chose deterministic on-device templates (no Gemini) — no per-user cost. **PI + sub-scores + deterministic insights all FREE**; Pro gates AI-augmented features (image-AI per F1b, future AI coaching). Pins: (1) **Image-AI food logging remains strongest revenue driver per industry benchmark** (MyFitnessPal Snap It + Lose It Snap It paywalled successfully); **adaptive TDEE + adaptive macros are differentiated optimisation features** most apps don't have; AI coaching is v3 scope; (2) **CFs already running for all users** per P1's existing infra; no gate change in Sub2; CF cost negligible at small scale (~$0.0001/user/month); (3) **`paywall_viewed` indirect attribution still works** — PI being free generates discovery surfaces (Home, Widget) but doesn't directly trigger paywall; user discovers Tropos via PI, hits a Pro feature later → `paywall_viewed` fires. **Sub2b → A (keep F1b's locked cap structure) with one pin**. Text-AI free 10/day + image-AI Pro 300/day. F1b already grilled; no new evidence to revisit. Pin: F1b's structure held unchanged in Sub2b; no new pins beyond confirmation. **Sub2c → D (plateau detection FREE; adaptive TDEE + macros Pro) with four pins**. Plateau detection is a **SAFETY feature** — flags stalling/regressing users so they can adjust before frustration accumulates. Gating safety behind Pro is hostile + creates negative outcomes (frustrated free users churn instead of upgrading). Adaptive TDEE + adaptive macros are **optimisation features** — compounding value over months, reasonable to gate. D aligns positioning — Tropos protects free users (safety), upsells optimisation. Pins: (1) **`plateauDetection` runs as part of existing weekly rollup**; incremental cost negligible; same CF, broader audience; (2) **Plateau surfaces via insight strip + optional notification** (existing `nutritionInsights.ts` patterns); free users get same UI surface as Pro users for plateau alerts; no new UI work; (3) **Free users get STATIC TDEE** (Mifflin-St-Jeor calculated from height/weight/age/activity at signup; adjusts only when user updates body metrics in Settings); **Pro users get adaptive TDEE** that auto-adjusts to weight trends; **surface gate**: free users see TDEE number but not "Adjusted X kcal based on 7-day trend" callouts; tap-to-learn → ProModal explains adaptive TDEE; (4) **Free users get FIXED daily macros** (one ratio for all days); **Pro users get day-type-specific macros** (higher carbs on training, higher fat on rest per `phaseNutrition.ts`); surfaces in macro display as "Same macros every day" for free with subtle upgrade hint. **Sub2d → B (locked features visible with lock icon + ProModal on tap) with three pins**. Hidden (A) creates surprise on upgrade ("wait, this exists?"). Preview (C) is teaser-ad UX, feels icky for Tropos's calm voice. Mix (D) inconsistent. B matches current `ProModal` pattern + standard SaaS UX. Pins: (1) **Lock icons appear only on FEATURE SURFACES** (adaptive TDEE tooltip, macros day-type indicator, image-AI camera shutter), **NOT on Home dashboard tiles** — free user's Home is clean, Pro gates are contextual when they reach the specific feature; (2) **ProModal copy uses `proFeatures.ts` registry** (`title` + `tagline` + `label`) per feature — already wired per the file's design comment; no new copy needed for v1; existing copy validated by Sub2's narrowed scope; (3) **Feature flags layer on top of subscription tier** — flag-gated Pro features check flag first, then tier; users with flag + free tier see ProModal (paywall); users with flag + Pro tier get feature; users without flag don't see it at all. **Cross-cutting (3 pins)**: (1) **Re-gating previously free features post-launch is HOSTILE** — creates Pro-user dissatisfaction (paying for what was free) + free-user churn (losing what they had); **don't re-gate ever**; if revenue insufficient post-Sub2, raise PRICE or ADD new Pro features, never revoke free features; (2) **Trial expiration drops Pro-gated features only**; PI + plateau (now free per Sub2) stay accessible regardless of trial state; no regressions on tier transitions for free-tier features; (3) **One-time email + in-app message at Sub2 launch** to existing Pro subscribers: "We've moved Performance Index and plateau detection to free for everyone — your Pro subscription continues to unlock adaptive TDEE, adaptive macros, AI food logging, and AI coaching. Thank you for supporting Tropos." Acknowledges change + reinforces value-prop retention. **Critical implications:** (1) **`proFeatures.ts` schema updates** — REMOVE `performance_engine` + `advanced_insights` keys; KEEP `ai_food_logging`, `ai_coaching`, `adaptive_macros`, `adaptive_tdee` (Pro narrows from 6 keys to 4); (2) **`subscription.ts` `featureAccess` updates**: free gains `performanceInsights` + `plateauDetection`; pro is `aiAdjustments`, `aiFoodLogging`, `phaseModes`, `adaptiveTDEE` (4 Pro flags); (3) **`ProGate` callsites for `performance_engine` and `advanced_insights` removed**; (4) **Migration is non-breaking** — existing Pro users get superset (everything they had); free users gain PI + plateau detection access; (5) **Telemetry tracks `paywall_viewed_by_feature`** to validate which features actually drive conversion; if conversion drops significantly, revisit at Sub2-r. **Connections**: P2's PI Home card + Widget + Watch Smart Stack now accessible to free users — matches hero-card positioning P2 locked; P1c's HealthKit toggle stays FREE per P1c lock (consistent with Sub2c-D's "safety/observability features stay free" principle); F1b's text-AI cap structure preserved; F3's image-AI Pro-gating preserved; A1c re-auth gates payment changes when free user upgrades or Pro user changes payment. **R1A intersection**: no new R1A items — Sub2 is policy on existing infrastructure; account deletion handles subscription cancellation per Sub1's R1A pin. **Out of scope**: specific monthly/yearly pricing numbers (live in `proPlans.ts`, not grilled); Pro feature deprecation policy (if Pro feature is removed, what happens to subscribers — defer until needed); Pro tier splits (basic Pro vs pro+) — single tier sufficient; Sub2-r revisit triggers — if conversion drops post-shrinkage, reassess. **No Watch impact** (Pro-gating happens at feature surface; Watch surfaces follow same gating per existing pattern). **No PR-L impact** (per-user account state). Second decision in the Sub (Subscription) arc. **STATUS 2026-05-24 — audit + partial implementation.** Audit (`docs/audits/2026-05-24-sub2.md`) found that Sub2's user-facing intent ("PI free, Pro narrows 6→4") was mostly true _by accident_ — the `featureAccess` map Sub2 narrows is cosmetic (6 of 7 flags are never read; only `phaseModes` consulted, and at a single callsite that gates program-configuration buttons, not the day-type macros Sub2c pin #4 describes). Real Pro-gating in the product = ONE `<ProGate>` wrapper on `AdaptiveTDEECard` + direct `isPro` checks. **Sub2c pin #3 shipped** (PR-pending: free users now see TDEE number in header with adaptive callouts replaced by an inline unlock CTA → ProModal with `featureKey="adaptive_tdee"`; 5 TDD'd tests pin the contract). **Sub2c pin #4 deferred** (fixed-macros-for-free is a real UX regression for current free users; defer until first real free-tier traffic validates the lock). **Sub2b deferred to F1b's implementation slice** — Sub2b ratifies F1b's structure but F1b was never actually implemented (see F1 STATUS line). **Track A queued**: delete the cosmetic `featureAccess` map + replace with a JSDoc pointer at the top of `subscription.ts`. **STATUS 2026-05-25 — Sub2 arc fully shipped.** Track A (cosmetic `featureAccess` map deletion + JSDoc pointer to real Pro-gating sites) shipped via PR #737. Track B Sub2c pin #3 (adaptive TDEE free preview — header value visible to free users, adaptive callouts replaced by inline unlock CTA → ProModal with `featureKey="adaptive_tdee"`) shipped via PR #735. **Sub2b ratification now true post-F1b:** PR #757 implemented F1b's separate-counters-per-action + daily-reset + image-AI Pro-only shape, so Sub2b's "keep F1b's locked cap structure" assertion is honoured by production code (was true by accident pre-#757; now true by construction). **Still deferred:** Sub2c pin #4 (fixed-macros-for-free is a real UX regression for current free users; defer until first real free-tier traffic validates the lock). |

### Page IA arc (Set1–)

Page-level information-architecture decisions — first scope was Settings IA (Set1), broadened to Home IA (Home2) and other pages as consolidation grills accumulate. Numbered Set1+ / Home2+ / etc. to keep separation from Q / W / RP / F / S / P / A / Sub arcs. **Consolidation arc** — surfaces have accumulated across feature arcs (S/A/P/Sub etc.) and need coherent placement on the pages they live on; this arc reconciles them.

Within the original Hist4 audit punch-list (`docs/audits/2026-05-24-hist4-food6.md`): H1 (custom date range picker) and H4 (`/history?filter=running&from=&to=` deep-link contract) are formally DEAD-BY-SUPERSESSION per Hist5e (negative-space lock for custom date range). H3 (charts < 3 data points → empty-state copy) is now subsumed by Hist5d's unified `dataConfidence.ts` suppression policy (T1-T5 thresholds; per-decoration suppression copy). H5 disposition (closes audit punch list): the original Hist4a-pin specifying "persistence via URL search params + `localStorage` fallback" is superseded by code rationale at `src/pages/History.tsx:150-156` — `sessionStorage` chosen instead because the hint sources (StreakFlame in-app deep-link + other one-shot routing entry points) are intentionally session-scoped to avoid stale-hint routing when a user re-opens History weeks after a side-channel deep-link fired. Lock-text was generic ("standard SPA pattern") and didn't anticipate the one-shot semantic; code's `sessionStorage` choice is correct. Pattern observation (worth surfacing in a follow-up CLAUDE.md docs entry): Tropos uses `sessionStorage` for one-shot routing/hints (this case) and `localStorage` for permanent state (Soc5 crew-banner dismiss, coachmark dismissals). H2 (chart drill-down sheets) is DEFERRED-PENDING-TELEMETRY per Hist5f (PR #724) — telemetry foundation ships in the Hist5f implementation PR. |

| PI1     | Performance metric consolidation (replaces HealthScore on Home)                                                | **First decision in the Performance arc. Replaces Round 1/2 council direction with grilled spec.** Consolidates Home's two overlapping 0-100 composites (Health Score daily + Performance Index weekly) into a single PI-driven hero card. Council-grilled across 12 stress-test rounds; converged at diminishing returns. Three sub-decisions locked: metric semantics, verb taxonomy, cold-start UX. **Q1 → Rolling 7-day PI (not weekly)** — Home's daily-refresh promise requires the headline metric to update daily. Rolling 7-day window with prior-28-day baseline; CF rewrite required (functions/performanceEngine.js becomes date-keyed not weekKey-keyed; on-write triggers + daily cron drive computes). Off-by-one drift in lifetime counters from Firestore count() eventual consistency is accepted as documented limitation; daily cron reconciles within 24h. **Q2 → 5-verb taxonomy with deload override**: `Recovering` (PI<25 / deload band), `Building` (PI 25-44 / low band), `Cruising` (PI 45-69 / moderate band), `Sharpening` (PI 70-84 / high band), `Backing off` (PI≥85 OR deloadRecommended === true — deload override always wins so the verb stays aligned with InsightStrip's recommendation). Verb derived in client from (loadBand, deloadRecommended). Ring colour from (score, deloadRecommended) — deload mutes the gradient so chrome agrees with verb (no more PI 82 + green ring + "Backing off" incongruence). Verbs are localisable enum keys not raw strings. **Q3 → Option U (engine emits signals; client constructs line)** — converged answer after rejecting Options A-T across 12 rounds. CF doc additions: `signals: { bothLoadsStrong, liftAheadOfBaseline, runAheadOfBaseline, recoveryWeak, adherenceWeak, deloadFlag, lifetimeWeeks, daysSinceLastTraining }`. Client `getLine(state, signals)` maps to a data-aware tone-aligned supporting line in a single TS constants file. Engine bullets continue feeding InsightStrip only (no hero+InsightStrip duplication). **Card states**: (1) `loading` — muted placeholder; HomeSkeleton handles initial Home load; framer-motion fade-in on cache-miss first doc arrival; (2) `empty` (no doc exists) — card chrome + muted ring + `—` number + line "Your Performance will appear after your first logged session"; NO verb, NO delta — re-introduced after stress-test caught that brand-new users (logged nothing ever) genuinely have no doc and need a render, contradicting earlier "no empty state needed" claim; (3) `low-confidence` — full ring + PI + verb, but supporting line uses sparse-data variants ("Establishing your week" / "Settling in" / "Building back up" / "Re-engaging — log a session to refresh"); delta chip HIDDEN; empty-state and low-confidence copy are DISTINCT mappings in getLine; (4) `steady` — full card with ring + PI + verb + data-aware line + delta chip. **Five refined adjustments (locked after stress-test of stress-test)**: (1) **Firestore aggregation queries (NOT denormalised counters)** — CF uses count() + ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 1 for lifetimeWorkoutCount / lifetimeRunCount / lastWorkoutAt / lastRunAt; ~4 extra reads per compute; wrapped in try/catch with fallback to previous compute's value; rejected denormalisation because consistency drift + atomicity + offline-queue + deletion-trigger gaps were worse than 4 extra cheap reads; (2) **No coach mark** — card has visible chevron `›` on right edge (existing Tropos pattern) as tap-affordance; PerformanceTab grows "About Performance Index" disclosure section, collapsible, default-open on first visit only via localStorage flag mirroring `home-day-tap-seen` pattern; (3) **Loading state via existing pattern** — wire `loading: boolean` from `usePerformanceWeeks` into card consumer to gate empty-state rendering; motion.div fade-in on first non-loading render; NO per-card skeleton (piggybacks on HomeSkeleton); NO connectivity-error state (over-engineered — onSnapshot persistence handles 99% of cases); (4) **Defensive defaults + observability** — extend `normalisePerformanceDoc` in usePerformance.ts to fill missing `signals` fields with sentinel defaults; fire `errorReporting.captureMessage` ONCE per session with fingerprint ("perf-doc-missing-signals", weekKey); pre-launch backfill script (idempotent, batched) runs after deploy to populate signals on existing docs; new card hidden behind feature flag until backfill completes; flag removed post-rollout; (5) **Accessibility spec** — short `aria-label` ("Performance ${pi}, ${verb}" or "no data yet" for empty); `aria-describedby` references a SIBLING `<span className="sr-only" id="perf-detail-{weekKey}">` carrying line + delta + low-confidence note; | PI3     | Performance card colour function (getCardColour — score-band migration)                                        | **Third decision in the Performance arc** — closes the score-band-threshold question from PI1's ungrilled list. The consolidated Performance card (PI1) needs a unified colour function replacing HS's `getScoreColor(score)` thresholds (≥70 green, ≥50 orange, <50 coral). PI's loadBand thresholds differ (≥85/≥70/≥45/≥25), `deloadRecommended` overrides, and the locked verb taxonomy needs visual coordination. Grilled 4 rounds, converged at diminishing returns. **Decision: Option F-refined — brand-purple stroke with continuous glow intensity above PI 45, amber for Backing off, two-channel visual signalling.** **Two-channel design (load-bearing insight from stress-testing)**: stroke colour carries verb-state categorically (brand purple OR amber); glow intensity carries score-quality continuously (0 → 1 across PI 45-100). Two separate channels, one signal each — dissolves the tension that broke Options D (categorical 3-bucket, collapsed states + sport-coding), E (continuous opacity, imperceptible + verb-colour mismatch at overreach), and F-first-pass (glow threshold misaligned with verb threshold). **Implementation** (`src/lib/performanceColour.ts`): `if (deloadRecommended \|\| loadBand === "overreach") return { hue: THEME.amber, glowIntensity: 0 }; const glowIntensity = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (pi - 45) / 55)); return { hue: THEME.brand, glowIntensity };` **Verb ↔ stroke ↔ glow mapping**: Recovering (deload, PI<25) → brand purple, glow 0; Building (low, PI 25-44) → brand purple, glow 0; Cruising (moderate, PI 45-69) → brand purple, glow 0 → 0.44; Sharpening (high, PI 70-84) → brand purple, glow 0.45 → 0.71; Backing off (overreach OR deloadRecommended) → amber, glow 0. Above-target verbs have glow; below-target don't; Backing off suppresses glow (warnings don't celebrate). **Six spec amendments locked after stress-testing**: (1) **Animation API**: use `useMotionValue` + Framer Motion's `animate()` (NOT `useSpring` — takes stiffness/damping not duration); glow animates over 1.2s ease-out synchronized with the ring's stroke-dashoffset fill. (2) **Alpha notation**: `rgba(123, 114, 233, 0.21)` not `#7B72E935` for Safari ≤ 14 compatibility (Capacitor edge case). (3) **High-contrast mode explicit**: `@media (prefers-contrast: more)` renders solid stroke (no gradient) + `filter: none` (no glow, no drop-shadow); stroke colour alone carries verb-state in HCM. (4) **Reduced motion**: glow value updates instantly (no animation); stroke colour also instant; CountUp already respects reduced-motion via PI1's spec. (5) **Pre-launch QA pin**: verify no drop-shadow rendering jank on mid-range Android (Pixel 4a, Galaxy A52) — continuous `drop-shadow` filters can be GPU-expensive at lower tiers. (6) **Cross-surface coordination flag**: when PerformanceTab gets grilled (its "About Performance Index" disclosure per PI1, plus potentially its own Performance score visual), match the Home card's colour function — note in PI3 lock so future grills don't fork the visual language. **Trades consciously accepted**: (1) **Cruising verb gets multi-treatment within itself** — glow scales 0 → 0.44 across PI 45-69; same verb, different glow level; intentional two-channel design — verb is categorical, glow is continuous; NOT 1-1 verb-glow, only "has glow vs doesn't" is 1-1. (2) **Hard discontinuity at PI 85 (overreach boundary)** — PI 84 (brand + glow 0.71) → PI 85 (amber + no glow) is a big visual flip on 1 PI point; verb-driven (PI1 locked overreach → Backing off); rare peak-performer segment only; accept. (3) **Sport-coding visual stacking on Home** — WeekStrip uses brand purple for lift dots, Performance card uses brand purple stroke; visual hierarchy (24px ring vs 6px dots) differentiates them; acceptable. (4) **Recovering and Building share "no glow + brand purple stroke"** — differentiated by verb + supporting line + ring fill arc length; verb carries state distinction, colour doesn't try to. (5) **Dark mode glow more dramatic than light mode** (brand purple on #1A1A1F vs on white) — product call, feature not bug — dark-mode users get richer visual celebration. **Rationale for key choices**: brand purple chosen over a new "performance" token because Tropos's brand purple is used cross-cuttingly (streak flame, focus rings, Pro CTAs, tab indicators, brand wordmark) — not strictly sport-coded for lifting; PI is a hybrid meta-metric above sport-coding; simpler to use the existing brand colour, can add a Performance-specific token later if dogfooding shows confusion. Amber chosen over coral/red for Backing off because red/coral would scold (against calm-positioning); amber is informational warning matching Run7 Q10's amber-warning-banner pattern (Tropos has no red-alarm tokens by design per CLAUDE.md "no red banners" — errors are toasts not banners). Categorical 5-bucket palette rejected (Option C in grill) — 5 colours competing on a card with 5 elements is visual noise; verb taxonomy already carries the 5-state nuance, colour doesn't need to repeat. Continuous opacity-only gradient rejected (Option E in grill) — 4% opacity shift per 10 PI points is imperceptible at the 96px ring size; glow (drop-shadow blur radius) is far more visible continuous signal; Whoop Strain (cited "calm gradient" reference) actually scales hue + saturation not just opacity. **Stress-test pattern (4 rounds, decreasing yield)**: Round 1 (D categorical 3-bucket): sport-coding, collapsed states, threshold flips. Round 2 (E continuous opacity): verb-colour mismatch at overreach, imperceptibility. Round 3 (F glow at PI 50): verb-threshold misalignment (Cruising entry vs glow entry), timing issues. Round 4 (F-refined glow at PI 45): spec gaps (useSpring API, HCM behaviour), edge cases, accepted trade-offs. No new architectural problems after round 3; locked at round 4. **Scope**: ~1 hour total. New `src/lib/performanceColour.ts` (~25 lines); wire into the consolidated card's chrome (rename existing `getScoreColor` import → `getCardColour`, pass `(pi, loadBand, deloadRecommended)` instead of `(score)`, swap drop-shadow filter to use `glowIntensity * 10px`); add `@media (prefers-contrast: more)` rules. Plus pre-launch QA: drop-shadow jank check on mid-range Android. **Connections**: replaces `getScoreColor` from `src/lib/healthScore.ts` (deleted per PI1) AND the legacy band-colour pattern; aligns with PI1's locked verb taxonomy + deload override; coordinates with Run7 Q10's amber-warning-banner pattern (amber is shared semantic for "back off / warning" across surfaces — when both surfaces fire amber simultaneously they reinforce a single narrative, not compete); cross-surface coordination flag for the future PerformanceTab grill so its visual treatment matches Home. **Five Performance-arc questions remain ungrilled**: Home page layout adjustments; deep-link target reconciliation; InsightStrip future; prevHealthScore state cleanup; implementation rollout plan. | PI4     | Home page layout adjustments (drop-in PI hero; PerformanceCard slot deleted)                                   | **Fourth decision in the Performance arc** — closes the Home-page-layout question from PI1's ungrilled list. **Decision: Option A — drop-in replacement.** The consolidated PI hero card (per PI1) stays in HealthScoreCard's current slot (Home.tsx line 482, slot 6 in top-to-bottom layout). PerformanceCard's slot (line 491-500) is removed. Layout naturally collapses by one card via existing gap-4 spacing. All other surfaces (WeekStrip, DayPeekCard, TodayEnergy, StackedCTACards, InsightStrip, conditional surfaces) stay in current positions. **Resulting Home layout**: (1) Header — unchanged; (2) Trial/upgrade strip conditional — unchanged; (3) Coach marks conditional — unchanged; (4) Streak-at-risk nudge conditional — unchanged; (5) WeekStrip + DayPeekCard — unchanged; (6) **Consolidated PI hero card** replaces HealthScoreCard chrome, drives PI data; (7) DELETED (was PerformanceCard); (8) TodayEnergy — unchanged; (9) StackedCTACards (action pills + Weight/Steps tiles) — unchanged; (10) InsightStrip conditional on high/overreach/deload — unchanged. **Rationale**: (1) **Glance-friendly card first** — Home's primary use case is re-engagement glance; PI hero (single ring + verb + line + delta) is glance-friendly; TodayEnergy (calories + macros + targets + rings + insight chip + post-workout nudge) is detail; glance > detail for Home's open-and-look moment. (2) **Brand-identity reinforcement at every touch** — Tropos's "calm-adaptive" positioning makes PI the brand-differentiating signal; first hero card on Home reinforces brand identity at every re-engagement touch, not just acquisition. (3) **Smoother cognitive-load gradient** — A: WeekStrip (low) → PI hero (low) → TodayEnergy (moderate) → CTAs (low); gentle rise then drop. B: WeekStrip (low) → TodayEnergy (moderate) → PI hero (low) → CTAs (low); spike then dip. Calm-positioning favours the smoother gradient. (4) **Smoother visual rhythm** — A: thin → medium → tall → action; progressive height growth. B: thin → tall → medium → action; jumps then shrinks. (5) **Minimum change reduces regression risk** — PI1 + PI2 + PI3 already touch 5 files; adding a Home reorder increases "what might break" surface area; A keeps PI4 trivial. (6) **PI4 is reversible in minutes** — if post-launch dogfooding reveals macro-checking friction, flipping motion.div order is a one-line change. **Why NOT Option B (today-first)** — genuinely considered across the grill; B's case rested on speculative claims that didn't survive stress-testing: (a) "Reference apps put today-first" is true for today-only metrics (Apple rings, Whoop Recovery) but Tropos's PI is rolling 7-day; the analogue is Garmin Training Status or Strava CTL which live on dedicated tabs or below daily-status surfaces (Tropos doesn't have an equivalent daily-only summary card) — analogy is muddied; (b) "Locked daily-refresh principle favours B" is overclaim — PI1 Q1's locked principle was about METRIC SEMANTICS not card order; both A and B satisfy it; (c) "Most common first-paint task is checking macros" is speculation without data; equally plausible: glancing at streak/PI for re-engagement; macro-heavy users navigate to Food page directly; (d) "TodayEnergy = canonical daily-refresh" is overstated — multiple cards refresh daily after PI1 (PI rolling, Water, Weight, Steps, Energy); no unique elevation reason. **Oscillation as convergence signal** — grill produced A → B → A → A across 4 rounds. Flip-flop IS the convergence test — stress-testing exposes weak arguments on whichever side commitment is made. | PI5     | Implementation rollout plan (split PI1 into PI1a backend + PI1b frontend, no flag)                             | **Fifth decision in the Performance arc** — closes the "implementation rollout plan" question from PI1's ungrilled list. **Decision: Option K — split PI1 into PI1a (backend + types + utility) and PI1b (frontend + deletions + Home layout). No feature flag. Backwards-compat at both layers via defensive defaults. Sequential merges deliver staged visibility for free.** **Retracts PI1's locked-spec language about "new card hidden behind feature flag until backfill completes; flag removed post-rollout"** — that line was generic-playbook copy and didn't grapple with PI1's wholesale-deletion design making flag-based gating functionally useless (no fallback state to gate to, because the old card is deleted). **Convergence story (3 grill rounds)**: Round 1 proposed C+F (per-user flag + backwards-compat); stress-test found the flag has no meaningful fallback state because PI1 deletes the old card. Round 3 proposed K (split into PI1a + PI1b, no flag, backwards-compat at both layers); each prior round's mega-PR defense got weaker; stress tests kept validating the split. **PI1a — Backend + types (~0.5-1 day, first PR)**: CF rewrite in functions/performanceEngine.js (rolling 7-day window with prior-28-day baseline, daily compute trigger, on-write triggers + daily cron per PI1 lock);
