| Hist5   | History page consolidation to Analytics frame                                                                  | **Page IA arc, eighth grill — first post-Run7 refinement, opens History/Analytics sub-arc.** User flagged "history page slash analytics page" — page identity itself was unresolved. 4 sub-questions stress-tested across 60 cumulative attacks (Q2 ×12, Q3 ×20, Q4 ×40). **Surface inventory**: 6 tabs (`all/running/lifting/nutrition/performance/badges`), TimeRangePills (1W/1M/3M/6M/1Y), WeeklyOverview hero (3 rings), Running section (Distance + Pace stat cards, Running PRs, ShoeMileage, RunningHistorySection), Lifting section (Volume + Sessions stat cards, VolumeChart, MuscleHeatMap, Lift PRs), Nutrition section (Adherence row + macro stat cards, MacroDistribution donut, TrendWeight, CalorieBalanceChart), Lifetime totals. **Reference apps**: Strava (Profile recent feed + Training analytics — split), Garmin Connect (Calendar log + Performance analytics — split), MyFitnessPal (Diary + Reports — split), Hevy (Profile history list + Stats + separate all-time PRs tab — split), NRC (Activity + Stats — split). **Pattern: fitness apps universally split history-as-log from analytics-as-dashboard. Tropos's conflation is the exception.** PRs always sit on a SEPARATE surface in best-in-class apps. Thin-data suppression converges on "suppress decorations below density thresholds; raw values always shown" (Hevy ≥4wk, NRC ≥4 activities, MacroFactor explicit caveats). **Hist5a → B (commit to Analytics frame, keep one page) with seven pins**. Renaming to a separate `/analytics` route costs deep-link breakage + bottom-nav slot economics; keeping current `/history` URL + nav label is correct. Page title becomes "Analytics" (frame commitment); URL + nav unchanged. Reversible if usage data later flips. Pins: (1) **URL stays `/history`** — backward-compatible deep-links preserved; (2) **Bottom-nav label stays "History"** — established short label; (3) **Page title inside is the frame statement** (separate from URL identity); (4) **No `/analytics/X` nested route precedent** — drill-downs are inline expansion or peer routes; (5) **PR #635's `/history#performance` deep-link target unchanged**; (6) **Performance hero on Home stays the glanceable surface** — Analytics surface is compact/inline ring, not duplicate hero; (7) **Hist5 is the eighth Page IA grill** — opens post-consolidation refinement sub-arc, NOT a close of Page IA. **Hist5b → 3-tab structure (Analytics / PRs / Badges) following reference apps with eight pins**. Initial recommendation was 2 tabs (Analytics + Badges) but Stress 12+ revealed PR mismatch — strict TimeRange + embedded all-time PRs creates sublabel sprawl. Reference apps universally SPLIT PRs to a dedicated surface. Drop the 3 sport-filtered tabs (`running/lifting/nutrition`) — pure noise filters. Fold Performance into Analytics as compact strip + inline accordion expansion. Pins: (1) **Sticky anchor chip row at top with scroll-spy** using IntersectionObserver (not static offsets) — replaces dropped sport-filtered tabs; (2) **Only ONE sticky element above content** — chip row sticky; TimeRangePills, tabs, offline-banner all non-sticky to avoid iOS Safari drift compound (Layout.tsx PWA Safeguard 2 already handles single-element drift; stacking risks regression); (3) **Performance = compact ring/strip on Analytics + inline accordion expansion** — NO drawer, NO new route, URL hash `#performance-expanded` for refresh-safety; (4) **PRs tab has Lifetime + Recent-bests subsections** — Lifetime unit-true (overwrites on improvement; progression timeline via drill-down to existing `/history/exercise/<name>`); Recent bests rolling 30-day, sublabeled; (5) **PRs tab includes Indoor/treadmill PRs** (separately tracked) so treadmill-only users aren't permanently empty; "Outdoor GPS only" exclusion lifted; (6) **PRs cold-state is designed onboarding**, not fallback — empty-state CTA + return-link toast on PR-eligible save closes the loop; (7) **PRs tab two sport-coded sections** (Running coral section + Lift purple section) — sport identity preserved at section level after migration off sport-filtered tabs; (8) **Badges tab is interim placement** — migrates to Profile alongside PRs + Lifetime when Profile arc lands (no Profile route exists yet; interim caveat documented). **Hist5c → reference-app strict global TimeRange + tier carve-outs with eleven pins**. Initial three-tier sublabel discipline (Option B) was preserving the problem; revised to reference-app pattern — PRs OFF Analytics, strict global TimeRange honoured by everything remaining. Tier 1 = TimeRange-honouring (stat cards, VolumeChart, MuscleHeatMap, MacroDistribution, adherence). Tier 2 = always-lifetime/current (PRs tab, Lifetime totals, Performance hero "Current week" label). Carve-outs justified individually with explicit sublabels. Pins: (1) **Strict global TimeRange honoured by every Analytics surface** unless explicitly Tier 2 labeled; (2) **WeeklyOverview renamed PeriodOverview** — rings auto-scale targets ("Past week / Past month / Past 3M / Past 6M / Past year"); (3) **TrendWeight projection suppressed at TimeRange < 1M OR < 5 weight points** — chart display honours TimeRange; EWMA model uses full history with explicit sublabel "Trending value uses full weight history"; (4) **CalorieBalance 14-day window is Tier 3 carve-out** — metabolic adaptation window baked into adaptiveTDEE; sublabel "Trailing 14 days · matches adaptive-TDEE window"; (5) **CalorieBalance phase-aware framing fix (audit E1 — biggest UX bug surfaced)** — Bulk+deficit conflict renders amber "at odds with your phase" message, NOT contradictory raw lines; full phase × actual-trend reconciliation table; (6) **Lift PRs "Last 7 days" hardcode removed** — PRs moved off Analytics to dedicated PRs tab (Tier 2 lifetime); (7) **Adaptive chart granularity by TimeRange** — daily bars 1W-1M, weekly bars 3M, monthly bars 6M-1Y; (8) **MuscleHeatMap shades by relative-volume share** (normalized % within window), not absolute volume — survives 1Y windows without saturating; (9) **Adherence warning has sample-size guard** — suppresses at very short windows or very low log count; (10) **TimeRange URL-persists across tab switches** (inherits Hist4's `?range=` URL contract); (11) **URL redirect map** — legacy `?tab=running/lifting/nutrition/all` → `?tab=analytics`; `?tab=performance` → `?tab=analytics#performance`. **Hist5d → unified data-confidence tier system with twelve pins**. Today nutrition section is the only surface with thin-data suppression (`showSparklines`/`showDelta`); lifting/running/macros/weight confidently show decorations regardless of N. Result: same page treats data-density inconsistently. New shared `dataConfidence.ts` utility consumed by every surface — single source of truth. T0 raw values always shown; T1 sparkline gated on ≥4 distinct days; T2 vs-last delta gated on ≥4 in both windows (rolling prior, not calendar-aligned); T3 trend projection gated on ≥1M window + ≥5 points; T4 donut gated on ≥7 logged days (absolute count, NOT adherence %); T5 bar charts gated on ≥3 bars (omit when fewer, no substitute). Pins: (1) **Threshold numbers are v1 best-guesses** — documented as such in lib header; telemetry-driven tuning post-launch; (2) **Per-metric correct units** — distinct days (sport), logged days (nutrition), data points (weight); never OR'd alternatives; (3) **Raw numbers always shown** — suppression only abstracts visual decorations; sometimes the raw number IS the bad signal (over-calorie days); donut suppression doesn't hide it; (4) **Ghost-preview = `bg-muted` background + caveat copy below** — NO dashed border, NO diagonal stripes, NO opacity tricks; uses existing design system vocabulary; opacity treatments rejected after stress-testing (colour desaturation defeats info, fails `prefers-contrast: more` / `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`); (5) **a11y fallback to boxed empty-state** under `prefers-contrast: more` / `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce` — same suppression copy, no decorative treatment; (6) **Suppression copy is single muted ≤30-char line** (English v1 budget; i18n re-evaluates per language at i18n arc); (7) **Suppression copy frames patience for time-gated decorations** ("Building trend · check back") + **action for activity-gated** ("Log first run") — time can't be hurried, activity can; (8) **Computed ETA when current-rate can predict** ("Trending in ~22 days") — falls back to generic "keep logging" when rate is 0; (9) **Stat cards have fixed outer height** regardless of decoration state — suppressed sparkline area becomes whitespace; no card-height jitter across rows; (10) **Threshold-cross renders cross-fade** (caveat fades out, decoration fades in) over 200ms; NO celebratory toast on suppression-release — too aggressive for passive threshold cross; (11) **Server-side PI `confidence` field maps to three explicit UI degradations** (high → full hero + sub-scores + accordion; medium → hero + sub-scores muted; low → PI number alone + "Establishing baseline") PLUS surface-level sanity check (`pi > 0 && all sub-scores > 0`) — engine artefacts treated as low-confidence in UI regardless of stored `confidence`; (12) **Suppression telemetry batched per page-load** — single `analytics_decorations_suppressed` event with array payload `suppressions: [{decoration, surface, reason, points}, ...]`, NOT per-decoration events; quota-safe. **Cross-cutting (5 pins)**: (1) **Q2-style sport-segment auto-hide composes with Q4 decoration suppression** — section-level visibility decision precedes card-level suppression; never conflicts; full sections render → per-card T-tier applies; section hidden entirely → T-tier doesn't get a chance; (2) **Recent activity surface is item-capped ("Last 10 activities"), not TimeRange-scoped** — Tier 2 with hard item cap; tap "View all" → `/history/log` (drill-down route for the event-log spine); (3) **Share card generator respects T-tier suppression** — share button GATES on confidence (≥50% decorations rendering required before user can share); thin-data share cards render with caveat instead of misleading viz; (4) **Prior-window definition is rolling-back-by-windowDays**, NOT calendar-aligned — composes cleanly with arbitrary TimeRange picks; no calendar-boundary edge cases; (5) **`dataConfidence.ts` has stable extensible API; surface hooks own per-surface wrappers** — avoids god-utility coupling without losing unified-policy benefit; new decorations added as optional return fields (backwards-compatible). **Critical implications**: (1) **Tabs go 6 → 3** (Analytics / PRs / Badges) — drops sport-filtered noise filters; (2) **PRs migrate from embedded sport sections to dedicated tab** — Tier 2 lifetime contract honoured at tab level; (3) **TrendWeight projection suppression + adaptive chart granularity + MuscleHeatMap normalisation** = three concrete chart bugs fixed; (4) **CalorieBalance phase-aware framing fixes audit E1** — the single biggest UX bug surfaced by the audit; (5) **Performance fold into Analytics + inline accordion expansion** — eliminates dedicated Performance tab; deep-links continue to `/history#performance` via anchor; (6) **Shared `dataConfidence.ts` utility** — new module + surface-hook wrappers + telemetry instrumentation; (7) **Cold-start uses ghost-preview placeholders + onboarding-quality empty states**, not blank suppression — first-day UX explicitly designed (Stress 6 + Stress 9 + Stress 19 all converge here); (8) **Threshold numbers documented as v1 best-guesses** with telemetry-driven post-launch tuning; (9) **Bucket-1 vs Bucket-2 vs Bucket-3 honest framing**: 8 items are unambiguous bug fixes (CalorieBalance phase contradiction, TrendWeight projection lying at 1W, VolumeChart unreadable at 1Y with 52 bars, MuscleHeatMap saturation, Lift PRs "Last 7 days" mismatch, empty-section dead-space CTAs, WeeklyOverview label hardcode, adherence false-alarm at small N); 4 items are structural bets (tab consolidation 6→3, PRs split to dedicated tab, Performance fold into Analytics, frame rename to Analytics in title); 6 items are plumbing (URL redirects, IntersectionObserver scroll-spy, telemetry batching, Lifetime/Badges/PRs provisional placement comments, dataConfidence shared util, surface-hook wrappers); | S4e     | Restricted-user MVP (manual admin restriction, deferred automation)                                            | **Sub-decision in the S4 arc — closes the moderation-MVP gap surfaced by the 2026-05-24 Soc5+Food6 audit.** Soc5 #15 (Find-tab restricted-user gate) and Food6 F3 (verify food-logging not gated by restriction) both blocked on a backing store + client read path that S4d's critical implications (3, 7, 8) specced but never implemented. **Decision: Option B from 50-round stress test — minimum viable restriction with manual admin trigger, deferred strike-counter + auto-lift + write-time rules enforcement.** **S4d-original mismatch.** S4d pin (8) specs "Cloud Functions check this collection before accepting kudos/comment/share-to-crew operations." Tropos has no such CFs — `toggleKudos`, `addDoc(comments/...)`, activity creation are direct client-side Firestore writes via `socialApi.ts`. The locked architecture didn't match the built architecture. S4e accepts this mismatch by deferring write-time enforcement entirely; restriction is enforced via UI gate only. Same shape of problem as the Hist5 lock recovery — the architectural truth shifted after the lock was written, and rather than retrofit the lock we acknowledge the gap and reframe. **Scope (~3-4 hr + ~30-45min admin-UI extension):** (1) `globalRestrictedUids/{uid}` Firestore collection per S4d critical implication (3) schema: `{ uid, restrictedAt, restrictionEndsAt, lastActionedReport, strikes: number }`. S4e writes `restrictedAt` + `lastActionedReport` only; `restrictionEndsAt: null` + `strikes: null` signal "manually restricted via admin action, not auto-strike" — schema forward-compatible with future S4d-full where strikes/endsAt are populated. (2) Firestore rules for the collection: `match /globalRestrictedUids/{uid} { allow read: if request.auth.uid == uid; allow write: if false; }` — Admin SDK writes only; user can only read own status (no cross-user restriction discovery). (3) Client hook `useRestrictedStatus(uid)` modelled on `useBlockedUsers` — module-level cache to avoid redundant reads across re-mounts; onSnapshot for reactive updates when admin lifts mid-session. (4) Soc5 #15 UI gate on Find tab: disabled state on search input + each `FollowButton` + invite-link share button; restriction banner copy "Your account is restricted · Contact support" per Soc5a-pin-2 lock. (5) Admin-side extension: `resolveReport` Cloud Function gains optional `restrictUser?: boolean` field; when true, atomically writes to `globalRestrictedUids/{targetUid}` via Firestore batch alongside the report-resolution. Admin queue UI (`src/pages/AdminModeration.tsx` lines 232-252) gains a third button "Restrict user" alongside existing Dismiss + Hide content — currently has TWO buttons only (verified pre-lock). Audit-log via existing `functions/auditLog.js`. **Six deferred items (must close before public launch unless explicitly punted again):** (D1) **Write-time enforcement** — restricted user can still bypass UI gate via direct Firestore writes to `kudos`, `comments`, `activities`, `following`. Pre-launch with one user (who is the operator) this is acceptable; post-launch it's a hole. **Closure path:** add `!exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/globalRestrictedUids/$(request.auth.uid))` predicate to the relevant Firestore rules (activities create, kudos/comment subcollection writes) — adds 1 extra Firestore read per write; cost trade-off acceptable for the security gain. Alternative: custom claims via Firebase Auth (no extra reads, but slow token-refresh propagation). Pick one in S4f or whenever this closes. (D2) **Strike-counter Cloud Function** — auto-restrict at 3 actioned reports per S4d pin (5). Defer because pre-launch volume is zero. **Closure trigger:** moderation queue exceeds N actions/week where manual restriction becomes the bottleneck. (D3) **30-day auto-lift scheduled CF** — admin must manually delete from collection. Risks soft permaban via admin forgetfulness; "Contact support" copy is the user's recourse. **Closure path:** scheduled `pubsub` CF that deletes docs where `restrictionEndsAt < now`. (D4) **Crews tab Join action gating** — S4e narrow scope (Find tab only per Soc5 #15 lock). Restricted user can still join crews. Spec drift vs S4d-original "share-to-crews" gating; consistent with Soc5 #15 surface-list. **Closure path:** extend UI gate to Crews tab Join + Crew page Join (`src/pages/Crew.tsx`); add to Soc5 punch list as item #16. (D5) **Kudos / comments UI gating** — S4d-original specced these; S4e doesn't gate them in UI even though backend rules deferral (D1) means they're not blocked anyway. **Closure path:** disable the kudos heart and comment input on `ActivityCard` when `useRestrictedStatus(currentUid).isRestricted`. Bundle with D1 closure. (D6) **Settings → "Why am I restricted?" link** per S4d critical implication (9). S4e ships "Contact support" copy in the gate as the only restriction-explanation surface. **Closure path:** add accordion section to `src/components/settings/PrivacySection.tsx` that renders when `useRestrictedStatus(currentUid).isRestricted`; copy explains the strike system + 30-day window once strike-counter (D2) ships. **Implementation pins (15):** **(P1)** Schema's `strikes: null` + `restrictionEndsAt: null` is the in-band signal for "manually restricted". S4d-full's auto-write populates both — the same hook reads both shapes correctly because `isRestricted = doc exists` regardless of field values. **(P2)** Module-level cache pattern: `useRestrictedStatus` mirrors `useBlockedUsers`' approach — one onSnapshot subscription per UID, results cached in module scope so multiple component instances share the read. Saves 1 read per re-mount. **(P3)** Doc-absence = not-restricted: hook returns `{ isRestricted: false, loading: false }` when snapshot is empty. Don't render a doc per non-restricted user (would be 1M-user-scale read amplification). **(P4)** Atomicity: `resolveReport` extension uses Firestore batch — `reports/{id}` status update + optional `globalRestrictedUids/{targetUid}` create succeed-or-fail together. Per stress-test attack #8. **(P5)** No write-time rules enforcement in S4e (per D1). The new `globalRestrictedUids` rules in scope item (2) cover doc readability/writability only, not the consuming-collection write paths. **(P6)** Repeat-offender audit trail (lift → re-restrict cycle) loses history because S4e writes the same doc on re-restriction. Deferred to a `globalRestrictedUids/{uid}/history` subcollection if/when pattern detection matters. Per stress-test attack #4. **(P7)** Offline UX: restricted users may briefly see "not restricted" UI from Firestore offline cache; on reconnect, hook fires and UI updates. With D1 not closed, offline writes succeed regardless — accept this pre-launch. **(P8)** Race: admin restricts while user is mid-write. Write succeeds (D1 deferred), gate appears next Find-tab mount. Acceptable for MVP. **(P9)** Concurrent admin restrict+lift: last-write-wins on the doc. Acceptable at single-digit admin count. **(P10)** Mid-typing search input: restriction state can flip while user is typing → input becomes disabled. Loss of typed input is a minor annoyance; no special handling beyond standard React controlled-input semantics. **(P11)** Restricted user's PROFILE remains editable (display name, bio, photo) — user can fix any offending bio that triggered restriction. Restriction is forward-looking-social only. **(P12)** Restricted user's existing kudos / activities preserved per S4d intent ("restriction is not a content nuke"). Self-feed view of own already-flagged content uses the existing "Under review" placeholder per S4d critical implication (10). **(P13)** Telemetry: fire `social_restricted_gate_shown` event on every Find-tab mount where the gate renders; add to `src/lib/socialAnalytics.ts` event union. Per stress-test attack #40. **(P14)** Smart-default precedence: if a new user with smart-default-to-Find-tab is restricted (unusual cold-start case), the restriction gate copy fully overrides Soc5c's coachmark. Per stress-test attack #45. **(P15)** Read-only suggestion list: restricted user can still SEE suggestions (`useSuggestedPeople` is read-only); only inline FollowButton is disabled. Per stress-test attack #46. **R1A intersection:** account deletion must hard-delete `/globalRestrictedUids/{uid}` when present. `functions/accountDeletionInventory.json` has ZERO references to this collection today (verified pre-lock). MUST be added to the R1A inventory in same PR as S4e implementation. Per stress-test attack #30. **Connections:** Unblocks Soc5 #15 (the original Soc5-audit punch-list blocker — see Soc5 STATUS line). Resolves Food6 F3 by inheritance (food logging stays not-gated under S4e, matching the locked spec). Builds on S4a (blocking) + S4b (two-tier reports) + S4c (three-checkbox modal) + S4d-implementation-shipped-pieces (reports collection, listPendingReports, resolveReport, profanityFilter, BlockAwareAvatar, useBlockedUsers, ReportModal). Soc5's existing UI surface gets the gate; no new pages. No Watch impact (W7 APNs routing; restrictions don't fire user-visible Watch notifications). No PR-L impact. **Out of scope / NEGATIVE-SPACE:** (N1) **Restricted-user badge on profiles visible to OTHER users** per S4d pin (5) — defer indefinitely. Tropos's calm-positioning rejects scarlet-letter UX. Re-evaluation trigger: only if a legit business case emerges (e.g. legal compliance signal). (N2) **Cross-device sync of restriction status** — relies on Firestore's standard onSnapshot real-time propagation. No special cross-device coordination layer. **Re-trigger to upgrade S4e → S4d-full:** (T1) ANY of the six deferred items causes a real-world incident → close that specific item, don't blanket-promote to S4d. (T2) Moderation volume reaches N actions/week where manual flow bottlenecks → ship D2 (strike-counter CF). (T3) Pre-public-launch checklist — D1 (write-time enforcement) MUST be closed before public launch unless explicitly re-locked-as-deferred with named-owner sign-off. | Hist5e  | Custom date range (NOT pursued — negative-space)                                                               | **Negative-space decision in the History/Analytics arc.** Formalises the implicit dissolution Hist5 already made: the original Hist4b-pin-2/3 custom-range picker + `?from=&to=` URL contract was superseded — without explicit acknowledgement — when Hist5c (60-attack stress-tested grill) adopted strict global TimeRange with tier carve-outs. **Decision: lock as negative-space rather than building or leaving ambiguous.** **What Tropos WILL ship (affirmative scope per Hist5c).** Five fixed `TimeRangePills` (1W/1M/3M/6M/1Y) per `src/components/analytics/TimeRangePills.tsx`. URL contract is `?range=<pill>` per Hist5c-pin-10 (inheriting from Hist4). Strict global TimeRange honoured by every Analytics surface per Hist5c-pin-1 unless explicitly Tier 2 labeled. **What this lock makes explicit-NOT-shipping.** (a) Custom-range pill / calendar-picker sheet (the Hist4b-pin-2/3 feature). (b) `?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD` URL contract — orthogonal to the Hist5c-pin-10 `?range=` contract; the `?from=&to=` shape is dead by Hist5 supersession, not by oversight. (c) Capacitor `UIDatePicker` integration (the Hist4b iOS-native picker hook). (d) Custom-range telemetry variant (`history_range_changed` with bucketed-dates payload). **Source of dissolution.** Hist5 lock body (commit `1aaa7bb`, recovered to main via PR #720) contains ZERO references to "custom range," "date picker," `?from=`, or `?to=` across 4 sub-decisions + 60+ stress-test attacks + 11 Hist5c pins + critical implications. The Hist5c-pin-1 "strict global TimeRange" + Hist5c-pin-10 "inherits `?range=`" pair locks the contract to fixed pills only. The dissolution was implicit but architecturally load-bearing: Hist5d's unified `dataConfidence.ts` thresholds (T1=4pts, T2=4+4pts, T3=30d+5pts, T4=7days, T5=3bars) assume fixed-bucket windows; arbitrary user-chosen ranges would invalidate the bucket-derived defaults. **Reference-app grounding (50/50-ish split).** Apps WITH custom range: Strava (Premium-gated — even Strava treats it as power-user not table-stakes), MyFitnessPal (buried in reports), Cronometer (calendar), Garmin Connect (rich calendar — but Garmin is the explicit opposite of Tropos's calm-positioning). Apps WITHOUT: Nike Run Club, Hevy, Strong, MacroFactor (period-only), Apple Fitness (Day/Week/Month/Year navigation but no arbitrary from-to). Tropos's calm-positioning aligns with the second cohort. Note: reference-app claims here are from grill-session knowledge; if a future grill needs higher-fidelity competitor data, dedicate a `/browse` pass to verify. **Known accepted limitation.** Week-boundary alignment (e.g. "last 7 days ending Saturday" for users on Sunday-Monday training-week convention) has NO workaround in the fixed-pills design — `1W` is calendar-rolling from today. Accepted for v1. **Re-evaluation trigger:** if telemetry or support volume shows users specifically requesting week-boundary alignment (distinct from generic "more range options"), this single use-case may warrant a narrow opt-in (e.g. Settings → "Training week starts on Sunday/Monday") WITHOUT broadening to full custom-range. **Re-evaluation triggers (general).** (T1) Substantial user-request signal — same vague-by-design wording as F4 voice-food + Food6 recipe/templating negative-space items; thresholds intentionally not quantified to avoid gaming. Measurement mechanisms when available: support tickets, app-store reviews, in-app feedback. (T2) Export feature (CSV/PDF) launches — exports legitimately need user-chosen ranges; if export ships, custom-range becomes a real Hist5e re-grill question. (T3) Pro-tier scope amendment (Sub2) — Hist5e doesn't lock out the Strava pattern of "custom range as Pro feature." A future Sub2 amendment proposing custom range as a Pro carrot would re-open this question. (T4) Week-boundary alignment as a narrow opt-in (per known limitation above) — narrower than full re-grill. **Pins:** **(P1)** Cite Hist5c-pin-1 ("strict global TimeRange") and Hist5c-pin-10 ("inherits Hist4's `?range=` URL contract") as the load-bearing references for the dissolution. Not citing makes the lock body unanchored. **(P2)** Negative-space is dissolvable, NOT a permanent ban. Mirror Food6's F4 framing: "if substantial user-request signal emerges, this re-opens." Locked-as-not-pursued ≠ rejected-as-harmful. **(P3)** `?from=&to=` URL contract is also negative-space (not just the picker UI). If a user pastes such a URL from elsewhere, React Router silently ignores the unknown params — no error, no validation, no fallback messaging. Standard browser-router behaviour, intentionally not special-cased. **(P4)** Pre-launch caveat acknowledged. Locking negative-space pre-launch with one user has a real "unfalsifiable signal-absence" weakness. This lock's rationale rests on Hist5c's 60-attack stress test (a real design exercise) and reference-app convergence patterns — NOT on "we don't see user requests yet." Per CLAUDE.md "Reject reasoning that appeals to single-user transience." **(P5)** Hist4 row gets a STATUS line in the same PR noting H1 + H4 (audit punch-list items: custom date range + `?from=&to=` URL contract) are SUPERSEDED-BY-HIST5E, not unshipped-by-oversight. Closes the audit-vs-lock loop. **(P6)** No Sub2 amendment from this lock. Sub2 (Pro feature scope) doesn't mention custom range today; Hist5e doesn't require touching Sub2. T3 above is the only Sub2-relevant future path. **(P7)** No R1A intersection — negative-space items have no data model. **(P8)** No Watch / PR-L / Programme impact — TimeRange is web/iOS analytics surface only. **(P9)** E2E tests verified clean of custom-range assumptions (`grep -rn 'from=\|fromDate\|date-picker\|customRange' e2e/` → empty pre-lock). No regression surface to monitor. **(P10)** If a future grill DOES re-open this (per T1-T4), the upgrade path is a new locked decision (`Hist6` or similar) superseding Hist5e — same shape as Hist5 superseding parts of Hist4. NOT an in-place edit to Hist5e. **Methodology:** 50-round stress-test against Option C (negative-space lock) during the post-S4e grill session. Convergence around attack #30. 2 ❌ found: (a) unfalsifiable signal-absence claim — addressed by P4 (rationale shifts from "no signal" to "Hist5's 60-attack grill already decided"); (b) week-boundary alignment as a real persistent gap — addressed by known-limitation section + T4 re-evaluation trigger. 20+ pins captured. No architectural showstoppers; the lock does the job lock-discipline asks of it (making an implicit decision discoverable). **Closes:** Audit punch-list items Hist4 H1 (custom date range picker) and Hist4 H4 (deep-link URL contract mismatch). Both are now "dead by Hist5 supersession" not "unshipped pins." Defer until telemetry OR benchmark shows actual lag at realistic max item counts. **Re-evaluation triggers (T1-T4):** (T1)`food_meal_slot_perf`telemetry shows P95`renderDurationMs > 100`across N+ users within first 6 weeks of public launch. Thresholds vague-by-design per Hist5f / F4 / Food6 negative-space convention. If benchmark shows no perceptible lag even at 200 items, F2 promotes to permanent negative-space in a future Food6f lock; if benchmark shows real lag, T2 fires immediately. | PR-J-Q1 | Completion-detection rule for the soft-link reframe (replaces stored `completed_*` statuses with a derivation) | **Picked (d'') — date-tolerant distance match with quality-bucket guard, race-day exact, single-claim resolution; legacy values readable, no migration write; `expired` derives; skipped is reversible.** **Match rule (the predicate).** A saved run completes a planned runDay slot when ALL of: (1) `saved.date ∈ [planned.date, planned.date + 1]` — same calendar day OR day-late only. NEVER day-early (prevents Mon-pulling-Tue pre-emption). (2) `saved.distance ≥ 0.7 × planned.distance`. (3) EITHER the scheduled template is non-quality (easy / long / recovery / shake-out), OR the saved run's avgPace bucket from `paceTrends.ts` matches the expected bucket for the quality type (intervals / tempo / race). Pure-distance doesn't satisfy a quality session. (4) The saved run has not already been "claimed" by another slot. Resolution order: same-date slots first, then date+1 slots; within a date, by `dayIndex` ascending. A claimed saved run can't simultaneously credit two slots. **Race-day carve-out.** Race-day runDays require BOTH `templateId === "race"` on the saved run (which RunSummary writes when started via `?scheduledRunId=...` linking to the race) AND distance ≥ 95% of planned. Recovery entry fires ONLY on this strict match — never on the loose rule. Closes stress-test #12 (DNF triggers recovery) + #14 (substitute long run on cancelled race day). **Stored statuses post-J.** Only `planned The `completed*_`triple goes away.`expired` is DERIVED at read time (`status === "planned" && date < today − 7 days && no saved run claimed`), NOT stored — the plan file's framing of `expired`as a stored value was inconsistent with "completion is derived" and is corrected here.  **Skipped is reversible.** Legal transitions become:`planned → skipped`, `skipped → planned`, `planned → race*no_show`, `race_no_show → planned`. No transitions into a "completed" state because completed isn't stored anymore.  **Migration.** Type widens to accept legacy `"completed_exact" \| "completed_modified" \| "completed_late"` as readable values. The reader treats them as "derived completion holds" — the day shows ✅ in UI regardless of whether the corresponding saved run still exists. No migration write — existing data stays correct, the new derivation runs forward. Closes #15, #16 by not touching the past.  **`linkedRunId`removal.** Dropped from`ScheduledRunDay`type. The "missed-detection" guard at`programTypes.ts:172`that read`!linkedRunId`is rewritten to use date + saved-run-presence directly. The "tap completed run → view saved run" navigation hook that the field was reserved for is deferred — when needed, recompute the link at click time from (runDay.date, runDay.templateId) → saved-run lookup.  **Stress-test summary.** Survives 40 scenarios across two rounds. Known accepted regressions: (a) Day-late completion is kept (capped at +1 day; reference apps cap there too). (b) User deletes saved run → day flips back to "planned" in UI; surface a one-time toast "Run deleted — your training history was updated." (c) Race-recovery latency shifts from "instant on completeRunDay" to "next-app-open detection." Plan accepts this; recovery is multi-day state, not seconds-critical.  **Pre-implementation budget item.** Audit`streaks` (`useStreaks.ts`), `performanceEngine`(weekly rollups),`badges` (`features/streaks/badges.ts`), History page, and any adherence-scoring sites for consumers of the dropped `completed*_`enum values BEFORE writing the PR-J ticket. Itemise the find/fix surface so the PR scope is honest. The plan file's PR-J line implied a small change; the surface is larger —`RunWeekStrip.tsx:102-104`, `ProgrammeRunSection.tsx:227`, `DayPeekCard.tsx:127`, `DayActionSheet.tsx:156`, `planBuilder.ts:230-235`, `migrations.ts:104`, `useProgram.ts:802-898 (completeRunDay)`+ ~327 (race-no-show effect) are confirmed touchpoints.  **Reference-app alignment.** Strava + NRC + Garmin all do invisible date-tolerant completion linking. Tolerance window of +1 day matches Strava's "assign to yesterday" affordance. Bucket guard for quality sessions matches TrainingPeaks' workout-type detection.  **Pins (locked).** **(P1)** Date window is`[planned.date, planned.date + 1]`, asymmetric (no day-early). **(P2)** Distance threshold is 70%. **(P3)** Quality templates require pace-bucket match; non-quality (easy / long / recovery) accept distance-only. **(P4)** Race day requires `templateId === "race"`on saved run + ≥95% distance. Recovery entry fires ONLY here. **(P5)** Single-claim rule — a saved run credits ≤1 slot. Resolution: same-date first, then date+1; within a date, by`dayIndex`. **(P6)** `expired`is derived, not stored. Threshold:`date < today − 7d && no saved run claimed`. **(P7)** `skipped → planned`is a legal transition (skip is reversible). **(P8)** Legacy`completed*\*`enum values stay readable forever; no migration write. **(P9)**`linkedRunId`field removed from the`ScheduledRunDay`type. **(P10)** Recovery entry shifts from instant (in`completeRunDay`) to deferred (effect on app open). Accepted regression.  **Open downstream questions (will grill in follow-up rounds before PR-J ships).** (Q2) What does `completeRunDay`become — does it still exist, or is it deleted entirely? If deleted, what writes`runPlan.phase = "recovery"`? (Q3) How are the cross-feature consumers (streaks / Performance Index / badges / adherence) refactored? Inline derivation vs shared helper? (Q4) Test fixture refactor strategy — touch all fixtures or write a legacy-compat helper? (Q5) UX surface for the "extra run" case (saved run that doesn't claim any slot)? (Q6) Strava sync arriving days late — does derivation re-run on every read, or do we cache the claim? (Q7) Saved-run deletion UI — exact copy + toast trigger? (Q8) Migration timing — does the type widening land in PR-J or as a precursor?  **Methodology.** Two rounds × 20 stress-tests (40 total). Revised to (d') with quality-bucket guard + race-day exact + single-claim. Round 2 attacked (d') and surfaced ±1 day directionality, expired-stored contradiction, skipped one-way door, cross-feature consumer audit gap. Final form (d'') resolves all surfaced issues except three acknowledged regressions (above).  **Connections.** First locked decision in the PR-J arc. | PR-J-Q2 | Disposition of `completeRunDay` + manual mark-complete mechanism in the soft-link reframe                      | **Picked (a'''') — delete `completeRunDay` entirely; manual mark-complete writes a `manualCompletions` map under `programState`; derivation reads three branches (saved-run match, manual entry, legacy status).** **What goes away.** `completeRunDay` at `useProgram.ts:802-898` is deleted. The two responsibilities it carried split: (1) Recovery-entry side effect moves to a new `useProgram` effect keyed on derived race-day match. (2) Week-complete celebration toast moves to a new effect watching derived completion of `runDays + workouts`, with a session-scoped `firedForWeek: weekKey` ref guard. The function's third concern — writing `runDay.status` + `linkedRunId` — was already removed by Q1. **What replaces "Mark complete (manual)".** Q2's hardest sub-question. Synthetic-saved-run write (initial recommendation `a`) was broken — would pollute social fan-out, challenge progress, streaks, Performance Index, health score, history, and onboarding (rejected after 7+ stress-test failures #1-#7 + #20). Settled on: `programState.manualCompletions: Record<runDayId, { completedAt: Timestamp }>` — a map of explicit user intent to mark a slot complete without a saved run. Derivation reads alongside saved-run matches. **No fake saved-run write.** Q1's "completion is derived, never stored" framing survives: status is derived; inputs (saved runs, manual intent, legacy status) are stored — same pattern as `skipped`. **Derivation formula (P27 — load-bearing).** `isComplete(runDay) = matchingSavedRun(runDay) \|\| manualCompletions[runDay.id] != null \|\| isLegacyCompleted(runDay.status)`. Three branches. `isLegacyCompleted` returns true for `"completed_exact" \| "completed_modified" \| "completed_late"` OR for `completed === true` on pre-status legacy docs. Without the legacy branch, archived weeks silently lose their ✅ — surfaced by Round 3 stress #45-#46. **DayActionSheet "Mark complete (manual)" behaviour.** On `planned` runDay: writes `manualCompletions[id]`; slot UI flips to dimmed/manual ✅. On `skipped` runDay: two-step transition — first writes `status: skipped → planned` then sets `manualCompletions[id]`. Skip and manual-complete are mutually exclusive (skip = negative intent, manual = positive intent). On `race_no_show` runDay: button UI-suppressed. Race-day completion is strictly real-saved-run-only (Q1 P4). Manual override on race day is not allowed; user must log a retroactive saved run. On already-✅ runDay: button hidden; "Undo" affordance writes a removal of the map key. **Recovery-entry effect.** Replaces the in-function side effect from `completeRunDay`. Watches derived race-day match: `profile.runMode === "race_prep" && raceDay.exists && matchingRealSavedRun(raceDay, race-strict)`. Race-strict = Q1 P4 (`templateId === "race"` on saved run + ≥95% distance). Manual completions do NOT enter recovery. Idempotent: no-op if `runPlan.phase === "recovery"` already (P13). Tracks `runPlan.completedRaces: string[]` (runDay IDs already entered) so a multi-race plan can enter recovery per-race, not per-plan (P28, surfaced by Round 3 #52). Replaces Q1's looser P14. Checks both `runDays` AND `weekHistory[].runDays` so auto-rollover doesn't strand the trigger (P22). Uses bounded `where('date', '==', raceGoal.targetDate)` query for the saved-run match instead of scanning the full subscription (P23). Race-no-show effect (existing `useProgram.ts:327`) gains reversal trigger: `race_no_show → planned` when a matching saved run appears post-no-show (P15). Q1 P7 already legalised this transition. **Map lifecycle.** Cleanup sweep on auto-rollover (PR-G) and on plan regenerate — drop `manualCompletions[id]` where `id` is no longer in the active `runDays` set (P19). One-liner on the plan-state save path. Map keyed by `runDay.id` which is preserved across moves but lost on plan regenerate. Accepted trade-off (P18). Optimistic-update + rollback on offline manual-complete writes uses map-key removal as the rollback mechanic. **Visual treatment.** Single design token distinguishes manual ✅ from real ✅. Applied in RunWeekStrip + DayPeekCard + ProgrammeRunSection. Hevy / Strong precedent (P24). **Engagement-system honesty.** Streak counter, Performance Index, and week-complete toast all read `realSavedRunMatch && !manualComplete` — only real activity feeds gamification (P25). Closes Round 2 #36-#38 (expectation mismatch). Explicit copy near streak counter explains "logged runs only." Saved-run distance = 0 (treadmill / no-GPS manual) is accepted false negative. DayActionSheet hints user can use the manual-complete map OR edit the saved run (P30). Race-day onboarding coachmark surfaces "Tap here on race day to start" on the race-day runDay first-mount when a race is in the plan. suppressed on the Run page. **P17:** Toast only fires when at least one real saved-run-derived completion. **P18:** `manualCompletions` keyed by `runDay.id`; preserved on moves, lost on plan regenerate. **P19:** Cleanup sweep on auto-rollover + plan regenerate drops orphan map keys. **P20:** Manual complete on `skipped` does two-step `skipped → planned` then map set. **P21:** Manual complete UI-suppressed on race-day runDays. **P22:** Recovery-entry effect checks `runDays` AND `weekHistory[].runDays`. **P23:** Bounded saved-run query for race-day match (`where('date', '==', raceGoal.targetDate)`). **P24:** Manual ✅ visually distinct from real ✅ via design token. **P25:** Streak / PI / toast read `realSavedRunMatch && !manualComplete` only. **P26:** `runScheduler.ts` added to pre-implementation find/fix surface. **P27:** Derivation formula = saved-run match ∪ manualCompletions ∪ legacy `completed*\*`/`completed: true`. **P28:** Recovery-entry per-race via `runPlan.completedRaces: string[]`; supersedes P14. **P29:** Planned distance ≤ 0 falls back to date + template-bucket; distance branch skipped. **P30:** Saved-run distance = 0 accepted false negative; UI copy guides. **P31:** Race-day onboarding coachmark surfaces "Tap here on race day to start."  **Open downstream questions (remaining for PR-J grill).** Q3 cross-feature consumer refactor strategy (inline derivation vs shared helper — `isComplete()` lives where, exported from where, signature takes what). | PR-J-Q5 | UX surface for the "extra run" case — saved runs that don't claim any planned slot                             | **Picked (b'') — inline display in the date's RunWeekStrip cell (stacked under the planned slot when present, standalone when not), with visual differentiation, a 2-extra cap per cell + "+N more" expand sheet, contextual "Mark complete" hint when same-date planned slots remain unclaimed.** **The four "extra" scenarios.** A saved run becomes an extra when: (1) no planned slot exists for that date; (2) all matching planned slots are already claimed by other saved runs (user double-ran the day); (3) distance is below the 70% threshold (Q1 P2); (4) quality-bucket mismatch (Q1 P3 — planned tempo, did easy). The saved run is real and stored in `users/{uid}/runs/` either way; Q5 decides how the Programme UI surfaces it. **Why inline display, not Ignore / Collapsed.** Reference apps (Strava, NRC, Garmin Connect) all show extras inline on the training calendar on the day they happened. Three-of-four convergence on the pattern. Ignore (a) is dishonest — user DID run; plan view shouldn't hide it. Collapsed (c) buries the data behind extra interaction. Relaxing the matching rule (d) defeats Q1's quality-bucket-guard intent. Promoting to first-class plan items (e) is overkill — saved runs aren't plan items. **Visual treatment.** Distinct from planned ✅ + manual ✅ via MULTIPLE channels (size + border style + text contrast) — NOT color alone. Outlined-not-filled border (planned uses filled); smaller pill height; dimmed text. Single design token applied consistently in RunWeekStrip, DayPeekCard, ProgrammeRunSection. Survives `prefers-contrast: more` / color-blind users. Same vertical-stacking layout across breakpoints — no per-breakpoint divergence (P84). **Cell rendering.** Extras stack BELOW the planned slot in the day cell (when planned exists) or stand alone (when no planned slot for that date). Cap at 2 visible extras per cell; "+N more" indicator opens an expand sheet listing all extras for that day. Pill text truncated to `Freeform · 5km · easy` (distance + bucket); full pace/duration shown in the expand sheet detail. **Same-date paradox mitigation (P74 — load-bearing).** When a planned slot remains unclaimed but a same-date extra exists (scenarios 3 + 4 above — distance or bucket fail), DayActionSheet → "Mark complete (manual)" surfaces a contextual hint: "An extra run is logged for this date. Mark this planned slot as done?" Lets user resolve the friction via the Q2 P11 manualCompletions map write. Race-day still UI-suppressed (Q2 P21 wins — race-day completion is strictly real-saved-run-only). Applies to BOTH planned-and-unclaimed AND skipped-with-extra cases (P86) — for skipped, tap follows Q2 P20's two-step transition `skipped → planned → manualCompletions[id]`. **Race-day strict-rule paradox (P80).** User races sub-95% (e.g. half-marathon DNF at 19/21.1km = 90%). Race-day slot stays planned; 19km renders as extra. DayActionSheet → "Mark complete (manual)" remains suppressed on race day. Only path to race-day ✅ is logging the full distance (edit the saved run, OR wait for Strava sync of the complete data). Onboarding coachmark P31 mentions the strict rule explicitly. Accepted UX cost of Q1 P4's design. **Engagement-system accounting.** Extras count in REAL-activity sources: weekly mileage totals, Performance Index, streaks, badges, crew leaderboards (per Q2 P25). Extras do NOT count in plan-adherence math ("X/3 planned runs completed" stays plan-only). Two ledgers, one source of truth. **Single-claim tiebreaker.** Multi-level deterministic walk so two same-date saved runs claim deterministically: (P81) primary by `saved-run.createdAt` ASC; secondary by `saved-run.id` lex ASC. (P82) Legacy saved runs without `createdAt` fall back to `saved-run.date` string ASC, then id lex. Same ordering applied in client + server (PR-L port). **Week-boundary rendering.** Extras render in the week strip whose `weekKey` matches the saved-run's `date` per the same `getWeekStart()` helper the strip uses (P83). No second source of truth for week boundaries. Closes the Sun-vs-Mon convention drift edge surfaced by Round 2 #3. **Plan-mutation triggers re-derive (P85).** When a runDay is moved (long-press → "Move to another day"), the claim map recomputes. An extra that becomes a same-date match post-move PROMOTES to a claim. The previously-planned date that just lost the moved slot may surface its own unclaimed extras. Re-derivation runs through the standard memoised selector — no special move-time path. **Touch + a11y discipline.** Extras pill has ≥44px touch target via invisible padding (P75 — iOS HIG). Extras carry distinct `aria-label="Extra run: 5km easy logged at 5:30pm"` for screen-reader announcement separate from planned slots (P76). Dragging / move gesture ignores extras — they're saved-run facts, not plan slots (P78). Removal happens via RunSummary → delete saved run, not via plan view (P17 of Q4 round 2 — same pattern). **Performance.** Unclaimed-runs selector memoised at `useProgram` level — returns `Map<date, SavedRun[]>` of unclaimed runs keyed by date string. Cells read by O(1) lookup, not per-cell filter (P77). 7 cells × lookup = 7 reads per render, vs 7× O(S) filter scans. **Onboarding.** 1-time coachmark "Your logged runs show here · Tap to open" surfaces on first extra render of a session (P79). Prevents new-user confusion about why an unfamiliar pill appeared. **Freeform-mode bonus.** Users in `runMode: freeform` (no plan) get an unintended-but-positive side effect — RunWeekStrip's empty cells now populate with extras, becoming a sparse weekly calendar log. Not a Q5 design intent but a clean emergent property of the inline-display choice. **Cross-feature.** History page subscription is separate; History shows ALL saved runs unconditionally. Programme's extras are a SUBSET (those unclaimed). No conflict — different framings of the same underlying data. PR-L's per-user CF iteration counts extras toward PI/streaks/weekly stats per Q2 P25; PR-L scope, not Q5. **Stress-test summary.** Two rounds × 25+ scenarios. **Round 1** surfaced the same-date paradox (#7–#9), race-day strict-rule paradox (#25), tiebreaker / a11y / touch-target gaps. **Round 2** surfaced the multi-level deterministic walk (#1–#2), cross-week boundary (#3), layout-consistency commitment (#5), plan-mutation re-derive (#13), skipped+extra interaction (#21). No architectural breakage; mitigations all expressible as pins. **Accepted UX costs.** **Pins (locked — Q5).** **P69:** Extras render inline in date's cell, stacked under planned slot when present, standalone when not. **P70:** Visual differentiation via multiple channels (size + border + contrast), not color alone. **P71:** Cap 2 extras visible per cell; "+N more" → expand sheet. **P72:** Extras count in real-activity sources (mileage, PI, streaks, badges) but NOT in plan-adherence math. **P73:** First-by-saved-run-timestamp-ASC claims; rest become extras (single-claim tiebreaker). **P74:** Same-date planned-but-unclaimed paradox — DayActionSheet "Mark complete (manual)" surfaces contextual hint. Race-day suppression wins. Applies to planned AND skipped scenarios. **P75:** ≥44px touch target on extras via invisible padding. **P76:** Distinct `aria-label` for extras. **P77:** Unclaimed-runs selector memoised at useProgram level, returning `Map<date, SavedRun[]>`. **P78:** Extras not draggable; move gesture ignores them. **P79:** First-extra coachmark — 1-time "Your logged runs show here · Tap to open" on first extra render of a session. **P80:** Race-day strict-rule copy added to Q2 P31 coachmark — explains the ≥95% requirement. **P81:** Tiebreaker on identical `createdAt` = `saved-run.id` lex ASC. **P82:** Legacy saved runs without `createdAt` fall back to `date` string ASC, then id lex. **P83:** Extras render in the week strip whose `weekKey` matches the saved-run's `date` per the same `getWeekStart()` helper. **P84:** Same vertical-stacking layout across breakpoints — no per-breakpoint divergence. **P85:** Plan-slot move triggers claim re-derivation; extras can promote to claims on same-date match post-move. **P86:** P74 contextual hint applies to skipped slots too (follows Q2 P20's two-step).

**Open downstream questions (Q6–Q8).** Q6 Strava-sync caching strategy (derive on every read vs cache the claim — Q3 implicitly chose "derive every read with memo"; Q6 confirms or refines for the specific Strava-sync-arriving-late case). Q7 saved-run deletion UI copy (toast trigger + wording — Q1 accepted regression "saved run deleted → planned reverts ✅"). Q8 migration timing (type widening lands in PR-J or precursor — Q4 P59 specified the shape, Q8 picks the timing).

**Methodology.** Two rounds × 20-25 stress-tests (45+ total). Round 1 surfaced the load-bearing UX paradoxes (same-date planned-but-unclaimed; race-day strict) and the a11y / touch-target / performance discipline. Round 2 surfaced deterministic-walk multi-level tiebreaker, cross-week boundary, layout consistency, plan-mutation re-derive, skipped+extra interaction. No architectural breakage; final (b'') resolves all surfaced issues. Reference-app convergence (Strava + NRC + Garmin) supports inline display as the right pattern at this product scale.

**Reference-app alignment.** Three of four reference run apps (Strava, NRC, Garmin Connect) show extras inline on the training calendar. TrainingPeaks similar via "planned vs actual" tracking. Hevy / Strong (lifting analogue) also surface non-program workouts inline. Tropos's pattern matches the dominant precedent. Calm-positioning preserved by the visual-restraint discipline (P70 outlined-not-filled, smaller pill, dimmed text).

**Connections.** Fifth locked decision in the PR-J arc. Q1 (predicate) + Q2 (writers/readers) + Q3 (where) + Q4 (tests) + Q5 (UX surface). Q5 closes the "what does the user see when X" question. Q6-Q8 are caching / copy / migration — narrower scope. PR-L: the unclaimed-runs selector (P77) is client-side memoisation; PR-L's server-side recompute doesn't need it (per-trigger full recompute per Q3 P47). Hist5d-style design-token discipline (P70) applied to extras pill. R1A: extras are saved-run reads in the UI; no new R1A intersection. Sub2: no Pro gating — extras are universal infrastructure.
| PR-J-Q6 | Strava-sync caching strategy — derive-on-read with memo vs additional caching layer | **Picked (a') — keep Q3's pure derive-on-every-read with memo. No additional cache layer. Memo guard handles the Strava-sync incremental-update case transparently; mass backfill gets a loading state.** **Question reframed.** A user with Strava connected may have ~10 saved runs land in a 5-second window when reconnecting after a few days offline. Each saved-run write fires the Firestore subscription. Q3 P37's fingerprint detects content change → claim map recomputes once per surfaced event. The question: does this path need additional caching (output cache, debounce, server-persisted claims) or does Q3's render-time memo suffice? **Why not the alternatives.** (b) Output cache by `(runDayId, savedRunFingerprint)` pair adds an invalidation surface without meaningful gain — Q3's memo already filters at the per-render-tick level. (c) Persisting the claim map to Firestore violates Q1's "completion is derived, never stored" — hard rejection. (d) Debouncing memo invalidation over 500ms hides the responsiveness of per-event updates and offers no perf benefit (recomputes are <5ms each). **Cost model.** 10 incremental sync events × ~5ms recompute = ~50ms total CPU spread over 5 seconds. Each recompute is O(R × S) where R = ~57 runDays (active + weekHistory) and S = ~200 saved runs ≈ 11k comparisons. PR-L symmetric per Q3 P47 — server-side full recompute per trigger, same cost shape. **Mass-backfill carve-out (P87).** Initial Strava connect with multi-year history can land 1000-2000 saved runs in a single batch load. First-load compute = O(R × 2000) ≈ 114k ops, ~50-200ms. **Pin: surfaces affected (RunWeekStrip, History) show a loading state when initial recompute exceeds 200ms.** Subsequent incremental sync events stay transparent. **Incremental-flicker as a feature (P88).** UI updates as each saved-run write lands during the sync window. Visual progress reflects Strava sync activity. No `useTransition` wrapping; no debouncing. The flicker IS the responsiveness signal. **No Strava-special-casing (P89).** Strava-imported saved runs are treated identically by the claim derivation. Fields like `stravaActivityId` / `stravaSyncedAt` are read-through metadata — Q3 P41 DI'd helper reads only canonical fields (`date`, `distance`, `avgPace`, `templateId`). **Selector consolidation (P90 — new from Round 2).** Q3 P77's unclaimed-runs selector (returns `Map<date, SavedRun[]>` of unclaimed runs for the extras display per Q5) and Q3's claim map (`Map<runDayId, ClaimState>`) must derive from the SAME memoised computation, sharing the fingerprint. Otherwise two parallel memos = two opportunities for drift + duplicate work. Single source of truth for claim resolution across both consumers. **Edge cases handled by Q3's memo discipline.** Subscription metadata-only re-fires → fingerprint catches no-change. Strava webhook double-fire → identical content → no recompute. Strava-imported timestamp clustering → Σ updatedAt still detects change. Activity deletion sync → length change → recompute. iOS background suspension → buffered events flush on resume. Capacitor offline cache cold start → 2× compute guaranteed (cache → server). All transparent. **Race-day strict edge survives (Q5 #51 / Q1 P31 inheritance).** Strava sync of a race-day activity that lacks `templateId === "race"` doesn't pass Q1 P4 strict → recovery doesn't enter. User must tag in Strava OR manually log. Onboarding coachmark P31 explains. Accepted regression carried forward. **Multi-mount cost.** `useProgram` mounted on Home + Program + History = 3× memos. Strava sync invalidates all 3. Acknowledged in Q3 #5; acceptable trade-off vs hook-level singleton complexity. **PR-L per-trigger cost.** Server-side `onRunCreated` trigger fires per Strava-imported run. 10 imports × O(R×S) ≈ 110k server-side ops. Bounded; PR-L scope to add batched recompute optimization only if telemetry says so. **Midnight invalidation (existing edge, NOT Q6 scope).** Q2 P38 / Q3 #3 — `today` argument doesn't auto-change at midnight. `useEffect` with `setTimeout` to next local midnight invalidates manually. Pre-existing pattern; Q6 doesn't add new mechanism. **Time-zone change mid-sync.** User crosses time zone → `today` arg changes → memo invalidates → recovery-entry effect day boundary shifts. Recovery effect is idempotent (Q2 P13) so re-firing safe. ✅ **Stress-test summary.** Two rounds × 15 scenarios (30 total). Round 1 covered baseline (mass sync, flicker, race conditions, memo correctness, Strava metadata, strict-mode). Round 2 covered subscription re-fire patterns, optimistic local writes, webhook double-fire, timezone change, iOS suspension, Capacitor cache, PR-L cost, selector duplication risk. No architectural breakage. Only refinement: selector + memo single source of truth (P90). **Pins (locked — Q6).** **P87:** Initial Strava connect / mass backfill (>200ms recompute) shows loading state. **P88:** Visual flicker during incremental sync is accepted UX — feels responsive. **P89:** Strava-imported saved runs treated identically; no special-casing on Strava-specific fields. **P90:** Q3 P77's unclaimed-runs selector + claim map share the same memoised computation and fingerprint. Single source of truth across consumers. **Open downstream questions (Q7, Q8).** Q7 saved-run deletion UI copy (toast trigger + wording — Q1 accepted regression). Q8 migration timing (type widening lands in PR-J or precursor — Q4 P59 specified shape, Q8 picks timing). **Methodology.** Two rounds × 15 stress-tests. Shorter than Q1-Q4 (60 total) because the question is narrower — pure performance / caching strategy with no new state. Q6's surface is the existing Q3 memo; Q6 confirms it's adequate vs explores alternative architectures. **Reference-app alignment.** No reference app exposes its sync-caching strategy publicly. The render-time derivation pattern matches React's standard memoisation discipline (TanStack Query, useMemo, useSyncExternalStore). Server-side per-trigger full recompute matches the Firebase Cloud Functions design pattern (idempotent triggers, no client-side caching of server state). **Connections.** Sixth locked decision in the PR-J arc. Q1-Q5 established the architecture; Q6 confirms Q3's caching strategy survives the Strava-sync scenario. PR-L: Q6 P90 selector consolidation applies client-side; PR-L server-side does per-trigger full recompute (no analogous selector). R1A: no R1A intersection (selector is pure). Sub2: no Pro gating. Hist5d's `dataConfidence.ts` shares the "share the memoised compute, don't fork" precedent (P90 is the same shape, different domain).
| PR-J-Q7 | Saved-run deletion UI copy — toast trigger, wording, no-Undo affordance | **Picked (b') — toast fires only when deletion / edit changes claim state (precise trigger), from user-initiated handler only (not subscription observation), Strava-style wording, no Undo button.** **The accepted regression.** Q1 P8 + Q2 P27 accepted: deleting a saved run that was claiming a planned slot flips that slot from ✅ back to "planned" (or to a different claim if another saved run promotes via the date+1 window). Q7 picks the exact UX disclosure. **Trigger (P91 + P97 — load-bearing).** Toast fires ONLY when the deleted saved run was claiming a runDay AND the delete came from a user-initiated handler (delete button click in RunSummary or History). NOT from subscription observation. Critical because R1A cascade (Phase D bulk deletes), Strava-side webhook deletions, and any other passive-update path all surface via Firestore subscription — if the toast watched the subscription, account deletion would spam the user with N "training history updated" toasts during the cascade. Pin: toast handler is wired into the explicit delete-button click flow only, awaits `deleteDoc(...)` success, then fires. **Wording (P92 + P99).** Delete: "Run deleted. Training history updated." Edit (when the edit changes claim state — distance / date / templateId): "Run updated. Training history changed." Both deliberately vague — "Training history" covers all the things that change (slot may flip to planned, slot may be re-claimed by another run via promotion, weekly mileage shifts, PI/streak math updates). Robust phrasing across all branches. **No Undo (P93).** Hard-delete via Firestore. No soft-delete + 5s window. Considered alternative (mark `deletedAt`, CF hard-deletes later, toast offers Undo) but adds: (a) two-step write per delete; (b) R1A inventory interaction; (c) re-creation state machine. All overengineered for a rare edge case. Strava + NRC don't offer Undo on activity delete either. **Dedupe (P94 + P100).** Within a 3-second window, claiming-deletes coalesce into a single toast. Cleanup session ("delete 10 runs from history") shows ONE toast, not 10 stacking. Dedupe state lives in a module-level ref (e.g. `deletionToastDedupe.ts`), NOT component state — survives cross-page navigation (user deletes from RunSummary then jumps to History to delete more; both deletes fall within the same window). **Recovery interaction (P95).** Race-day saved-run deletion does NOT auto-exit recovery. Per Q2 P28, `runPlan.completedRaces` is the source of truth for recovery state; once entered, it persists until mode-switch or timer. Deletion removes the underlying saved-run but doesn't reverse the lifecycle event "race was completed." User exits recovery via Settings or wait. Symmetric: deletion can't FIRE recovery either (entry requires a claim, deletion removes one). **Manual-completion undo (P96).** DayActionSheet's "Mark as planned again" affordance on a manually-completed slot has its OWN toast: "Marked as planned again." Different surface, different verb. Don't conflate with saved-run deletion. **Two surfaces wired (P97 + delete handlers).** RunSummary's delete button + History page's delete action (row swipe or overflow menu) both wire the toast logic. Single source-of-truth function: `notifyClaimStateChange(deletedRunId, claimMapBefore)` shared by both call sites. **Toast on resolution, not optimistic (P98).** `await deleteDoc(...); if (wasClaiming) notifyClaimStateChange(...)`. Optimistic UI flip happens in parallel for responsiveness, but the toast waits for write success. Prevents "deleted" toast on offline write rollback. **Cross-surface side effects don't toast.** R1A executor's Phase D deletion sweep → claim map updates silently. Strava webhook deletion → claim map updates silently. Server-side migration → claim map updates silently. Only the deliberate user click fires the toast. **Accessibility.** sonner default `aria-live="polite"` → screen readers announce. No additional work. ---

## What's NOT in scope here

- **The earlier deferred "hybrid week-advancement" debate (atomic vs lift-only).** Dissolves under B-loop auto-rollover — the loop is calendar-driven, not completion-driven, so the gate question becomes moot. The Lift-tab manual button keeps the runMode-aware atomic semantics for users who want to advance early.
- **Future navigation hook for `linkedRunId`** ("tap completed race in History → jump to RunSummary view"). Field reserved by PR-D; consumer UI deferred until a real use case lands.
- **Coach analytics on no-show rates / completion rates.** Would require a Cloud Function instead of the client effect; defer until product asks for it.
- **`recovery` as a user-selectable runMode for ad-hoc recovery** (injury, overreach, life stress). Q14 rejected this; if real demand emerges later, promoting phase → mode is the path.
- **Distance-scaled recovery template variation** (e.g. one short long run mid-recovery). Q15 picked "all easy" for v1; the duration scaling alone covers the marathon-vs-5K distinction adequately.

| Streak1 | Streak forgiveness model (calm forgiveness, NOT a token economy) | **Streaks gamification arc, first grill.** Question: how should the activity streak forgive missed days, given competitor patterns and Tropos's calm/anti-gamification brand? User pushed back twice — first questioning weekly-cadence ("what's the point?"), then smelling finickiness in a freeze-token proposal ("is this just finicky? do other apps do this?"). Both push-backs were correct and reshaped the answer. **Key architecture fact:** Tropos's streak is an ENGAGEMENT streak, not a training streak — `computeActiveDateSet` (useStreaks.tsx) counts a logged meal-with-items OR workout OR valid run as an active day, so rest days where you still log food already keep the streak alive. This WEAKENS the NRC weekly-cadence borrow (which solves rest-day-punishment in pure training streaks) → **weekly cadence DROPPED** (park behind a data trigger: revisit only if real data shows streaks breaking for training-pattern reasons food-logging doesn't cover). **Reference-app finding (per CLAUDE.md reference rule):** forgiveness is now table stakes — even Apple Activity rings (the most rigid streak in existence) capitulated and added Pause in watchOS 11 after years of complaints; MyFitnessPal uses retroactive backfill; habit trackers (Finch/Everyday/Habiting/Habi) use "never miss twice" (James Clear) / grace budgets (~3 skips per rolling 30d) framed as self-compassion, "reward showing up not perfection," no shaming graphs. The ONLY finicky + off-brand pattern is Duolingo's earned-token economy — search-confirmed criticism as "pay-to-win," engagement-not-learning, and "prompts you to refill even when you still have freezes equipped" (a dark pattern that directly violates Tropos's "calm over flashy / no harsh contrasts" design law). **DECISION (locked by product owner 2026-05-30):** **Tier A → BUILD** budgeted grace inside `computeCurrentStreak` (useStreaks.tsx:162). Walking back from the today/yesterday end anchor, when a non-active day is hit, bridge it ONLY if no grace was spent within the prior 6 days of the walk; else stop. This single spacing variable enforces BOTH "never miss twice" AND "≤1 forgiven day per rolling 7" and prevents the every-other-day degenerate (which matters for the 1000+ user base, esp. training-centric users who don't log food daily). Grace days count toward the streak SPAN (Duolingo-consistent mental model so the number doesn't mysteriously lag) but NOT toward `totalActiveDays` (= activeDateSet.size stays the honest "days you actually showed up" count — a clean forgiving-continuity vs honest-attendance split the derived architecture gives for free). Pure-function change + unit tests; feeds badge thresholds unchanged (a 7-day Week Warrior may include ≤1 grace day — acceptable, matches field). **Tier B → ALREADY WORKS, zero engine code:** streak derives from each meal/workout/run's own `date` field, and the Food page already logs to a past day via `/food?date=YYYY-MM-DD` (useMeals saves `date: selectedDate`, lines ~471/514). Backfilling a past day already re-enters that date into activeDateSet and bridges the streak. Only gap is DISCOVERABILITY → optional future one-line nudge, not a build. **Tier C → PARK:** explicit vacation/illness Pause (Apple watchOS-11 model — a stored pause window excluded from the walk). Defer until a real user need; do not build pre-launch. **NOT BUILDING:** token/freeze economy, equipping, repair-store, pre-emptive "your streak is in danger — buy a freeze" prompts. **Visibility:** gentle AFTER-the-fact reassurance only ("yesterday's rest day is covered — still on a 12-day streak"), NEVER a pre-emptive threat. Two tuning forks left to product owner at impl time: pure never-miss-twice vs budgeted-1-per-7 (recommended: budgeted), and invisible vs gentle-surfaced grace (recommended: gentle-after). **STATUS 2026-05-30 — locked on claude/new-session-3T7ZJ; verify merged to main so next agent sees it. Sources: Apple watchOS 11 ring pause (macworld), MyFitnessPal backfill (support.myfitnesspal.com), Duolingo streak-freeze criticism (androidauthority), habit-tracker grace design (habi.app).** **STATUS 2026-05-30 — post-impl 3-agent adversarial review (engine correctness / hook+UI wiring / downstream ripple). Engine walk verified correct by 65k-shape brute force; ONE real bug found + fixed: the `yesterday` anchor used DST-unsafe ms-subtraction (`now - 86400000`) which collapses a live streak to 0 on a 25h fall-back day and skips a day on the 23h post-spring-forward day — was pre-existing on main, carried by the refactor and replicated into the two new callbacks. Fixed via a single `yesterdayKey(now)` calendar-step helper + dedicated DST regression tests (commit 01be84c2). No other engine bugs; mutual exclusivity of the three Home nudges proven; deep-link validated; no lock drift; no bad ripple into reminder/badges/profile/functions. DECISION (honest-vs-grace-inflated metrics): `currentStreak` AND `longestStreak` stay grace-INCLUSIVE, INCLUDING the `users/{uid}/public/profile` mirror other users read — coherent with the already-locked "the number counts grace" intent, bounded to ≤1 grace/7, and `totalActiveDays` remains the honest attendance metric (no separate honest-streak concept exists). `longestStreak` is monotonic so a grace-padded span permanently ratchets the public all-time record — accepted.
