| Polish1 | App-improvement sweep — two delegated product decisions (cold-start PI presentation; phase-nutrition macro reconciliation) | **"Improve the app" 3-agent read-only sweep (UX / correctness / perf-a11y), then product owner delegated the two findings that needed a design call ("do these two, stress-test, make your decision").** Shipped mechanical wins first (WaterBubbles off-screen pause, ExercisePicker 44px+aria close button, History Firestore-listener dedup via props, two dead components deleted, EmptyState/Home brand-token swaps). One scout "flagship" (gps.ts isValidReading wall-clock speed-gate) was VERIFIED-AND-DROPPED: GPSPoint.timestamp is set to Date.now() at processing time, so Date.now()-lastPoint.timestamp is wall-clock minus wall-clock (true elapsed) — accepting 500m over a real 60s gap is physically valid, and "fixing" it to pos.timestamp would introduce a cross-clock bug. **DECISION 1 (cold-start PI) → "establishing baseline" state, client-only.** The engine's `safeRatio(x,0)→1.0` makes a new user's first week read as "at baseline" (~67, "moderate load"); `computeConfidence` can even return "high" for week 1. BUT the Home hero ALREADY gates this (`signals.lifetimeWeeks < 4 || weeksAvailable < 2` → renders ", establishing baseline", hides delta). The leak was PerformanceTab, which showed a confident "Moderate effort / Balanced workload" verdict + load band with no caveat. Fix: bring the tab under the same gate (`weeks.length < 4`) — headline "Establishing your baseline", load band reads "Establishing", delta hidden; centralised in `getPlainLanguageSummary(..., establishing)` so hero/tab share one copy contract. CLIENT-ONLY by design — the misleading server `confidence` field is never surfaced, so NO dual-engine change (src/lib + functions/performanceEngine.js) and NO functions deploy was needed. Reference-app aligned: Whoop/Garmin/Strava all have an explicit baseline-establishing period. NOT TOUCHED (deliberately): the server engine's `confidence`/`loadBand` math — flagged for a future vetted dual-engine + deploy pass if those fields ever get surfaced raw. **DECISION 2 (phaseNutrition) → carbs are the balancing macro.** `getAdjustedTargets` recomputes protein from bodyweight (`proteinMultiplier*weightKg`) but carbs only tracked the calorie surplus and fat stayed at base, so whenever stored base protein ≠ bodyweight*multiplier (stale onboarding value / weight change / different upstream multiplier) the macros surfaced via useEffectiveTargets on Home/Food silently summed to a DIFFERENT number than the calorie goal beside them — despite a code comment claiming they reconciled. Fix: `carbs = max(0, round((calories - protein*4 - fat*9)/4))`, extending the documented "carbs absorb the training surplus" intent to also absorb the protein delta; keeps bodyweight-derived protein (nutritionally correct) and fat-at-base (carbs fuel training, not fat). Guarantees protein*4+carbs*4+fat*9 === calories (±2 cal gram rounding) in all cases; identical to old output when the base is already consistent (so production targets unchanged). Rejected alternatives: adjusting fat (contradicts the carbs-fuel intent), pinning protein to base (loses current-weight correctness). Tests: updated 6 carb assertions that pinned the old inconsistent values + added an invariant guard across day types + a negative-carb clamp test. **STATUS 2026-05-30 — both shipped on claude/new-session-3T7ZJ, full suite green (3292). Verify merged to main.** |

| Run9 | Programme run-section redesign — race-goal-only model, unified surface, hide periodization | **Run-section overhaul.** Triggered by the owner flagging the Programme run tab as the worst-off part of the app ("looks terrible, a lot is wrong"). Resolved via a `/grill-me` session backed by a current-state audit + a competitor teardown (Nike Run Club, Garmin Coach, TrainingPeaks, Runna, Strava→Runna, Couch-to-5K). **Current-state diagnosis:** `ProgrammeRunSection.tsx` is a 990-line god-component rendering ~12 conditional top-level states with an implicit state machine (10+ derived booleans) — vs the lift tab's clean DayStepper hierarchy. Real defects: (a) dual source of truth for the race goal (`profile.raceGoal` vs `programState.runPlan.raceGoal`) that can diverge; (b) "All runs done" affirmation shows on rest days (nextStartable null on a planned rest day); (c) up to 6 stacked amber/blue edge-state banners (race-elapsed, compressed, no-show, recovery, recovery-complete, malformed-plan) plus the Home FellBehindSheet, where competitors show calm copy + one action. **Competitor convergence (3+ apps, so the convention unless Tropos has a reason):** date-anchored plans built backward from race day; the week is a calendar with a dominant "today's/next run" card; a run = warmup→work→cooldown with plain-language types; freeform is the always-on substrate and a plan layers on top (NO freeform/structured mode toggle — the concept every consumer app deliberately lacks); periodization vocab (base/build/peak, TSS, load curves) is hidden, taper named only in plain copy near race day; post-race recovery is light except Runna's explicit block; missed-runs handling is the main fault line (Garmin silent auto-adapt / Runna one-tap realign tray / TrainingPeaks mark-missed-no-adapt / NRC self-coach). Biggest lesson for a hybrid app: project the plan onto the same run surface used for free runs, hide the phase machine, make "I fell behind" a one-tap non-judgmental realign (more important for hybrid, since lift days compete with run slots so falling behind is the common case), and ship a light explicit post-race recovery (run easy while lifting ramps). **LOCKED DECISIONS (owner, 2026-05-29 grill):** Run9a MODE MODEL → freeform is the always-on substrate and a RACE GOAL is the only "plan"; retire the freeform/structured/race*prep user-facing toggle; "has a race?" derives from `raceGoal` presence (no mode enum the user manages). Run9b LAYOUT → one consistent surface for every state: a next-run hero (freeform Start CTA, or next prescribed run, or recovery/race-day prompt) + the 7-day week strip + a slim race header (countdown) only when a race is set; the ~12 conditional cards and 6 banners collapse into hero/header content + at most one contextual slot; scope is the run tab only (do NOT refactor the lift tab). Run9c FELL BEHIND → a single calm in-tab "Realign" prompt with one primary action that COMPRESSES remaining weeks to keep the booked race date by default, plus a secondary "my race moved →" to change the date; informed, not silent; replaces the 3-button shift/compress/skip FellBehindSheet mechanism-surfacing. Run9d POST-RACE → keep an explicit recovery state, hero-framed ("Recovery week — easy runs only, N days left; your lifting can ramp back up"), skippable in one tap; lean into the hybrid angle; not a banner. Run9e PLAN ENTRY → a "Train for a race →" CTA on the run tab itself (discovery where running lives) that routes into the EXISTING ProgrammeSettings editor at /settings/training (NOT a parallel form — preserves the Pgm4 single-editor invariant). Run9f PHASES → base/build/peak stay internal; surface ONLY a plain-language taper line in the race header during taper weeks; no phase badges, diagrams, TSS, or load numbers. **ENG-LEVEL DECISIONS (architect, downstream of the locks):** (1) SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the race goal — `profile.raceGoal` is canonical user intent; `runPlan` holds only DERIVED plan state (generated runDays + phase/recoveryEndDate/totalWeeks/compressed), NOT a second copy of raceGoal; kills the divergence bug. (2) Retire the `runMode` enum as a user-managed field; freeform-vs-plan derives from raceGoal presence (recovery is a post-race sub-state on runPlan). (3) Split the 990-line ProgrammeRunSection into RunHero / RunWeekStrip (exists) / RaceHeader / race-setup-CTA with ONE explicit state discriminator replacing the 10 derived booleans. (4) Fix "all runs done" so a rest day reads as a rest day, not a completion. (5) MIGRATION: existing `structured` users → freeform (they lose auto-assigned weekly run-type variety; freeform = log runs freely, matching NRC/Strava); existing `race_prep` users with a valid future raceGoal → race overlay; legacy runMode values map through on read. **STATUS 2026-05-29 — locked from grill; design only, NOT yet implemented. Implementation touches the correctness-critical runScheduler (race-prep/taper/recovery state machine) + a data migration, so it should be planned + verified carefully (workflow-class) before coding. Verify this lock is in origin/main ancestry so the next agent sees it.** STATUS 2026-05-29 (adversarial stress-test, 3 critics) — core UI overhaul UPHELD (kill god-component into hero+strip, collapse banners, rest-day fix, recovery hero-framed, single-source raceGoal). Five holes found + resolved. (1) NO-RACE SUBSTRATE: Run9a over-corrected by leaving non-racers a bare Start button while lift gives a full programme. RESOLVED: lift is the structured anchor, running is deliberately the flexible side (reason documented in CONTEXT.md); do NOT add a no-race plan engine, but ENRICH freeform with a weekly run target + progress so the tab is not barren; the stale "matches NRC/Strava" migration rationale is WRONG (Strava removed static plans 2025-07) — drop it. (2) COMPRESS SAFETY: Run9c compress-to-keep-date defaulted into unsafe plans (flat 2-week floor, weekly long runs). RESOLVED: use per-distance RACE_CONFIGS.minWeeks as a taper-safe floor; compress-by-default only while within it; once breached, the primary realign action flips to "move your race date" and compress is no longer offered as the safe default. (3) PHASE INCONSISTENCY: lift shows a phase badge, run hides phases. RESOLVED: keep Run9f (run hides phases, names only taper); the asymmetry is deliberate (lift phase = user-chosen mesocycle; run phase = auto-derived from race date) and is documented in CONTEXT.md. | RunWk1 | Week-view unification across Programme (Lift + Run) and Home — calendar vs rotation axis | **Run-week scheduling-ontology lock (2026-05-30 `/grill-with-docs`, owner-delegated "U decide" after a stress-test).** Trigger: owner flagged drift/disjointedness across FOUR "week"/day representations on different axes — Home `WeekStrip` (calendar dates + density dots), Programme **Lift** tab `DayStepper` (rotation **Day 1–N** numbered circles), Programme **Run** cockpit `HybridWeekRail` (calendar S–S lane pills, just shipped), and `DayActionSheet` (calendar day). Owner proposed: Run should share Home's language AND have its own calendar; maybe adopt the "This week" rail into the Lift tab instead of just the workouts. **CODE FINDING (the crux, cross-referenced):** the app already runs TWO different lift mappings — the Lift tab's `todayIndex = workouts.findIndex(d => !d.completed && !d.skipped)` (`Program.tsx:386`) is pure **rotation** ("next incomplete in the split", weekday-agnostic), while every calendar surface resolves lifts via `trainingResolver` → `liftIndexForDayOfWeek(weekSchedule, dow)` (pure **calendar**, weekday-pinned). They disagree the moment completions happen out of weekday order / on a non-lift day / skip-and-make-up. So the owner's "adopt the calendar rail into the Lift tab" is, underneath, a proposal to switch lifting from a flexible rotation model to a date-pinned calendar model — a behaviour change, not a reskin. **STRESS-TEST (adversarial, owner asked me NOT to rubber-stamp):** 4 attacks. (1) "can't draw a rotation on a calendar" LANDS — placing a lift on a calendar tile re-pins it to a weekday, and the just-shipped `HybridWeekRail` already does this via `liftIndexForDayOfWeek`, so it's on the calendar side of the fork. (2) "does the drift matter?" — partially defuses: the MODAL disciplined in-order lifter sees rotation≈calendar agree; divergence is an edge case for the flexible/lapsed segment (which CLAUDE.md says to design FOR, so not dismissible). (3) "two models already leak, you're painting over it" LANDS, sharpest — the `DayActionSheet` (calendar) and Lift tab (rotation) can ALREADY show two different "current lifts" today; visual unification alone is lipstick. (4) steelman for force-calendar REVERSED my prior: the two models are domain-CORRECT, not tech debt — **lifting = volume accumulation → rotation** ("don't lose a session if a day slips"); **running = date-specific stimulus → calendar** (long run Sunday, race countdown). Flattening lifts to calendar would mark a Tuesday-instead-of-Monday lift "missed Monday" and DROP that session's volume — worse for adherence + punishes the light/lapsed trainer. **DECISION (owner "U decide"):** KEEP BOTH ontologies — runs **date-pinned**, lifts **split-ordered** — do NOT flatten. Reconcile as **plan vs progress**: the **week rail** renders the _planned_ week (date-pinned runs + planned lift day-types) and is the shared glance on both Programme tabs; the **next-up cursor** (`DayStepper`) is the lift _execution_ surface; they share `workout.completed` so completion never disagrees; "planned weekday ≠ next session" (after working ahead / off-schedule) is normal plan-vs-progress, not a bug. CONSTRAINT this places on the shipped rail: its lift lane must NOT assert an authoritative weekday-pinned session identity ("Push IS Monday") — it shows the planned shape + shared completion, deferring session-identity selection to the cursor; do NOT "fix" the rail toward force-calendar. Therefore the week-view unification is a **visual + interaction-coherence** effort (shared cell anatomy, colours, today indicator, language across `WeekStrip`/`HybridWeekRail`/`DayStepper`), NOT a scheduling-model migration. Q3 (one shared rail vs lift-only variant): ONE shared `HybridWeekRail`, shown on the Run tab (done) and to be ADDED to the Lift tab above the stepper (owner's instinct), Lift emphasising the purple lane. Q4 (Home): `WeekStrip` stays the multi-week date NAVIGATOR (dots), adopting shared colour/today conventions; a single shared "week-cell" primitive with two density modes (dots for multi-week scroll, lanes for single-week) is a deferred future refactor, not this arc. **CAPTURED:** `docs/adr/0002-dual-scheduling-ontology.md` (the date-pinned/split-ordered decision + rejected force-calendar) + `CONTEXT.md` glossary terms (date-pinned, split-ordered, planned-week-vs-progress, week rail, week strip, next-up cursor) + fixed the stale `CONTEXT.md` `runMode` entry (still listed retired `structured`). **STATUS 2026-05-30 — design locked; NOT yet implemented. Implementation arc (visual/interaction only): (1) add `HybridWeekRail` to the Lift tab; (2) harmonise `WeekStrip`/`DayStepper` cell anatomy + today indicator + colours with the rail; (3) keep the cursor as the lift execution surface. Verify this lock is in origin/main ancestry. | Pgm5 | Durable user decisions — the engine bootstraps and adapts but never silently discards a user's plan choice | **Programme ownership model.** Triggered by the split-picker investigation (draft PR #936): the Split-preference picker writes profile.preferredSplit but it is NEVER consumed by the buildPlan→generateProgram rebuild path — split is 100% chooseSplit(liftDays); the only real consumer of preferredSplit is matchTemplate.ts ~line 44 (a separate onboarding-class path). Widened into a positioning question once the EXISTING exercise editor was surfaced. **Three-altitude model:** L1 skeleton/split (how many days, each day's focus, the movement-category slots) — owned by the ENGINE via chooseSplit; the user's only L1 lever (the split picker) is inert. L2 exercise selection (which exercise fills each slot) — HYBRID via the Program-page editor (swap/add/delete/reorder, Program.tsx ~224-373). L3 execution (sets/reps/weight/progression) — engine via auto-progression. **Verified current-state bugs:** (1) split picker inert in the rebuild path (above). (2) On EVERY configurePlan save the engine rebuilds workouts from a fixed template skeleton, preserving only per-slot exerciseId+weight+history via findExisting(dayIdx,exIdx) in programEngine makeExercise — so a swap-in-place survives when the slot category is unchanged, but add/delete/reorder are silently wiped. (3) WorkoutDay.isCustom exists (programTypes.ts ~120) but is DEAD — never set by the edit handlers, never read by the engine; half-built custom-day protection that was abandoned. Net: the app forgets what the user told it, at BOTH L1 (split) and L2 (structural edits). **Reference-app audit (per CLAUDE.md reference rule):** Fitbod generates + lets you swap exercises AND pick a split, and REMEMBERS (a swap becomes a durable preference); Hevy/Strong are full-manual, the routine persists forever; Boostcamp/Future are coach-authored with minimal edit. NONE silently discard user edits on a settings change — Tropos's ephemeral-edits + inert-picker is the anomaly. **DECISION (Option A, product owner 2026-06-01):** commit to the principle "the engine bootstraps and adapts but NEVER silently discards a user decision." Two implementation threads, each correctness-critical engine work needing its own grill + tests: T1 — split picker drives the L1 skeleton: thread preferredSplit into generateProgram, honour a split that is valid for the day count (the UI already gates incompatible picks via isSplitDisabled — PPL needs 5+, U/L needs 4+), with chooseSplit staying the "Auto (recommended)" default. T2 — wire up isCustom so a user-edited day survives regeneration: structural L2 edits become durable across rebuilds. **Open implementation grills (NOT decided here):** (a) split name→variant mapping — the picker speaks 3 names (Full Body / Upper-Lower / PPL) but the engine emits day-count variants (ppl_ul, ppl_x2); how does "PPL at 5 lift days" map onto session generation? (b) isCustom granularity — per-day lock vs Fitbod-style per-exercise durable swap preference vs warn-on-rebuild; and what happens to a custom day when the SPLIT itself changes (the skeleton differs, so positional preservation cannot hold). **Relationship to #936:** the presentational IA restructure (draft PR #936 — grouped sections, honest "Split preference" relabel + generated-split helper) ships UNDERNEATH this as the IA win and already stops the UI lying; this lock is the behavioural commitment that makes the controls real. Keep the buildPlan + configurePlan preserveHistory save path. **STATUS 2026-06-01 — locked by product owner (Option A). Lock on its own branch claude/lock-pgm5, PR'd immediately per lock discipline. T1 and T2 each need their own grill + plan→implement→verify before coding. Verify merged to main so the next agent sees the decision.** **STATUS 2026-06-01 (grill outcome) — T1 and T2 COLLAPSE into ONE thread: "structure-preserving regeneration." Root cause confirmed in code: TWO generation engines disagree — onboarding (matchTemplate + templates.ts) scores structure by goal+equipment+split+days and HONOURS preferredSplit (library covers full_body@3-4, upper_lower@4, ppl@5-6, bro_split@5), while regeneration (generateProgram + chooseSplit) sets structure = f(days) ONLY and ignores preferredSplit/goal/equipment. So ANY post-onboarding settings save silently REPLACES the onboarded structure (e.g. bro_split@5 → ppl_ul@5 — the procedural engine cannot even build bro_split) AND wipes structural exercise edits — the real pre-existing Pgm5 violation, independent of the inert picker. Procedurally there are exactly 6 curated balanced structures, one per lift-day count (1→FB, 2→FB|UL, 3→FB|PPL, 4→UL, 5→ppl_ul, 6→ppl_x2); genuine multi-structure choice exists only at 2-3 days. DECISIONS (product owner, this session): (Q1) the split picker is NOT a user chooser — it becomes a derived DISPLAY ("coach owns structure"); the user expresses preference via goal/days + the exercise editor, not a split toggle. (Q2) the fix is structure-preserving regeneration — keep the user's CURRENT day structure + exercise edits and only update CONTENTS (rep ranges, volume, per-slot exercise selection), instead of rebuilding from template. (Q3 boundary) content edits (goal, nutrition, experience, equipment, injuries) preserve the skeleton; ONLY a lift-days change (disclosed) or explicit Reset re-derives structure; a GOAL change does NOT restructure (Reset is the path to a fresh build). Stress-test commitments: regeneration mechanics must invert to update-in-place on programState.workouts (not rebuild-from-template); the lift-days disclosure must NAME the customization loss, and extend-the-structure (keep your split, add a day) over rebuild-from-scratch is a roadmap target because rebuild-on-small-day-change is disproportionately lossy; equipment downgrades (full→minimal) must degrade gracefully when a movement-category has no trainable exercise; and we CONSCIOUSLY drop the onboarding library's goal/equipment→structure refinements post-onboarding (a fat_loss→hypertrophy switcher keeps their structure rather than getting the library's hypertrophy@4 = upper_lower). SCOPE: this is real engine work, NOT a patch — deferred as its own deliberate project. #936 (presentational IA + honest generated-split helper; split still a tappable picker, NOT yet display-only) shipped + merged first as the safe partial win; the display-only split conversion belongs to THIS project (Q1), not #936.** **STATUS 2026-06-01 (SHIPPED — PR #953, merged to main) — implemented in 3 verifiable slices off a file-by-file Plan-agent plan. Slice 1 (Q1): split picker removed from ProgrammeSettings → read-only "Split" display (programState.splitType ?? chooseSplit(saved.liftDays) via splitLabel); preferredSplit still threaded inertly through buildPlan from the persisted value. Slice 2 (Q2, core): new programEngine.expectedDayCount(weeklyTarget) (= generateProgram's emitted workout count, pinned by a parity test n=1..7+0); buildLiftProgram now branches — if existingState.workouts present AND existing.length === expectedDayCount(liftDays) → PRESERVE the user's workouts verbatim (deep-clone) + existing splitType; else (no plan, or lift-days changed) → rebuild via generateProgram; Reset stays destructive via useProgram.regenerateProgram. No CF change (validatePlanPayload ignores workouts). Slice 3 (Q3): confirm-modal copy branches — lift-days change NAMES the customization reset, content-only edit reassures workouts are kept. Verification: +29 unit tests (expectedDayCount parity; content edit preserves workouts INCL. an added exercise + a reordered day; lift-days change rebuilds; split read-only; both disclosure branches), full suite 3408 passed/0 failed, tsc 0, eslint 0; emulator runtime check confirmed split-as-display (0 picker buttons), both confirm copies, 0 console errors. **STILL DEFERRED (each needs a persisted per-exercise role anchor the stored ProgramExercise lacks):** goal-driven rep/volume rescheme on a content edit (today a goal change keeps the lift structure + updates nutrition/macros, but does NOT refresh rep ranges — the immediate fast-follow); injury-aware in-place re-swap and equipment re-pick (regeneration ignores both today, so preserving is not a regression); extend-the-structure on a day-add (v1 rebuilds-and-discloses on a lift-days change). isCustom remains a dead field — superseded by the "preserve verbatim" approach, which makes per-day locking unnecessary for content edits.** **STATUS 2026-06-01 (follow-up SHIPPED — PR #955, merged) — injury-aware in-place re-swap. New exported matchTemplate.applyInjuryFiltersToWorkouts(workouts, injuries) — the WorkoutDay/ProgramExercise sibling of applyInjuryFilters; reuses buildContraIndex (now exported, keyed by exerciseId from PROGRAM_TEMPLATES) + findSafeSubstitute. Over-swap guard: an exercise is swapped ONLY when the contra index flags it for one of the user's CURRENT injuries (a knee exercise is left alone for a shoulder-only user); no safe sub → kept with a warning note. buildLiftProgram applies it to BOTH the preserve and rebuild outputs, so a settings injury change adapts the lift workouts on every route AND the rebuild path (which previously ignored injuries) is now injury-aware. Idempotent; no-op for healthy/"none"; removing an injury does NOT un-swap (no pre-swap id stored — future enhancement). Tests: applyInjuryFiltersToWorkouts unit suite (swap carries weight/history, no over-swap, no-op, structure preserved, idempotent) + planBuilder integration; full suite 3414 passed/0 failed, tsc 0, eslint 0. **REP-RESCHEME — INVESTIGATED & DEFERRED (won't-do for now):** recomputing rep ranges on a goal change while preserving the plan is NOT a clean role-anchored fast-follow — the templates assign per-slot (reps, progression) across ≥3 tiers (main-reps+main-prog, accessory-reps+main-prog, accessory-reps+linear) that don't reduce to a single stored "role" bit; doing it right means re-deriving from the template (the thing structure-preservation avoids) or persisting a full per-slot rep recipe, and it'd only help post-migration plans. Product call: a training-focus change is a MAJOR change that Reset already handles correctly (rebuilds fresh for the new goal) — and the reference apps (Fitbod et al.) regenerate on a goal change rather than rep-rescheming in place. So preserve-on-content-edit + Reset-for-a-goal-overhaul is the right behaviour; in-place rep-rescheme is gold-plating and is shelved unless a concrete user need surfaces. **REMAINING DEFERRED:** equipment re-pick (regeneration engine has no equipment filter — would need one built); un-swap on injury removal (needs the pre-swap id persisted); extend-the-structure on a day-add (vs rebuild-and-disclose).** **STATUS 2026-06-01 (follow-up SHIPPED — PR #957, merged) — equipment-aware in-place re-pick. New exported matchTemplate.applyEquipmentFilterToWorkouts(workouts, equipment, injuries). EQUIPMENT_AVAILABILITY maps each tier → allowed Exercise.equipment values, derived from the EQUIPMENT_OPTIONS copy: full_gym → everything (no-op); home_gym → {Dumbbells, Bodyweight, Kettlebell}; minimal → {Dumbbells, Bodyweight} — both exclude Barbell/Machine/Cable (the meaningful distinction the coarse equipment vocab supports; reversible product-data decision). For each exercise whose equipment (looked up via getExerciseById) is not allowed, picks a same-movement-category mate from exerciseBank that fits AND is not injury-contraindicated (injury-aware) AND not already on the day; carries weight/history; unknown/custom ids untouched; no fit → kept with a warning note. buildLiftProgram composes injuries-first then equipment on both preserve + rebuild outputs. Idempotent; full_gym (default) never filters so blast radius is limited to users who chose limited equipment. Tests: applyEquipmentFilterToWorkouts unit suite + planBuilder integration; full suite 3420 passed/0 failed, tsc 0, eslint 0. **ARC STATUS:** the high-value durable-plan work is DONE — preserve (PR #953), injury re-swap (#955), equipment re-pick (#957). Remaining items are diminishing-returns / gated: rep-rescheme (shelved, Reset covers it); un-swap on injury/equipment REMOVAL (needs the pre-swap id persisted on ProgramExercise — niche); extend-the-structure on a day-add (gated on the limited 6-structure template library — would need new high-day templates). None blocking; pick up only if a concrete user need surfaces.** |

| Run10 | Race Goal Planner — derived pre-save preview in the ProgrammeSettings race-prep editor | **Run-section follow-up (product owner approved 2026-06-01).** Triggered by a ~19-screenshot proposal ("derived nutrition phase" thread) for a guided Race Goal Planner. Before this, the race-prep editor took a distance + target date and validated only that the date was future (`raceDateInvalid` = past-or-empty); the confidence-building cockpit (`RaceCockpitCard` — weeks-out, Base·Build·Taper·Race rail, compressed note) appeared ONLY after the plan was created. **DECISION:** bring that cockpit language UPSTREAM as a calm, derived pre-save preview that answers what the chosen date means for the plan — weeks-out, a distance-aware timing status, the phase rail, the weekly structure, and post-race recovery — then a status-aware save CTA. **Lock constraints (all verified against code, not assumed):** (Pgm4) stays inside the unified ProgrammeSettings editor — NO wizard, NO full-screen flow, NO second save flow; reuses the existing sticky save bar + confirm modal. (Run9/Run9a) race-goal-only model preserved — NO mode chips, NO structured mode; periodization stays mostly hidden, surfacing only what the cockpit already shows post-save. (Pgm5) too-soon-but-future dates are NEVER hard-blocked — they save as a "finish-safely plan"; only empty/past dates block (= today's `raceDateInvalid`, unchanged). (Single-source-of-truth, the `computeProgrammeChanges` lesson) every previewed number is READ from the SAME engine the save commits — `planBuilder.buildRunPlan` calls `generateRacePlanV2` with `weekStart = localWeekKey(parseLocalDate(currentDate))` + the same `currentDate`; the helper mirrors that derivation exactly, and status comes straight from the engine's own `compressed`/`belowFloor` booleans, NOT a parallel re-classification. Closed palette: coral = running; calm copy; no medical warnings, no performance promises. **FIVE states, not four (the proposal said four):** `empty` (no date — calm prompt, save disabled) / `invalid` (past — "Pick a future race date", save disabled) / `healthy` (≥ ideal build — "Save race plan") / `compressed` (below ideal, ≥ floor — "Save compressed plan") / `below-floor` (below taper-safe floor — finish-safely, "Save finish-safely plan", still SAVES). below-floor is DISTINCT from compressed — below the floor compress-to-keep-date stops being the safe default. **What we did NOT build (deliberate):** the proposal's "smarter run-day recommendation" (screenshot #5) — `generateRacePlanV2` TAKES `weeklyRunDays`, it does not recommend one; inventing a recommendation would break single-source AND Run9's hide-periodization, so the planner surfaces "N run days/week the plan will build" (the value the engine uses), not a novel number. **Engine constants confirmed exact** (`runScheduler.ts`): ideal `minWeeks` 5k=4/10k=6/half=8/marathon=12; taper-safe floor `taperWeeks+1` 5k=2/10k=2/half=3/marathon=4; recovery 5k=1/10k=2/half=3/marathon=4. **Display subtlety locked:** headline `weeksOut` is the NATURAL unclamped `ceil(daysOut/7)`, never the engine's `totalWeeks` (which has a hard floor of 2) — so a 7-day-out race never reads "2 weeks out · 7 days". **SHIPPED (PR pending review) — branch `claude/tropos-ultrathink-eval-NGMcw`.** New pure helper `src/lib/raceGoalPlanner.ts` `getRaceGoalPlannerState({distance,targetDate,currentDate,liftDays,weeklyRunDays})` + 12 unit tests (all five states, distance-awareness, double-days, sub-2-week display). New presentational `src/components/program/RaceGoalPlanner.tsx` (uses the design-system `SegmentedControl` tone="running" for distance, matching main). Extracted shared `src/components/program/PhaseRail.tsx` used by BOTH the planner (highlights week 0) and `RaceCockpitCard` (highlights the current week) so before-save and after-save surfaces can't drift. ProgrammeSettings wiring: `plannerState` memo, status-aware save CTA, confirm-modal note for compressed/finish-safely; `raceDateInvalid` stays the only disable gate. Verification: full suite passed/0 failed, tsc 0, eslint 0, production build clean. **PROCESS LEARNING (recorded per retro discipline):** the feature branch was cut 76 commits behind main; main had already migrated the race-distance picker to `SegmentedControl`. A first implementation pass built against the stale branch (hand-rolled button group) and even "corrected" the plan's correct `SegmentedControl` call to a button group by trusting stale code over the plan. Caught before PR, rebased onto `origin/main`, adapted to `SegmentedControl`, re-verified, force-pushed. Lesson: rebase/inspect `origin/main` for the target file BEFORE implementing, especially on a long-lived feature branch. **STATUS 2026-06-01 — locked by product owner; lock on its own branch `claude/lock-run10`, PR'd immediately per lock discipline. Verify merged to main so the next agent sees the decision.** |
